## §H27z.86 THE cuBLAS->OURS MAPPING, FINALLY PROVEN -- and it flips the answer (2026-08-12)

Settles the question §H27z.58 left open and §H27y.25 was written for. Two claims existed IN THE
SAME TREE, in direct contradiction:

    [A] tools/h27z85_step3.sh:20-23  "cuBLAS MxN == our NxM, cluster label unchanged"
    [B] Bgemm_sm90_warpspecialized_template.cuh:677
        "Cluster 2x1 + raster v is cuBLAS's 1x2_h translated into our coordinates (§H27z.59 swap)"

**[B] IS CORRECT. [A] WAS MINE AND IT WAS WRONG.**

### WHY BOTH EARLIER "PROOFS" WERE WORTHLESS -- the circularity trap

[A] rested on an nsys run in which cuBLAS issued `nvjet_..._256x128_64x4_1x2_h_coopA_NNT` while we
issued `bgemm_sm90_kernel<Sm90WarpspecConfig<128,256,64,1,2,...>>`. That proves NOTHING: the harness
selects our config from `--tile=`/`--cluster=` (test_bgemm_sm90_matrix.cu:278, 410), so the kernel
that ran is the one named on the command line. §H27z.19's 7/7 launch-count table has the identical
defect and the doc already said so: *"the correspondence is by construction, not evidence."*

**Rule: a mapping cannot be proven by an experiment in which we choose our side of the pair.**

### TRAP 2 -- the persistent grid, which nearly produced a SECOND false proof

Reading tile counts out of `Grid Size` in the 164 archived ncu captures gave "TRANSPOSE 6/6". It was
an artifact. cuBLAS launches a PERSISTENT grid clamped to the SM count:

    distinct grid tuples over 163 shapes and many different tiles:
        (2,66,1) x134   (2,64,1) x25   (2,65,1) x2   (4,28,1) x1   (8,12,1) x1
    M4096 N24576 320x128 -> (2,66,1)      M4096 N896 112x128 -> (2,66,1)

2x66 = 132 = SM count. Identical grid for a 27x different N and a different tile. Those six "wins"
were rows where the transpose prediction happened to equal 128, which IS the clamp value. Any row
with grid in {128,130,132} carries ZERO information.

### PROOF 1 -- THE TILE TRANSPOSES (grid, clamp-free rows only)

`tools/tile_orientation.sh`, 3 repeats, kernel+grid identical across runs. Of its 14 rows, 11 are
clamped at 128 and carry nothing. The **3 clamp-free rows all agree**, none contradict:

    M      N     cuBLAS tile   grid   transpose-pred   direct-pred   verdict
    64     4096  48x64         88     86 (->88)        128           TRANSPOSE
    4096   64    64x48         88     86 (->88)        128           TRANSPOSE
    448    2048  128x64        112    112 exact        128           TRANSPOSE

86 -> 88 is the grid rounded up to a whole number of clusters (that kernel launches a 4-CTA
cluster; 86 -> 88). So: **cuBLAS's first number is our N. Their AxB means our BM = B, BN = A.**

### PROOF 2 -- THE CLUSTER AND RASTER ALSO SWAP (launch dims, 15/15, not inferrable-away)

nsys records `clusterX/Y/Z` in CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL. Read directly from run_1.sqlite:

    name cluster  raster   LAUNCHED cluster
    1x2           h        (2,1,1)        <- name is TRANSPOSED w.r.t. the launch
    2x1           v        (2,1,1)        <- name is DIRECT
    1x4           h        (4,1,1)        <- TRANSPOSED
    4x1           v        (4,1,1)        <- DIRECT

Three facts, 15/15 kernels, zero exceptions:
  1. EVERY cuBLAS cluster launch is 1-D `(S,1,1)`. Never 2-D.
  2. `1x2_h` and `2x1_v` launch the IDENTICAL cluster. They are the same physical cluster; the name
     writes the pair along the raster axis, so the raster letter tells you how to read it.
  3. The name's cluster pair correlates PERFECTLY with the raster letter: every `h` is `1xS`, every
     `v` is `Sx1`.

We do the same thing: `clusterDim.x = CLUSTER_SIZE, y=1, z=1` (template.cuh:4439) with CLUSTER_M/N
applied internally as `cluster_rank % CLUSTER_M`. Both sides launch 1-D clusters and interpret them
in the kernel, so the comparison is apples to apples.

### THE MAPPING

    cuBLAS  AxB_<raster>   ->   our BM = B, BN = A            (tile transposes)
                                cuBLAS 1x2_h  ==  our 2x1 raster v
                                cuBLAS 2x1_v  ==  our 2x1 raster h
    stages  cuBLAS 64xS    ->   S pipeline stages
    layout  NN*->nn  TN*->nt  NT*->tn   (correlation from the trainer capture; H8.5 warns the
                                         3rd letter is internal, so treat the 3rd letter as noise)

### CONSEQUENCE 1 -- the perf table in §H27z.85 compared the WRONG counterparts

It pinned our `128x256 c1x2` against cuBLAS `256x128_1x2_h`, whose real counterpart is our
`128x256 c2x1 raster v`. Every row of that table is void as a like-for-like comparison. The
correctness results (all bit-exact) stand; the %cuB numbers do not mean what the header said.

### CONSEQUENCE 2 -- we have 4 of the 8, not 8 and not 5

Recomputed under the corrected mapping, reading TEMPLATE ARGUMENTS not names, and including the 42
macro-generated configs that a `using`-only grep misses (BLUBLAS_SM90_CFG_VH / _VH_PD, both of which
pass only 9 template args so `_SPLIT_K` and `_EPI_TILE_N` always take defaults 1 and 0):

    V1  128x128_1x2_h_splitK  -> our 128x128 c2x1 v 6stg tn splitK   128x128x64_2x1_v_sk2   HAVE
    V2  128x256_2x1_v         -> our 256x128 c2x1 h 4stg tn          MISSING
    V3  192x192_1x2_h         -> our 192x192 c2x1 v 3stg nn          192x192x64_2x1_v       HAVE
    V4  192x192_2x1_v         -> our 192x192 c2x1 h 3stg nn          192x192x64_2x1_h       HAVE
    V5  192x192_2x1_v         -> our 192x192 c2x1 h 3stg tn          192x192x64_2x1_h       HAVE
    V6  192x192_2x1_v         -> our 192x192 c2x1 h 4stg nt          MISSING
    V7  256x128_1x2_h         -> our 128x256 c2x1 v 4stg nn          MISSING
    V8  256x128_1x2_h         -> our 128x256 c2x1 v 4stg nt          MISSING

**ALL FOUR GAPS ARE ONE THING: there is no 4-stage config at cluster 2x1.** Proven mechanically --
all 17 configs with `_EPI_TILE_N != 0` are cluster (1,2), zero at (2,1); all 10 with `_SPLIT_K > 1`
are cluster (1,1) or (2,1), zero at (1,2). The 4th stage comes only from the chunked epilogue
(§H27z.63), and the chunked epilogue was only ever ported to 1x2.

Corroboration that this reading is right rather than another flip: V1's match is
`128x128x64_2x1_v_sk2`, and the comment immediately above that config (template.cuh:677) already
says it is cuBLAS's `1x2_h` in our coordinates. And it explains the §H27z.85 measurements: V6 came
LAST at 81.6% and V2/V7/V8 sat mid-pack because we ran 3-STAGE kernels against cuBLAS's 4-stage --
a missing pipeline stage, not an unexplained bottleneck.

### WHAT TO BUILD -- one feature, four variants

Port the chunked epilogue to cluster 2x1: `256x128x64_2x1_h_ep32s2`, `192x192x64_2x1_h_ep32s2`,
`128x256x64_2x1_v_ep32s2`. Every knob already exists; only the (cluster, chunked) combination was
never instantiated. Re-run §H27z.85 against the CORRECTED pin list afterwards -- the numbers taken
before this section are not comparable.

## §H27z.87-89 THE MAPPING CLOSED (except raster), AND MEMORY ELIMINATED WITH A REAL CONTROL (2026-08-12)

Three experiments, run back to back. Two of them disproved their own premise, which is why they
were worth running.

### §H27z.87 LAYOUT -- PROVEN, both fields, and H8.5's caveat dissolved

The 3-letter suffix is TWO independent fields, so each was tested with the other held fixed.

**L1, first two letters.** Shape fixed at 4096x4096x4096, only OUR layout varied. We choose the
input, cuBLAS chooses the kernel -- so this is not circular the way §H27z.86's rejected "proofs"
were:

    our nn  ->  nvjet_..._256x128_64x4_1x2_h_bz_coopA_NNT
    our nt  ->  nvjet_..._256x128_64x4_1x2_h_bz_coopA_TNT
    our tn  ->  nvjet_..._128x256_64x4_2x1_v_bz_coopA_NTN

nn->NN, nt->TN, tn->NT, 3/3. nn and nt produced the IDENTICAL kernel config with only the suffix
moving -- a textbook single-variable result.

**L2, third letter.** Layout held at nn, only the shape varied:

    16384x11264x2048 -> 192x192_64x3_1x2_h_coopB_NN[N]    tile 192x192
    16384x2048x2048  -> 256x128_64x4_1x2_h_coopA_NN[T]    tile 256x128
    16384x2048x5632  -> 256x128_64x4_1x2_h_coopA_NN[T]    tile 256x128

The third letter moved N->T with the layout CONSTANT, so it is not the layout. Across the whole
164-shape archive it is a FUNCTION OF THE TILE -- 13 distinct tiles, and NO tile ever carries both
letters:

    'N' <- 112x128 128x192 128x256 144x128 168x128 176x128 192x192
    'T' <- 64x64 128x64 128x128 192x128 256x128 320x128

**H8.5's caveat is dissolved.** It worried that the first two letters varied under a FIXED op
config (citing `NTN`). The archive actually shows **all 18 distinct kernels are `TN`** -- constant,
exactly matching the fixed CUBLAS_OP_T/OP_N. Fix the op flags and the first two letters do not
move; vary them and they follow 1:1. The first two letters ARE the op flags.

**A first raster attempt that FAILED and must not be cited.** The same run compared our 192x192
against cuBLAS's 256x128 to fingerprint the raster. Different tiles read different amounts of data
regardless of raster, so it could attribute nothing. Recorded because the numbers exist in
test_reports/h27z87 and would otherwise look usable.

### §H27z.88 EXACT ARITHMETIC EXCLUSION -- the premise died, and that IS the finding

Method, chosen because "closest fingerprint" is similarity and not proof: an M-fastest walk fixes n
and sweeps every m, so it traverses ALL of A once per n-column. If A exceeds L2 it cannot be cached
between columns, so DRAM reads >= grid_n * sizeof(A) -- a HARD LOWER BOUND. Below a bound is not
"unlikely", it is IMPOSSIBLE. 14 of the 15 shapes give a usable bound; 6 give two-sided bounds.
All four of our (cluster x raster) possibilities were run on every shape: 56 ncu captures.

    RESULT   8 shapes: pure M-fastest EXCLUDED     6 shapes: BOTH walks EXCLUDED (contradiction)

Six contradictions is not noise -- it falsifies the premise. cuBLAS performs NEITHER pure walk. It
is confirmed by how close it runs to the theoretical minimum A+B:

    2048x512x16384  min 84MB  cuBLAS 84MB   = 1.00x        16384x512x2048  min 69MB  cuBLAS 71MB = 1.02x
    2048x2048x16384 min 134MB cuBLAS 134MB  = 1.00x        16384x2048x2048 min 75MB  cuBLAS 79MB = 1.05x

1.00x the minimum is unreachable by any pure 1-D walk on these grids. **cuBLAS uses GROUPED
(swizzled) rasterization.** So "is cuBLAS's h our v or our h" is a MALFORMED question -- their
raster field is not a pure direction.

Closest-config tally across all shapes was split 1x2_v:3, 1x2_h:3, 2x1_v:2, 2x1_h:6 -- no config
wins everywhere, so by the rule the analyser holds itself to: UNDETERMINED, not picked.

**A correction this forced.** §H27z.86 claimed the CLUSTER was proven from launch `clusterX/Y/Z`.
It is NOT. OUR 1x2 and OUR 2x1 both launch `(2,1,1)` as well -- CLUSTER_M/N are applied internally
as `cluster_rank % CLUSTER_M`. The launch record cannot separate them on either side. What the
launch data DOES prove stands: every cuBLAS cluster is 1-D of size S, and the name's cluster pair
is a logical label written along the raster axis, not the launch dims.

### §H27z.89 MEMORY IS ELIMINATED -- and this time with a proper control

Raster swizzle (rs2/4/8/16) swept on the two worst sites, cuBLAS captured in the same process:

    16384x11264x2048 nn  (gate_up-fwd)   min A+B = 113 MB
      config    DRAM MB   x min   L2 hit%   duration
      cuBLAS        538    4.75      84.1     1183 us
      plain       1,886   16.65      65.6     1369 us
      rs2         1,097    9.69      76.8     1366 us
      rs4           641    5.66      84.5     1357 us
      rs8           431    3.81      89.6     1358 us   <- LESS DRAM than cuBLAS, HIGHER L2
      rs16          689    6.08      87.1     1360 us

    16384x50304x2048 nn  (lm_head-fwd)   min A+B = 273 MB
      cuBLAS      2,297    8.41      88.9     5102 us
      plain       6,940   25.41      70.4     5672 us
      rs2         4,840   17.72      77.6     5689 us
      rs4         3,417   12.51      83.1     5703 us
      rs8         2,530    9.26      88.3     5689 us   <- cuBLAS's memory profile, matched
      rs16        3,539   12.96      85.3     5690 us

**DRAM traffic swings 4.4x and L2 hit rate swings 24 points, and the DURATION DOES NOT MOVE:**
gate_up 1369/1366/1357/1358/1360 us (spread 0.9%), lm_head 5672/5689/5703/5689/5690 (spread 0.5%).

This is the strongest form of the argument, and it is what every earlier memory investigation
lacked. Not "we measured DRAM and it looked acceptable" -- we deliberately drove our memory
behaviour BELOW cuBLAS's (431 vs 538 MB, 89.6% vs 84.1% L2 at gate_up) and the kernel did not get
one microsecond faster. At lm_head rs8 reproduces cuBLAS's memory almost exactly (2,530 vs 2,297
MB; 88.3% vs 88.9%) and we are still 5,689 vs 5,102 us = 89.7%.

**RETRACTED, same session:** an hour earlier I read the pure-raster 3x DRAM gap at these two sites
as "the lm_head answer". It is not. That gap exists only for pure rasters, which we do not ship,
and closing it entirely buys ZERO.

### WHERE THE GAP NOW STANDS -- everything controlled for

At gate_up-fwd we now hold constant: SAME tile (192x192), SAME stage count (cuBLAS 64x3, we derive
3), and memory BETTER than cuBLAS -- and we remain 13% slower. That is a pure implementation gap in
the compute/scheduling path.

Measured and eliminated, each independently: DRAM bandwidth, L2 reuse, shared-memory bank
conflicts, tile shape, the epilogue, the uniform datapath, and now memory traffic under a
manipulate-and-observe control.

### STATUS OF THE cuBLAS->OURS MAPPING

    tile          PROVEN     transposes; 3 clamp-free grid rows, direct excluded in all 3
    layout        PROVEN     nn->NN nt->TN tn->NT (L1) + 18/18 constant under fixed op flags
    third letter  PROVEN     not the layout; a function of the tile (13 tiles, no overlap)
    cluster       PARTIAL    1-D of size S on both sides; the logical M/N split is NOT
                             separable from launch data on either side
    raster        OPEN, but DOWNGRADED. cuBLAS uses a GROUPED walk (group ~4-8 by fingerprint),
                             not a pure direction, so the original question is malformed. And it
                             has ZERO measured effect on duration here, so it gates nothing.

### §H27z.89b WHAT OUR h/v PHYSICALLY ARE -- and why we must NOT change them

The raster name-mapping is unanswerable, but the practical question behind it ("are we using the
right raster?") IS answerable, and the answer is yes.

**Our letters, verified against hardware counters rather than the source comment.** Hypothesis from
the definition at the tile-decode site, tested on the 56 h27z88 captures:

    v = M-fastest : reuses B down a column, RE-READS A once per n-column -> cheap when A is SMALL
    h = N-fastest : reuses A across a row,  RE-READS B once per m-row    -> cheap when B is SMALL

Prediction "the winner is whichever re-reads the smaller operand" holds on **12 of 12 shapes where
the two rasters differ**. The other 2 (2048x512x16384, 16384x512x2048) measured v == h EXACTLY
(84/84 and 71/71 MB, both at ~1.00x minimum) -- ties where the whole working set fits, not
counterexamples. Examples: 2048x11264x16384 has A=67MB B=369MB -> v wins 707 vs 2,030; 16384x2048x2048
has A=67MB B=8MB -> h wins 78 vs 283.

**cuBLAS's letter is NOT the same kind of object** and cannot be mapped onto ours: §H27z.88 proved
its walk is GROUPED (below both pure-walk bounds on 6 shapes; 1.00x minimum traffic on four). A
pure-direction label and a grouped-walk label do not correspond.

**DECISION: change nothing.** Our dispatcher's raster choice already matches the physical rule on
13 of 13 shapes where the raster appears in the config name -- and it FLIPS correctly, picking v on
exactly the three shapes where A is the smaller operand (16384x50304x2048 nn, 2048x11264x16384 tn,
2048x50304x16384 tn) and h on the other ten. Those pins came from measured sweeps; the tables
independently rediscovered the physics without anyone deriving it. Re-labelling our v/h to chase
cuBLAS's naming would copy a label for a mechanism we do not share and would break 13 correct pins
for zero gain.

**The one real gap that remains here:** grouped rasterization coverage. We own `rsN` on only two
config families (256x128_1x2_h, 192x192_1x2_v) and the dispatcher already uses `_rs2` on 9 of 15
sites. Porting it wider has NO PROVEN VALUE yet -- §H27z.89 showed duration flat across rs2/4/8/16
on both shapes tested. It would need a shape where memory actually binds, and none has been found.

### NEXT

The compute path at gate_up-fwd, where tile, stages and memory are now all matched: instruction
mix and warp-stall reasons, ours vs nvjet, same process, same shape.

## §H27z.90 cuBLAS's TILE ORDER IS NOT OBSERVABLE ON THIS STACK -- proven, with a positive control (2026-08-12)

Closing the last open field of the mapping (raster) the only way that would have been exact: read
cuBLAS's tile visitation order directly instead of inferring it. Both available routes are dead,
each for a specific and verifiable reason. Recorded so nobody re-attempts this.

### ROUTE 1 -- NVBit: BLOCKED BY THE DRIVER

Requirements, from the NVBit README: SM <= 12.1 (sm_90 fine), CUDA >= 12.0 (fine), **CUDA driver
version <= 575.xx**. Every Verda box is on **580.126.09** -- five branches past the ceiling. It is
a MAXIMUM not a minimum because NVBit patches undocumented driver internals; newer drivers break
it. Latest release is 1.8 (Apr 2025) and the ceiling has not moved. Running it out of spec would
forfeit the only reason to use it (certainty), so it was not attempted.

### ROUTE 2 -- Compute Sanitizer public API: TOOL WORKS, GEMM IS INVISIBLE TO IT

The supported equivalent, and better on paper: ships INSIDE the CUDA toolkit so it is version
matched to the driver, and is Hopper-aware (TMA, wgmma, cluster barriers, DSMEM). A full tracer was
built (tools/sanitizer_tma_trace): device patch + injection library + decoder.

    instruction 3  GLOBAL_MEMORY_ACCESS      verify_kernel      -> 29,705 records (2.6 MB written)
                                             bgemm_sm90_kernel  ->      0
                                             nvjet_sm90_tst_... ->      0
    instruction 35 BULK_COPY_SHARED_TO_GLOBAL  all three        ->      0
    instruction 14 MEMCPY_ASYNC                all three        ->      0

**verify_kernel is the positive control.** An ordinary CUDA kernel in the same process, same run,
yielded 29,705 records. So injection, patch loading, per-context patching, callback data, the
device buffer, the drain and the file write are ALL functional. The zeros are not a broken tool.

**Root cause.** Both GEMMs do 100% of their global traffic through TMA *tensor* copies
(`cp.async.bulk.tensor.2d.shared::cluster.global.tile`). That instruction appears in NONE of the 40
`Sanitizer_InstructionId` values. The nearest, `SANITIZER_INSTRUCTION_BULK_COPY_GLOBAL_TO_SHARED`
(30), is documented at sanitizer_patching.h:635 as `cp.async.bulk.shared::cluster.global` -- the
NON-tensor form. There is no tensor-copy patch point.

=> On sm_90 with CUDA 13 / driver 580, no supported instrumentation can observe a TMA-based GEMM's
   operand fetches. This is a property of the tool set, not of our code.

### SIX REAL DEFECTS FOUND WHILE GETTING THERE -- all in the tool, all recorded in-source

  1. static-init-order crash: `__attribute__((constructor))` ran before the global std::string
     objects were constructed -> segfault in std::string::_M_replace during dlopen. Backtrace named
     it exactly. Fix: no constructor (the driver calls InitializeInjection itself after dlopen) and
     POD globals only.
  2. **--compile-as-tools-patch is MANDATORY** (API guide, "Writing a Patch"). Building the patch as
     ordinary device code produced a fatbin that CONTAINED blublas_tma_cb -- cuobjdump even printed
     `Function : blublas_tma_cb` -- but injecting it corrupted the patched kernel and crashed the
     driver inside cuInit. **A symbol being present is NOT evidence the patch is valid.** An earlier
     "-rdc=true" fix was treating the symptom of the missing flag.
  3. patches are PER-CONTEXT: calling sanitizerAddPatchesFromFile on every module load (a GEMM run
     loads many) is undefined per the header, and was the second driver crash.
  4. every SanitizerResult was unchecked -- silent failure looked identical to "no data".
  5. an async H2D copy sourced from a STACK local whose lifetime ended immediately.
  6. drain relied on SYNCHRONIZE callbacks the harness never raised; needs LAUNCH_END + atexit.

The tool is left in the tree in working order. It CAN trace any non-TMA kernel, which may be useful
later (the reduce kernels, elementwise, attention paths).

### WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE RASTER QUESTION -- closed as unobtainable, and it does not matter

    proven      cuBLAS does NOT do a pure walk (below both pure-walk bounds on 6 shapes, §H27z.88)
    proven      its memory fingerprint matches GROUPED rasterisation at group ~4-8 (§H27z.89)
    proven      our v = M-fastest re-reading A, our h = N-fastest re-reading B (12/12, §H27z.89b)
    proven      our dispatcher already picks the physically optimal raster on 13 of 13 shapes
    proven      raster has ZERO measured effect on duration (spread 0.9% and 0.5% across rs2/4/8/16)
    UNOBTAINABLE  the exact group size and orientation of cuBLAS's walk

The remaining unknown is a labelling detail with no performance consequence, and the two tools that
could close it are respectively blocked by a driver ceiling and by a missing patch point. Stop here.

### NEXT

The compute path at gate_up-fwd, where tile (192x192), stage count (both 3) and memory (ours BETTER
than cuBLAS: 431 vs 538 MB, 89.6% vs 84.1% L2) are all matched and we are still 13% slower.

## §H27z.91-99 V8 IN DEPTH: THREE HYPOTHESES KILLED BY MEASUREMENT, AND THE REAL CAUSE (2026-08-13)

Everything below is V8 only -- cuBLAS `nvjet_sm90_tst_256x128_64x4_1x2_h_bz_coopA_TNT`, layout nt,
our `128x256x64_2x1_h_ep32s2`, four shapes 16384x2048x{512,2048,11264,50304}. Verified per shape
from the nsys captures, not assumed: cuBLAS issues that ONE kernel on all four, we issue one config
on all four, template args byte-identical across the four (§H27z.96 phase 1).

### §H27z.95 THE RASTER MAPPING IS WRONG -- set A vs set B on one box

Both pin sets run on the same box in one session, because the H200 changed (31.22.104.211 ->
95.133.253.59) and a box change voids prior timings.

    set A (raster by measurement)  MEAN 90.8%
    set B (raster by the H27z.86 mapping)  MEAN 88.1%
    A - B = +2.7 pts     CONTROL rows (identical config in both sets, 6 of 15) drift -0.6 pts

The control bounds the noise at well under a point, so +2.7 is real. Per shape, set A picks the
operand-reuse-optimal raster on 9 of 9 and wins on 8 (the 9th, K=512, ties -- too few k-iters for
tile order to matter). **§H27z.86's `cuBLAS 1x2_h -> our v` name-mapping is therefore DISPROVED by
measurement**: following it put us on the physically wrong walk and cost 5-8 pts per shape. Raster
is now chosen by the §H27z.89b operand-size rule, which is verifiable, not by cuBLAS's letter,
which §H27z.90 proved unobtainable. This is not "picking the fastest" -- it is matching cuBLAS's
BEHAVIOUR (they are fast, so they walk efficiently too) instead of copying a label we cannot decode.

### THE SHAPE OF THE V8 DEFICIT -- one number explains all four shapes

    K        cuBLAS us    ours us    difference    %cuB
    512         54.8       71.4        +16.5      76.8
    2048       176.0      191.0        +15.0      92.1
    11264      916.0      927.2        +11.1      98.8
    50304     4304.3     4301.5         -2.7     100.1

A FIXED ~15 us, not a percentage. Predicts 78.5 / 92.1 / 98.4 / 99.7 against measured 76.8 / 92.1 /
98.8 / 100.1. Two of the four shapes have nothing to win -- we are at parity or ahead. Converting
to ABSOLUTE TIME is what made this legible; four messages of ratio-chasing (1.75x instructions,
45% barrier stall, 6.5x conflicts) could not explain a deficit that COLLAPSES with K, because every
one of those ratios is CONSTANT with K.

### §H27z.94 HYPOTHESIS 1 -- BANK CONFLICTS. DEAD.

ncu showed shared-STORE conflicts at 6.5x cuBLAS on V8 (12,163 vs 2,153). The swizzled epilogue
buffer (`EPI_SWIZZLE_BYTES=64`) was built for every pinned tile at cluster 2x1, each with an
unswizzled twin so the ablation isolates the swizzle from the chunk width.

    conflicts   12,127 -> ~173 on all four shapes      70x down, and 12x BELOW cuBLAS's own 2,153
    duration    unchanged (+0.2 / -0.9 / -0.1 / -2.4 %)
    correctness 14/14 bit-identical maxRelErr

Removed the suspected cause ENTIRELY and nothing moved. Bank conflicts are eliminated as V8's
bottleneck by manipulation, not by argument. Also: instructions ROSE by a constant +1,790 per shape
(the XOR), so the swizzle is a trade, not a free win. On 192x192 it is actively harmful (-13 to
-18%, and swz32ep16 -66%). NOT ADOPTED; the pins are unchanged. This reproduces §H27z.82's warning
on our own 2x1 configs -- and I had re-run an experiment that section already settled, which is the
mistake it exists to prevent.

**The swizzle work was not wasted**: it established that the swizzle is FREE, which is the
prerequisite for stmatrix (below).

### §H27z.96 LOCALISING THE COST -- what the 99 captured metrics actually say

Launch config, ours vs cuBLAS, K=2048: registers_per_thread 168/168, block_size 384/384, grid 132/
132, cluster_size 2/2, shared_mem 215/214 KB, waves 1.00/1.00, occupancy_limit_registers 1/1,
occupancy_limit_shared_mem 1/1 -- IDENTICAL on everything except:

    launch__barrier_count         ours 16   cuBLAS 3
    launch__occupancy_limit_barriers   4          21     (64 barriers per SM: 64/16=4, 64/3=21)

Cause: `bar.sync %0` with the barrier id in a REGISTER (`g = wg_id`), so ptxas reserves all 16.
cuBLAS uses immediates. NOT BINDING -- both sides are pinned to 1 block/SM by registers and smem,
so the freed barrier resource buys nothing. Recorded as a parity defect, not a performance one.

Stall decomposition (% of warp-active), the useful part:

    shape   side     SYNC(bar+membar)  MEMORY(lg+sh+mio)  ISSUING   tensor%
    K512    ours          52.0               24.2           11.5      57.9
    K512    cuBLAS        23.6               42.7           22.0      75.2
    K50304  ours          45.1               31.4           11.3      99.2
    K50304  cuBLAS        32.2               30.9           27.8      99.6

Our issue rate is PINNED at ~11.3% at every K; cuBLAS rises 22 -> 27.8%. cuBLAS is memory-throttled
(mio_thr 10-16%) and we are NEVER (0.0%) -- they saturate the memory pipes, we do not.

**BAR.SYNC count is NOT the problem**: cuBLAS issues 46 static BAR.SYNC to our 21 and stalls LESS.
The only thing they never emit is MEMBAR, and membar was the one stall term that TRACKED the
deficit (5.9/2.3/0.5/0.1% vs cuBLAS 0.0 on all four; collapses 59x as K grows, exactly as the
deficit does, while barrier/lg_score/wait are flat). That correlation drove hypotheses 2 and 3.

### §H27z.97 HYPOTHESIS 2 -- STMATRIX. DEAD, TWICE OVER.

SASS showed, per epilogue chunk: ours `STS x2 + BAR.SYNC + MEMBAR.ALL.CTA + FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S`
against cuBLAS's `STSM x2 + FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S`. STSM is warp-collective and internally ordered, so
the theory was that plain STS is what forces the barrier and the membar.

    every stmatrix config FAILED correctness on all four shapes

Template line 3934 already said why: *"Converting to STSM is REAL outstanding work... the
wgmma-fragment -> stmatrix register/address mapping must be derived and CuTe-verified, not
guessed."* The code compiles and runs; the mapping was never finished. That comment sits 48 lines
from a call site I did read, and I did not read it.

**And the SASS disproves the mechanism regardless of the failure:**

                    MEMBAR.CTA  MEMBAR.GPU  FENCE.VIEW  STS  STSM  BAR.SYNC
    ep32s2              10          2           9       128    0      21
    swz64r64stsm        10          2           9         0   16      21

STSM replaced all 128 STS and the MEMBARs and BAR.SYNCs did not move. They are emitted
unconditionally by our own `barrier_sync()` / `tma_store_fence()` calls, which do not care what
store instruction preceded them. A WORKING stmatrix would not have removed them either.

Also measured: `EPI_ROWS=64` (atom staging) costs -8.5% at K=512 and -5.0% at K=2048. That is the
form the one previously-"validated" stmatrix config uses.

### §H27z.98 HYPOTHESIS 3 -- FEWER MEMBARS. DEAD, and it made things WORSE.

The fence cannot be made cheaper. Compiled in isolation on sm_90a (`fence_probe.cu`):

    fence.proxy.async.shared::cta  (clobber or not) -> MEMBAR.ALL.CTA + FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S
    fence.proxy.async              (generic)        -> MEMBAR.ALL.GPU + FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S

EVERY writable form emits a MEMBAR, and CUTLASS uses the identical PTX (barrier.h:733,
copy_sm90_tma.hpp:1217). cuBLAS's 184 bare FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S with ZERO MEMBAR is **not reachable
from PTX** -- nvjet is emitted through NVIDIA's own path. So the only lever was issuing fewer:
`EPI_TILE_N=64` halves the chunks, 8 -> 4.

    MECHANISM WORKED   MEMBAR.CTA 10 -> 6, FENCE.VIEW 9 -> 5, BAR.SYNC 21 -> 13, instr 2104 -> 1984
    membar stall FELL  5.9 -> 4.9 at K=512
    PERFORMANCE        K512 77.9 -> 61.3% (-21.5%), MEAN 90.1 -> 85.7%

We removed 40% of the MEMBARs and the worst shape got 21.5% SLOWER. ncu says why: sync stalls fell
(barrier 47.1 -> 43.7, membar 5.9 -> 4.9) but MEMORY stalls rose (lg_score 21.9 -> 27.6, mio_thr
0.0 -> 3.2) and tensor% fell 58.8 -> 52.0. Doubling the chunk doubles the store buffer (16 -> 32 KB)
and leaves only 3 overlap opportunities against EPI_STAGES=2 instead of 7 -- the epilogue's own
pipelining collapses faster than the fences save. **The membar correlation was not causal.**
NOT ADOPTED. All numerics bit-identical (maxRelErr 0.00000) throughout, as expected for a staging
change.

### §H27z.99 THE ACTUAL CAUSE -- wgmma DESCRIPTOR CONSTRUCTION IN THE MAINLOOP

All three dead hypotheses were in the EPILOGUE. The cost is in the MAINLOOP. From the instruction
streams side by side (h27z96/03_sass), not from any counter:

**cuBLAS, between consecutive wgmma -- MEDIAN GAP 2 INSTRUCTIONS:**

    HGMMA.64  x128x16.F32.BF16 R24, gdesc[UR16], R24
    UIADD3    UR16, UR16, 0x2, URZ        <- increment the descriptor
    UIADD3    UR18, UR18, 0x2, URZ
    HGMMA.64  x128x16.F32.BF16 R24, gdesc[UR16], R24

Both adds are on the UNIFORM datapath. At a stage boundary they stay adds:
`UIADD3 UR16,UR16,0x200` then `UIADD3 UR16,UR16,-0x6`.

**OURS, per wgmma -- about 20 instructions, rebuilt from scratch:**

    VIADD        R6, R8, 0x20              recompute the smem offset
    LOP3.LUT     R6, R6, 0x3fc20, RZ       mask
    SHF.R.U32.HI R6, RZ, 0x4, R6           shift
    LOP3.LUT     R6, R6, 0x10000, RZ       OR the layout bits back in
    R2UR         UR16, R6                  cross VECTOR -> UNIFORM
    UMOV         UR19, 0x40000040
    IMAD.MOV.U32 R7, RZ, RZ, 0x40000040
    R2UR         UR17, R7                  cross VECTOR -> UNIFORM
    HGMMA.64     x256x16.F32.BF16 R24, gdesc[UR16], R24
    (plus the duplicated uniform chain: UIADD3 / ULOP3.LUT / USHF / ULEA, 28 per k-step)

    per k-step   wgmma   overhead   total
    ours            4       ~92        96
    cuBLAS          8       ~16        24

Roughly 70 of our 96 mainloop instructions are descriptor arithmetic; 4 are math. This IS the 1.75x
dynamic instruction count, it explains the 8 R2UR per k-step, and it explains the uniform-datapath
share gap (ours 17.1% vs cuBLAS 37.2%) -- they never leave the scalar path, we compute on the
vector path and pay to cross.

**Why this is consistent with the deficit collapsing at large K:** the overhead is always present
but only COSTS time when the tensor pipe has slack. At K=50304 tensor% is 99.2 and the extra
instructions issue in the wgmma's shadow for free; at K=512 tensor% is 57.9 and instruction issue
becomes the limit. Same reason our issue rate is pinned at 11.3% while cuBLAS's rises to 27.8%.

**Why it is recomputed:** the descriptor is an smem address plus layout bits, and across consecutive
k-steps the address advances by a CONSTANT. Ours is derived from the stage base each iteration, so
the compiler cannot prove the delta is constant through the `stage % DEPTH` wrap and rebuilds it.
cuBLAS keeps it live in a uniform register and adds a constant, compensating at the wrap.

STATUS: hypothesis 4, NOT YET TESTED. Unlike 1-3 this is not a counter correlation -- it is the
instruction stream doing demonstrably different work for the same wgmma. That is a reason to take
it seriously, not a reason to skip the measurement.

### §H27z.99b HYPOTHESIS 4 -- DESCRIPTOR HOIST. IMPLEMENTED, AND IT KILLS THE WHOLE INSTRUCTION-COUNT THREAD.

Implemented as `DESC_HOIST` (22nd template param, default false = byte-identical to what ships).
Build the descriptor once per stage, then add a compile-time constant per k16 step, as cuBLAS does.
Exactness argument: desc_encode(x) = (x & 0x3FFFF) >> 4 with the address in bits 0..13 and the next
field at bit 16, so desc(base+off) == desc(base) + (off>>4) given (a) both 16-byte aligned (smem is
__align__(1024), every offset a multiple of 16 B, static_asserted) and (b) base+off < 0x40000 so the
mask cannot wrap (Hopper max CTA smem 227 KB). Both hold unconditionally.

**STATIC SASS -- the algebra worked, but only partly:**

    mainloop            per k-step   per wgmma   R2UR  VIADD  LOP3  SHF  UIADD3  ULOP3
    ep32s2 (pin)             94        23.5        8     2      9    4      9      9
    ep32s2_dh                80        20.0        8     0      6    1      6      6
    cuBLAS                   24         2.0        0     -      -    -      2      -

Address arithmetic collapsed as predicted (VIADD 2->0, SHF 4->1, LOP3 9->6). **R2UR UNCHANGED at 8**
-- the hoist removes the arithmetic but cannot remove the vector->uniform CROSSING, because gdesc[]
demands a uniform operand while our descriptor is built in vector registers (its chain starts at
__cvta_generic_to_shared, which nvcc places on the vector path). cuBLAS pays zero crossings.

**DYNAMIC -- 14% of the instructions gone, and NOTHING MOVED:**

                  instructions             %cuB          tensor%        duration us
    K512      20,976 -> 19,238   -8.3%   77.4 -> 77.3   58.8 -> 58.4    90.2 -> 90.1
    K2048     57,981 -> 51,026  -12.0%   93.1 -> 92.2   84.6 -> 84.4   247.2 -> 247.6
    K11264   280,013 -> 241,789 -13.7%   96.9 -> 96.8   96.7 -> 96.7     1.1 -> 1.1
    K50304 1,220,536 -> 1,049,808 -14.0% 98.0 -> 97.0   99.3 -> 99.3     4.9 -> 4.9
    MEAN                                  91.4 -> 90.8      maxRelErr 0.00000 on all four

**INSTRUCTION COUNT IS NOT THE BOTTLENECK.** This does not merely kill hypothesis 4 -- it kills the
entire "we execute 1.75x cuBLAS's instructions" line that motivated it. Reaching cuBLAS's exact
count would buy nothing. Our warps are stalled ~88% of the time; the instructions were issuing in
the gaps, free. Removing them frees capacity we were not using.

NOT ADOPTED as the pin (-0.6 pts mean, K2048 -1.0%). Kept as a knob with a measured answer.

### §H27z.99c WHY THE `LARGEST EXCESS STALL: barrier +18.33` LINE IS MISLEADING

The stall table sorts by MAGNITUDE, not causality, and barrier is the largest gap in every V8 run.
It is not the cost, and this run proves it twice:

  1. The hoist removed 14% of instructions and barrier stall ROSE (46.9 -> 48.3 at K11264, 46.9 ->
     48.4 at K50304) with duration unchanged. Take work away, warps reach the barrier sooner and
     wait longer. **Barrier stall is ELASTIC -- it absorbs whatever slack is created.**
  2. At K=50304: barrier stall 46.9% AND tensor-active 99.3% AND 98% of cuBLAS, simultaneously.
     A 47% barrier stall coexists with near-perfect tensor utilisation.

Same disqualifier as membar: barrier stall is FLAT across a 100x range of K (46.9 -> 48.4) while
the deficit COLLAPSES (77% -> 98%). A constant cannot explain a collapsing effect. Also recall
cuBLAS issues MORE BAR.SYNC than us (46 static vs 21) and stalls LESS. Do not chase this number.

### THE ONE MEASUREMENT NEVER TAKEN

All four V8 shapes are 16384x2048xK -- **identical M and N**, so identical tile count (1024), with
only K varying. Nothing in any of this data can separate:

    ~15 us paid ONCE per launch        (prologue, TMA descriptor setup, grid ramp)
    ~15 us paid PER TILE x 1024        (~15 ns/tile of epilogue or scheduling overhead)

Raised after §H27z.96 and deferred twice. After four dead hypotheses it is the only branch left
uncut, and it is one run: same config, FIXED K, sweep M and N. If the 15 us scales with tile count
it is per-tile; if flat, it is launch setup. That halves the search space instead of proposing a
fifth knob.

### §H27za0 THE ~15 us IS PER TILE, NOT PER LAUNCH -- measured, decisively

Hold K fixed at 2048, swing the tile count 8x by varying M and N. tiles = (M/128)*(N/256), grid is
persistent at 132 CTAs; all four keep tiles/CTA >> 1 so wave quantisation cannot confound it.

    shape              tiles  tiles/CTA   ours us  cuBLAS us   DIFF us  DIFF/tile ns   %cuB
    8192x2048x2048       512      3.9        95.4      89.7       5.7       11.1      94.0
    16384x2048x2048     1024      7.8       189.2     176.2      13.1       12.8      93.1
    32768x2048x2048     2048     15.5       380.0     348.1      32.0       15.6      91.6
    16384x8192x2048     4096     31.0       774.1     711.5      62.7       15.3      91.9

DIFF/tile is FLAT (11-15 ns) while DIFF scales 11x for an 8x tile increase. Ratio-of-ratios 1.376
against 0.125 for the per-launch model. And %cuB degrades monotonically with tile count AT FIXED K
(94.0 -> 91.6) -- which no earlier run could have shown, because every one of them held M and N
constant at 16384x2048.

**PERMANENTLY RULED OUT** (all paid once per launch, so they cannot scale with tiles): the
cuTensorMap setup, the grid ramp, the 2x MEMBAR.ALL.GPU prologue cluster fence, the first tile's
pipeline fill.

Caveat on the record: 1.376 is slightly SUPER-linear, so a second smaller term probably grows
faster than tile count -- plausibly L2 pressure, since C grows 34 MB -> 268 MB across the sweep.
The per-tile term dominates but this is not a perfectly clean single effect.

### WHAT V8 STANDS AT

`128x256x64_2x1_h_ep32s2` remains the pin, 90-91.5% mean over the four shapes, unchanged through
all three experiments. Every alternative built (swz64, swz64r64, swz64stsm, swz64r64stsm, ep64s2)
measured worse or failed. The negative results are the value: bank conflicts, stmatrix and membar
count are all closed by manipulation, so no one needs to try them again.


## §H27za1-a6 THE V8 BOTTLENECK FOUND: A PER-TILE CLUSTER BARRIER, AND IT WAS VESTIGIAL (2026-08-13)

Seven hypotheses died before this one, and every single one was optimising AROUND a barrier none
of us had noticed. Recording the whole arc, because the negative results are what made the
positive one findable.

### THE HYPOTHESES THAT DIED, and what each actually changed

    1 bank conflicts   H27z.94  swizzled epilogue buffer   conflicts 12,127 -> 173 (70x, and 12x
                                                           BELOW cuBLAS)      TIME UNCHANGED
    2 stmatrix         H27z.97  EPI_USE_STSM               FAILED correctness; and SASS proved the
                                                           barriers are emitted UNCONDITIONALLY so
                                                           it would not have helped even if it ran
    3 membar count     H27z.98  EPI_TILE_N 32 -> 64        MEMBARs -40%   TIME 21.5% WORSE
                                                           (confounded: also doubled the buffer)
    4 instruction cnt  H27z.99  hoist the wgmma descriptor dynamic instrs -14%  TIME UNCHANGED
                                out of the k-loop          -> killed the CATEGORY, not one idea
    5 grid geometry    H27za1   (132,1,1) -> (2,66,1)      grid verified changed; duration,
                                                           tensor% and every stall IDENTICAL
    6 epilogue fusion  H27za2   none -- tested the SASS     DISPROVED before any GPU run: both
                                interleaving first          kernels are compute-then-store,
                                                            0/83 cuBLAS stores near a wgmma
    7 EPI_STAGES       H27za3   built, never run            superseded before it burned GPU time

Two decompositions made the search tractable, both from data already on disk:
    time  = a + b*K   ours a=16.6us b=0.08518   cuBLAS a=0.8us b=0.08555  -> SLOPES MATCH TO 0.4%
    instr = a + b*K   ours a=8,642  b=24.09     cuBLAS a=4,782 b=14.11
The mainloop computes at cuBLAS's rate. The entire deficit is a fixed intercept. And in the
epilogue we execute 1.81x the instructions but take 21x the time -- 3.38 cycles/instruction
against cuBLAS's 0.29. It was STALLING, not executing, which is why every instruction-count and
conflict-count fix did nothing.

### THE MEASUREMENT THAT FOUND IT -- PC sampling, after two tooling failures

`--section SourceCounters` collected nothing usable; requesting the metrics DIRECTLY worked:
    ncu --metrics smsp__pcsamp_sample_count,smsp__pcsamp_warps_issue_stalled_{barrier,membar,...}
    ncu --import x.ncu-rep --page source --print-source sass --csv     <- --print-source IS REQUIRED
ncu reports ABSOLUTE addresses; cuobjdump uses RELATIVE offsets. Without rebasing, every sample
lands past the epilogue boundary and the region split reads a meaningless 100% epilogue.

Rebased, K=64, 35,407 samples:
    0x64c0  22.4%  UCGABAR_WAIT     0x0660  6.1%  ERRBAR
    0x6460   3.2%  ERRBAR           0x06c0  2.2%  UCGABAR_WAIT      = 33.9% ON ONE CONSTRUCT

That construct is `cluster_sync()` at template :3662 (producer) and :3890 (consumer), INSIDE the
persistent tile loop: MEMBAR.ALL.CTA + MEMBAR.ALL.GPU + ERRBAR + CGAERRBAR + UCGABAR_ARV +
UCGABAR_WAIT -- a DEVICE-SCOPE fence plus a cross-CTA rendezvous, PER OUTPUT TILE, in BOTH
warpgroups. cuBLAS emits ZERO MEMBAR of either kind.

### THE COST (§H27za4, V8 = 128x256x64_2x1_h_ep32s2, nt)

    K       ON %cuB   OFF %cuB    gain
    64       60.9      96.9      +58.9%
    512      77.9      91.0      +17.2%
    2048     93.1      96.5       +3.6%
    11264    97.3      98.2       +0.8%
    50304    93.4      93.5       +0.3%

Monotonic in K = a fixed per-tile cost, matching §H27za0's independent 8x tile sweep (DIFF/tile
flat at 11-15 ns while DIFF scaled 11x). maxRelErr 0.00000 in both arms throughout.

### WHY IT IS SAFE TO DROP -- protocol, then measurement

    stage/phase live OUTSIDE the tile loop (:3593, :3855) and are NEVER reset -- state is
    continuous across tiles, exactly as cuBLAS carries it in uniform registers. There is no
    "tile-boundary reset" to get wrong (a theory I proposed and the source disproved).
    EMPTY_MBAR_ARRIVE_COUNT = WGs * (SHARE_M + SHARE_N - 1) = 4 for a 2x1 B-mc cluster, and
    release_empty delivers exactly 4. A producer cannot refill a stage until every peer has
    released it -- drift is already bounded per stage.

    full suite ON vs OFF     2990 PASS / 20 FAIL, IDENTICAL, same abort point (3010 cases)
    documented crash case    nn + A-multicast + large K + persistent, 5/5 PASS
    wider sweep              5 A-mc configs x 2 large K = 10/10 PASS, including 1x4
    tightest stress          1x4 cluster, K=50304, 10/10 PASS
    cuBLAS                   same structure, zero fences

### WHY THE ORIGINAL Xid 13 IS GONE

§H14.6 added the barrier for an NN A-multicast crash; §H14.7 removed it on design grounds;
§H27z.5 restored it because an Xid 13 "CTA Not Present" persisted. TWO cross-CTA multicast
ADDRESSING bugs were found AFTER that restore -- the §H22 SW64 bug (a peer writing at TWICE the
correct offset, hidden by the atom_w == BK == 64 coincidence at SW128) and the §H27z.4
nchunk_term bug. Either produces corruption-under-load that a cluster barrier appears to fix by
perturbing timing. The barrier was masking bugs that have since been root-caused.

### ACTION AND RESIDUAL RISK

BLUBLAS_SM90_PER_TILE_CLUSTER_SYNC default flipped 1 -> 0. A DEFAULT, not a deletion: rebuild
with -D...=1 to restore it instantly; the call sites and history stay in the source.
Honest caveat: the matrix suite still cannot complete (the 128x112 family and 128x128_2x1_v_sk8
abort with sticky launch failures in BOTH arms), so coverage is 3010 of 5712, 53%. A
timing-sensitive fault can hide from ~25 clean targeted runs.

### SEPARATE BUG FOUND AND FIXED ALONG THE WAY (§H27za5)

128x256x64_2x1_h_swz64stsm -- added by me in §H27z.97 with the stmatrix mapping known-unfinished
(template :3934 says so) -- raises an ILLEGAL MEMORY ACCESS, which is STICKY: it destroys the
CUDA context and aborts the matrix suite at case 299 of 5766. Every correctness run between
§H27z.97 and now silently covered 5% of the config space. All stmatrix configs unregistered; the
`using` definitions stay, documented with their measured failure.


## §H27za6b STEP-3 RE-SCORED AFTER THE BARRIER REMOVAL -- 90.8% -> 93.0% (2026-08-13)

Plain build, no flags: cuobjdump reports MEMBAR.ALL.GPU x 0, so the flipped default reaches every
config in the library. Re-ran the 15 step-3 shapes with the set-A pins.

    variant  shapes   before    after    gain
    V8            4    89.9%    94.6%   +4.7
    V3            1    86.9%    91.2%   +4.3
    V6            1    84.6%    87.5%   +2.9
    V4            1    83.1%    85.4%   +2.3
    V7            3    94.6%    96.9%   +2.3
    V5            1    83.5%    84.9%   +1.4
    V1            1    88.5%    89.0%   +0.5
    V2            3    97.1%    95.8%   -1.3   <- one shape, see below
    ALL 15       15    90.8%    93.0%   +2.2

Seven of eight variants improved; twelve of fifteen shapes. Biggest single move: V8 at K=512,
76.7% -> 91.1% (+14.4), which had been the worst shape in the whole table.

V2's -1.3 is driven entirely by 2048x50304x16384 reading 99.6% -> 93.5%. cuBLAS's OWN number on
that shape moved 799.8 -> 819.2 TF between the two runs, and it has swung 5-7% run-to-run all

as a regression.

Set B improved by the same amount (A-B gap 2.7 -> 3.0 pts, control drift -0.2), which is the
predicted result: the barrier was raster-independent, so it could not change the A-B relationship.

**THE TARGET HAS MOVED.** Worst was V8 K=512 at 76.7% and the 192x192 family at 84.5%. Now the
192x192 family (V3-V6) is the ONLY group under 90% -- V5 84.9, V4 85.4, V6 87.5, V3 91.2, mean
87.3%. Everything else is 89-98%.

## §H27za7 RACE HUNT, AND TEN PRE-EXISTING CONTEXT-KILLING CONFIGS (2026-08-13)

Purpose: close the remaining coverage gap on the barrier removal. PRECISION was never at risk and
cannot be -- a barrier does no arithmetic, and every comparison reported maxRelErr 0.00000, i.e.
BIT-IDENTICAL, not merely close. The only real risk is a RACE, which presents as a wrong answer or
a crash, never as a small drift.

### TEN CONFIGS ABORT WITH A STICKY CUDA ERROR -- ALL PRE-EXISTING

Auto-discovered one at a time (a sticky error destroys the context, so only one surfaces per run),
using the ON arm, i.e. the UNMODIFIED code:

    128x112x64_1x4_v    128x112x64_2x4_v    128x112x64_2x2_v    128x128x64_1x2_h_pd5
    128x112x64_1x4_h    128x112x64_2x4_h    128x112x64_2x2_h    128x128x64_2x1_v_sk8
    128x144x64_2x1_h    64x64x64_4x2_h

NOT caused by the barrier change -- proven by the ON arm giving IDENTICAL results to OFF
(2990 PASS / 20 FAIL, same abort point) before any skipping. The whole 128x112 family across four
cluster shapes, plus pd5, sk8, 128x144_2x1_h and 64x64_4x2_h.

### THEY ARE UNREACHABLE IN PRODUCTION -- three independent checks

    in our 8 pinned variants?       0 of 10
    reachable from the dispatcher?  0 of 10  (grep of Bgemm_sm90_dispatcher.cu: zero hits each)
    present with the barrier ON?    10 of 10 -- pre-existing

They are registered in the X-macro so the matrix test can exercise them; nothing in the dispatcher
can select them, so no real workload reaches them. Near-misses worth noting: 128x128x64_2x1_v_sk8
aborts while our V1 pin is 128x128x64_2x1_v_sk2, and 128x128x64_1x2_h_pd5 aborts while V1 is a
different cluster entirely.

### A SEPARATE PROBLEM THEY EXPOSE

Even with all ten skipped the suite reaches only 4373 of 5712 cases, so more aborts remain. And
the ON arm is NON-DETERMINISTIC: run 1 produced no summary (crash), run 2 gave 4234 PASS / 139
FAIL on the same binary with the same skips. That instability exists WITH the barrier, so the
barrier was never buying determinism.

Consequence, independent of the barrier question: **nobody can fully validate this library today.**
Ten context-killing configs plus a non-deterministic suite is its own work item. They should be
FIXED or UNREGISTERED, not left as permanent skips.

### WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN

Coverage is still short of 100%, and a timing-sensitive fault can hide from clean runs by
definition. The barrier removal is a DEFAULT, not a deletion: -DBLUBLAS_SM90_PER_TILE_CLUSTER_SYNC=1
restores the old behaviour in one rebuild, and the call sites and history stay in the source.
Before this reaches the 1.7B training run it should have (a) the suite completing, and (b) a
BluTrain end-to-end run with loss curves compared.

V8 only, its four shapes, on the PIN `128x256x64_2x1_h_ep32s2` nt. Box changed again
(hazy-wolf-falls-fin-02, GPU 3), so every number below was re-measured; nothing is carried over.

### TENSOR-CORE UTILISATION: DEAD AS A HYPOTHESIS

    K        tensor% ours   cuBLAS    gap
    512          65.7        75.3    -9.6
    2048         88.5        92.3    -3.8

### THE MEASUREMENT: PC SAMPLING, K=512 AGAINST K=11264 AS A CONTROL

Both shapes have the SAME 1024 tiles and differ only in k_iters (8 vs 176), so per address
    samples = F + V*k_iters   ->   V = (s11264 - s512)/168,   F = s512 - 8V
separates per-tile cost F from mainloop cost V. Sampling rates matched (103 vs 100 samples/us
over 10 profiled launches each), which is what makes the subtraction legitimate.

    FIXED (per-tile) total   24,809 samples = 24.03 us = 39.9% of the 60.3 us K=512 kernel
      inside the 8 epilogue chunks         14,904 = 14.44 us = 60.1% of fixed

    the store chain, FIXED component only        samples      us    % of fixed
      STS                                            872    0.84         3.5
      BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING                      2,358    2.28         9.5
      MEMBAR.ALL.CTA                                 169    0.16         0.7
      FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S                           3,284    3.18        13.2
      F2FP.BF16.F32.PACK_AB                          759    0.74         3.1
      FMUL.FTZ                                       739    0.72         3.0
      CS2R                                           652    0.63         2.6
      UTMASTG.3D                                     407    0.39         1.6
      ----------------------------------------------------------------------
      store chain total                            9,241    8.95        37.2
      of which PURE SYNC                           5,811    5.63        23.4

**5.63 us of synchronisation against a 6.39 us total fixed-cost deficit** (fit: ours a=18.88,
cuBLAS a=12.49). ~88% of everything V8 still loses, in one mechanism.

### AND IT CORRECTS THE MEMBAR THEORY

MEMBAR.ALL.CTA costs 0.16 us -- 0.7% of the fixed cost. It is the CHEAP half of the pair.
The expense is FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S (3.18 us) and BAR.SYNC (2.28 us). §H27z.98 doubled the chunk
width to halve the MEMBARs and measured 21.5% WORSE; it was aiming at the 0.7% instruction.
Membar count is now closed as a target on evidence, not on a failed attempt.

The SASS, verified statically: 8 MEMBAR.ALL.CTA, 8 of 8 immediately followed by
FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S, 8 UTMASTG.3D -- exactly BN/EPI_TILE_N = 256/32 = 8 chunks, one pair each.
MEMBAR.ALL.GPU is 0, i.e. §H27za4's cluster-barrier removal is still live in this build.

### WHY cuBLAS DOES NOT PAY IT, AND WHAT THE FIX ACTUALLY IS

    ours                              cuBLAS nvjet_..._256x128_64x4_1x2_h_bz_coopA_TNT
      F2FP.BF16.F32.PACK_AB             F2FP.BF16.F32.PACK_AB
      STS                               STSM.16.MT88.4
      BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING           FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S
      MEMBAR.ALL.CTA                    WARPGROUP.ARRIVE
      FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S

STSM is WARP-COLLECTIVE and internally ordered, so cuBLAS needs only the async-proxy fence. Plain
STS is per-thread, so before the TMA engine may read that smem we must rendezvous the warpgroup
(BAR.SYNC) and order the stores (MEMBAR) first -- 8 times per output tile.

The MEMBAR is NOT removable from PTX and that is settled, not assumed: `fence_probe.cu` compiled
in isolation on sm_90a shows EVERY writable form emits one (`fence.proxy.async.shared::cta` with
or without a memory clobber -> MEMBAR.ALL.CTA + FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S; generic -> MEMBAR.ALL.GPU +
FENCE). CUTLASS uses the identical PTX (barrier.h:733, copy_sm90_tma.hpp:1217). cuBLAS's bare
fence is emitted through NVIDIA's internal path and is not a technique that can be copied.

**So the fix is STSM, and STSM is REAL UNFINISHED WORK, not a knob.** §H27z.97 tried it and it
failed correctness because the wgmma-fragment -> stmatrix register/address mapping is unfinished;
template.cuh:3934 says so in the source, and §H27za5 unregistered all three stmatrix configs after
`128x256x64_2x1_h_swz64stsm` raised a STICKY illegal access that capped every correctness run at
5% coverage. The prerequisite (the swizzled epilogue buffer) is already proven free: §H27z.94
measured it bit-exact with conflicts down 70x and duration unchanged.

### WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT PROMISE

Ceiling if the sync cost went to ZERO: 6.39 - 5.63 = 0.76 us of fixed cost left, i.e. K=512 would
go from 90.7% to roughly parity and K=2048 from 94.4% to ~99%. K=11264 is already 98.0% and has
almost nothing to gain. That is the honest size of the prize: it is the whole remaining V8 gap,
but V8's gap is only large at small K.

NOT YET PROVEN: that a correct stmatrix epilogue actually removes the BAR.SYNC in OUR structure.
cuBLAS's does, and the mechanism is understood, but we have never had a working stmatrix path to
measure. Deriving and CuTe-verifying the fragment->address mapping is the prerequisite, and it is
the one piece of this that is genuine implementation rather than measurement.

### TOOLING FIXED ALONG THE WAY

  1 PC sampling collected NOTHING on the first attempt: `--sampling-interval` is unrecognised in
    CUDA 13's ncu (renamed --warp-sampling-*). The retry passed the same bad flag, so both arms
    died identically and the phase reported an empty source page as if the metrics were at fault.
    Flag dropped (auto is the default) and the metric list is now QUERIED from ncu.
  2 tools/h27z93_ncu_table.py matched metric columns by SUBSTRING, so it selected ncu's `.avg`
    column while the header said `.sum` -- and ncu scales dur/dram per row (us vs ms, MB vs GB).
    Both sides shared the wrong column so every RATIO was still valid and no conclusion drawn from
    them was wrong, but the absolute numbers were not what they claimed. Exact names now.
  3 h27za8 truncated its own SUMMARY.md, so re-running one phase to fix a tooling bug would have
    deleted the phases that already succeeded. It now appends, and each invocation also writes a
    standalone RUN-<stamp>.md. OUT= for a clean directory.
  4 The region split (prologue/mainloop/epilogue) is NOT trustworthy on this kernel: the heuristic
    takes the backward branch containing wgmma, which is the inner k-loop only, giving 184/96/1800
    of 2080 instructions. The persistent TILE loop therefore falls inside "epilogue", so that label
    means "not the k-loop". Read the PER-ADDRESS list, which is what located both this and the
    §H27za4 barrier.

## §H27zb0 THE STMATRIX ADDRESS BUG, AND THE SWIZZLE WIN IT UNCOVERED -- V8 94.97% -> 97.31% (2026-08-14)

V8 only, PIN `128x256x64_2x1_h_ep32s2` nt, GPU 3 on hazy-wolf-falls-fin-02.

### THE BUG, FOUND BY DERIVATION WITH ZERO GPU TIME

§H27za5 had unregistered all three stmatrix configs because `128x256x64_2x1_h_swz64stsm` raised a
STICKY illegal memory access that destroyed the CUDA context and aborted the matrix suite at case
299 of 5766 -- silently capping every correctness run at 5% coverage. The comment at
template.cuh:4139 blamed unfinished work ("the wgmma-fragment -> stmatrix register/address mapping
must be derived and CuTe-verified, not guessed"). That comment was THREE SECTIONS STALE: §H27z.76
derived the mapping, probe_stmatrix.cu verified it 0/256, §H27z.77 hoisted the address.

The actual fault was in the §H27z.77 hoist:

    stsm_lane_off[gl] = ((rr*9) ^ (4*gl + am)) * 8        ->  rr*64 + (rr ^ g)*8

Both terms are the SPAN=8 / SHIFT=0 special case and nothing asserted it. Derived generally from
epi_swz_index, whose consistency condition is C_BOX_N == EPI_SPAN*8, using the fact that band is
always a multiple of 8 (so (band >> shift) & (span-1) == 0 for every legal span and the row term
collapses to rr alone):

    epi_swz_index(band+rr, 8*g) = band*C_BOX_N + rr*C_BOX_N + ((rr >> SHIFT) ^ g)*8

Enumerated over every (band, rr, am, gl) in Python BEFORE touching the kernel:

    C_BOX_N=64 SPAN=8 SHIFT=0    old 0 mismatches    new 0     <- the one VALIDATED config
    C_BOX_N=32 SPAN=4 SHIFT=1    old 168             new 0     <- V8; old max index 4344 of 4096

The out-of-bounds index IS the sticky illegal access. The wrong XOR is why the atom-staged twin
`_swz64r64stsm` returned wrong numbers instead of crashing. And it explains why the ONLY config
that ever passed was `256x128x64_1x2_h_rs2_swz128r64stsm`: EPI_TILE_N=64 + EPI_SWIZZLE_BYTES=128
gives exactly C_BOX_N=64, SPAN=8, SHIFT=0, the case the formula was written for.

FIXED, plus two static_asserts pinning the invariant that was silently violated (C_BOX_N ==
EPI_SPAN*8, and C_BOX_N >= 32 since one stmatrix.x4 spans 32 bf16 columns). The use site
`stsm_lane_off[gj & 1]` also hardcoded two groups per chunk; it is now `(grp_tc % C_BOX_N)/32`,
which reduces to `gj & 1` at C_BOX_N=64.

### CORRECTNESS GATE: CLEAN, INCLUDING THE CONTROL

Every config bit-exact (maxRelErr 0.00000) on all four V8 shapes, each in its OWN PROCESS so a
surviving sticky fault could only kill its own run. `rs2_swz128r64stsm` was carried as the CONTROL
-- the one config that always passed, which the generalisation had to leave untouched -- and it
passed. Both previously-broken configs now pass.

### THEN THE ACTUAL RESULT: STMATRIX IS NOT THE WIN. THE SWIZZLE IS.

5 repeats per config, %cuB, spreads 0.1-0.5 points:

    config        K=512  (5 runs)                 mean    K=2048 (5 runs)              mean
    ep32s2        90.7 90.9 90.9 90.9 90.7       90.82    96.3 96.3 96.2 96.3 96.2    96.26
    swz64         95.6 95.8 95.6 95.9 95.8       95.74    97.7 97.7 97.6 97.7 97.8    97.70
    swz64stsm     92.5 92.7 92.7 92.6 92.6       92.62    96.9 96.5 96.9 97.0 96.9    96.84

Adoption rule, written down BEFORE the run: adopt only if the worst swz64 run beats the best
baseline run. K=512 95.6 > 90.9 (+4.7). K=2048 97.6 > 96.3 (+1.3). Both clear, and the three
configs' distributions do not overlap at all: swz64 > swz64stsm > ep32s2.

`swz64` differs from the pin by ONE template argument, EPI_SWIZZLE_BYTES=64. Tile, cluster, raster,
stages, layout and split-K are identical, so this is the same variant made faster, not a
substitution -- the apples-to-apples pin is preserved.

    V8, three reliable shapes (K=50304 excluded, 7.5% run-to-run per §H27za8)
        ep32s2   90.8 / 96.3 / 97.7   mean 94.97
        swz64    95.7 / 97.7 / 98.5   mean 97.31      +2.35 pts

### WHY WE MISSED THIS FOR A DAY -- HYPOTHESIS 1 WAS MASKED, NOT DEAD

§H27z.97 measured this EXACT config at 77.2% against the baseline's 77.4% and recorded the swizzle
as worthless. That run is stamped 2026-08-13T09:27Z. The per-tile cluster barrier came out at
~19:13 the same day. While that barrier was consuming 33.9% of all PC-sampling stall samples,
removing bank conflicts underneath it changed nothing measurable. With it gone the same knob is
worth +4.8 points.

**Bank conflicts were never a dead hypothesis. They were buried under a larger one, and the
"duration unchanged" result was recorded as a refutation.** The general lesson, which cost a day:
a null result only refutes a hypothesis if nothing bigger is masking it, and the way to know is to
re-test every null result after removing a dominant cost. §H27z.94/.97/.98/.99 were all measured
under the barrier and all of them are now suspect, not just this one.

### THE MECHANISM, ncu at K=512

    config          dur   tensor%  barrier  long_sb  mio_thr     bankconf         inst
    ep32s2         72.7      65.8     35.1     36.3      0.2    1,965,557   10,915,288
    swz64          68.2      70.2     37.8     30.4      0.0      399,484   11,874,385
    swz64stsm      71.3      66.9     35.5     31.1      0.0      344,063   14,566,656
    cuBLAS         63.8      75.0     23.4     31.6     10.4      348,803    6,338,534

The swizzle cuts conflicts 4.9x to 399K, which is PARITY with cuBLAS's 349K -- that inefficiency
is now closed. long_scoreboard falls 36.3 -> 30.4 and tensor% rises 65.8 -> 70.2, i.e. the
conflicts were producing real memory-dependency stalls.

STMATRIX cuts conflicts marginally further (344K) but adds 2.7M instructions, +22.7%, and the
duration goes straight back up. That is the whole explanation for why it loses to the plain
swizzle: the group-head filter plus the 4-register gather with a per-q beta path costs more scalar
work than the 8x store reduction saves. STSM is not wrong now -- it beats the baseline -- it is
INSTRUCTION-INEFFICIENT as written. Making it pay would need the gather restructured, and the
swizzle already banks most of the available ground.

### WHAT REMAINS AT K=512 AFTER THE SWIZZLE (95.7%)

    instructions   ours 11.87M vs cuBLAS 6.34M    1.87x       (§H27z.99 says count is not causal)
    barrier stall  37.8 vs 23.4                   1.6x        (§H27z.99c says elastic)
    mio_throttle   0.0 vs 10.4                    NEVER       <- still unexplained, still the
    mem_thr%       49.7 vs 61.4                                  most stable structural gap
    tensor%        70.2 vs 75.0

mio_throttle stayed at 0.0 through the swizzle fix, so removing conflicts did NOT make us saturate
the memory pipes. That gap is now the only counter difference that has survived every experiment.

### TOOLING FAILURE WORTH RECORDING

Phase 2's SASS census produced four IDENTICAL rows and confirmed nothing: the awk filter keyed on
`Li128ELi256ELi64E`, which matches every instantiation of that tile in the library rather than the
one config under test. Phase 3's instruction counts (10.9M / 11.9M / 14.6M) are what prove the
builds actually differ. A census that cannot distinguish the arms is worse than no census -- it
reads as evidence of "no change".

### IMMEDIATE FOLLOW-UP (not done, scope was V8)

`_swz64` configs already exist for the OTHER step-3 tiles: `256x128x64_2x1_h_swz64` (V2),
`192x192x64_2x1_v_swz64` and `_2x1_h_swz64` (V3-V6), and V7 shares V8's tile outright. If the
barrier was masking the swizzle on V8 it was masking it everywhere, and the 192x192 family is the
group still under 90%. That is the next measurement, and it is a pin change per variant, not new
code.

### §H27zb0b WHY THE 1.93x STMATRIX PROBE DID NOT TRANSFER, AND WHY BETA IS NOT THE COST

Two sub-questions closed with data already on disk, no new GPU time.

**Are the swizzle and stmatrix separable?** Only one way. stmatrix REQUIRES the swizzle and that is
measured, not stylistic (template.cuh:456 asserts it): probe_stsm_banks.cu put STSM on a LINEAR
buffer at 192 conflicts / 3.217 ms against plain STS's 192 / 3.230 ms -- worth 0%. On the SWIZZLED
buffer both hit 0 conflicts and STSM measured 1.93x (0.295 vs 0.570 ms). Swizzle is Stage A and is
legal alone; stmatrix is Stage B and is not.

**So why did the 1.93x not show up?** Because the probe measured the store path in ISOLATION, and
in the real kernel that path is 1.40% of the time (STS = 872 of 62,242 samples at K=512). A 1.93x
on 1.40% is worth at most 872*(1 - 1/1.93) = 420 samples = 0.68% of the kernel. stmatrix COSTS 4.5%
(68.2 -> 71.3 us). It is paying 4.5 to win 0.68. The probe was not wrong -- it optimised something
that does not matter at this scale, which is the bank-conflict lesson in reverse: a microbenchmark
makes a real speedup look decisive when the thing it speeds up is 1% of the workload. Any future
"probe says Nx" must be multiplied by that component's measured share of the kernel BEFORE it earns
implementation time.

Note stmatrix is still a NET-NEGATIVE ADD-ON, not a net-negative feature: swz64stsm at 92.6% beats
the 90.8% pin because it carries the swizzle, it just gives 2.9 of the swizzle's 4.8 back.

**Beta is NOT the overhead -- eliminated, do not re-open.** The epilogue chunks contain the whole
beta read-back path in static code, and it looks expensive: 64 LDG.E.CONSTANT, 128 FFMA.FTZ, 64
ISETP.GE.OR, 64 PRMT. PC sampling at K=512 says otherwise:

    opcode                sites   samples   % of kernel
    LDG.E.CONSTANT           64         0        0.00
    FFMA.FTZ                128         0        0.00
    ISETP.GE.OR              64         0        0.00
    PRMT                     64         0        0.00
    FSETP.NEU.FTZ.AND         1         6        0.01
    ---------------------------------------------------
    BETA PATH               321         6        0.01%     (FENCE 5.28%, BAR.SYNC 3.72%)

There is exactly ONE `beta != 0.0f` test in the region: the compiler hoists it and branches over
the entire read-back, so 321 static instructions execute zero times when beta==0. Making beta a
template parameter would remove 321 instructions of CODE SIZE and 0.01% of runtime, at the cost of
doubling the config count. Not worth it -- and this is where our single kernel matches cuBLAS's two.

**cuBLAS DOES specialise, and it buys them nothing we lack.** Already resolved 2026-07-24 by
examples/bz_probe.cu (single variable, same shape): beta=0 -> `..._h_bz_coopA_TNT`, beta=1 ->
`..._h_badd_coopA_TNT`. So `bz` = beta-zero, `badd` = beta-add: two kernels where we ship one with a
free branch. Every nvjet name we have ever profiled carries `bz` (28 of 30), because every
benchmark we run is beta=0.

**What is still unlocated:** the +2.7M instructions themselves. Not beta, not the store swap. Two
candidates remain -- (a) the runtime chunk filter `grp_ch != wg_ch_start + epi_ch` evaluated per
group-head per unit inside the r loop, and (b) the r loop failing to fold, since group heads are
r%16 in {0,2} so 48 of 64 iterations exist only to fail a predicate. Separating them needs SASS and
PC sampling for swz64 and swz64stsm, neither of which we have: every capture so far is of the PIN,
which contains neither the swizzle nor stmatrix. tools/h27zb1 phases 3 and 4.

## §H27zb1 THE SWIZZLE ROLLOUT, THE V6 CLIFF, AND THE BETA PREDICATION IN THE STMATRIX PATH (2026-08-14)

7 repeats per config throughout. Adoption rule, fixed before the run: adopt only where the
candidate's WORST run beats the incumbent's BEST -- overlap is not a result.

### V8 CONFIRMED ON ALL FOUR SHAPES, AND V7 TOO

    V   shape              pin     swz64    delta   verdict
    V8  K=512             90.80    95.80    +5.00   ADOPT  (swz min 95.8 > pin max 91.0)
    V8  K=2048            96.34    97.71    +1.37   ADOPT  (swz min 97.2 > pin max 96.4)
    V8  K=11264           97.86    98.16    +0.30   overlap
    V8  K=50304           96.60    97.74    +1.14   overlap (the known 7.5% shape)
    V2  2048x2048x16384   96.46    96.54    +0.08   overlap
    V2  5632x2048x16384   97.44    97.97    +0.53   overlap
    V2  2048x50304x16384  95.63    94.91    -0.72   overlap
    V6  16384x5632x2048   87.04    28.06   -58.98   *** REJECT ***
    V7  16384x2048x2048   96.24    97.57    +1.33   ADOPT
    V7  16384x2048x5632   97.57    97.81    +0.24   overlap
    V7  16384x512x2048    97.31    97.96    +0.65   ADOPT

swz64 returned 95.8 on all seven runs at K=512 against a pin that never exceeded 91.0. V2 is
neutral everywhere -- the 256x128 tile does not benefit, and that is itself informative: the
swizzle is not a free win per tile, it depends on the store geometry.

### THE V6 CLIFF -- 87% -> 28%, AND IT IS *CORRECT*

`192x192x64_2x1_h_swz32ep16` PASSES (the harness prints NO DATA for a non-PASS, and it printed
numbers) and runs 3x SLOWER than the unswizzled pin. Spread 27.8-28.3, so it is not noise.
This kills "roll the swizzle out everywhere": it is +5.0 on 128x256 at swz64 and -59.0 on 192x192
at swz32. UNINVESTIGATED. The obvious first suspect is that swz32 -> EPI_SPAN=2 -> C_BOX_N=16 ->
a 32-BYTE inner box for the C TMA descriptor, which is a quarter of a 128 B transaction, so the
store may be issuing 4x the TMA traffic. NOT confirmed. Do not pin any swz32 config until it is.

### PHASE 3 (STATIC SASS DIFF) WAS INVALID -- SAME CLASS OF BUG, SECOND TIME

    swz64:     6 kernels, 19208 instructions
    swz64stsm: 3 kernels,  5720 instructions

The tail pattern `Li32ELi2ELi64ELi0ELb0E` matched BOTH raster h and raster v swz64 configs because
the tile filter stopped at `Li128ELi256ELi64ELi2ELi1E` and never pinned the raster argument;
swz64stsm exists only at raster h. Every delta in that table is the artifact of 6 kernels against
3. This is the SECOND time a census filter has silently compared the wrong sets (§H27zb0 phase 2
keyed on tile dims and returned four identical rows). Rule: a census must print how many kernels it
matched, and any two arms with different counts are not comparable.

### PHASE 4 -- PC SAMPLING FOUND IT: THE BETA PATH IS PREDICATED, NOT BRANCHED, IN THE STSM ARM

    opcode                  swz64      stsm      delta   % of positive diff
    LDG.E.CONSTANT              0     2,733     +2,733       26.5
    MEMBAR.ALL.CTA             29     1,743     +1,714       16.6
    IMAD.U32                  109     1,238     +1,129       11.0
    PRMT                        0     1,067     +1,067       10.4
    FFMA.FTZ                    0       976       +976        9.5
    VIADD                     181       985       +804        7.8
    ISETP.GE.OR                 0       334       +334        3.2
    STS                       626         0       -626
    STSM.16.M88.4               0       197       +197
    totals                 58,319    61,150      +4.9%   (ncu duration said +4.5%)

LDG.E.CONSTANT / FFMA.FTZ / PRMT / ISETP.GE.OR are EXACTLY the beta read-back -- the global load of
C, the beta*C multiply-add, the bf16 unpack, the bounds guard. They are precisely ZERO in the
swizzle arm and executing in the stmatrix arm: 5,110 samples, 55% of everything stmatrix added.

CAUSE. In the stmatrix path the guard is `beta != 0.0f && global_row < M && gc + 1 < N` with `gc`
computed from the loop variable q, so the loop-INVARIANT beta test is &&-fused to a loop-VARIANT
bound. ptxas PREDICATES the sequence instead of branching around it. The scalar path spells the
condition identically but its `global_col` is computed OUTSIDE the loop, so it gets a real branch
(BSSY/BRA) and costs 0.01% (§H27zb0b measured that directly: 321 static sites, 6 samples).

NOT a correctness bug and NOT DRAM traffic -- `beta != 0.0f` is first in the &&, so C is never
fetched at beta==0. A predicated-off instruction still occupies an ISSUE SLOT, and that is what the
samples count. It matters because §H27z.96 already has us at an 11.3% issue rate against cuBLAS's
22-27.8%: issue bandwidth is the one resource we are demonstrably short of.

THIS REFINES A PRIOR CONCLUSION RATHER THAN OVERTURNING IT. The deferred-work list says the beta
C-read is "fully skipped at beta=0 (the bz fast path already exists, verified)". True semantically,
and true for cost in the scalar path. False for cost in the stmatrix path, where "skipped" is
predication, not a branch.

FIX (§H27zb2): split explicitly on beta before the q loop so the beta==0 arm provably contains no
LDG, no gc and no bounds test. Predicted: those four opcodes -> ~0, stmatrix total 61,150 -> ~56,040
against swz64's 58,319, i.e. stmatrix would move from losing by 3.2 points to winning.

### AND THE +23% INSTRUCTION COUNT, ANSWERED

ncu says instructions +22.7% (11.87M -> 14.57M) while duration is only +4.5% and samples +4.9%. So
the extra instructions are overwhelmingly CHEAP -- they are not the cost, and §H27z.99 already
established for this kernel that instruction count is not causal (-14% dynamic instructions moved
the duration by nothing). The 4.5% of TIME is what the PC-sampling table above decomposes, and 55%
of it is the predicated beta sequence. Do not chase the 22.7% as a number.

### OPEN, IN PRIORITY ORDER

  1 BETA GATE BEFORE ANY STMATRIX ADOPTION. The matrix harness never sets beta (zero occurrences of
    the word in test_bgemm_sm90_matrix.cu), so the beta!=0 arm of a PINNED config has never run on
    hardware. test_bgemm_sm90_beta covers beta but goes through the DISPATCHER, so it cannot reach
    a pinned stmatrix config -- the exact shape of the §H27z.47 miss, where b0-nan could not reach
    the SM89 path it would have caught. Needs --beta in the matrix test. BluTrain drives beta=1 on
    every grad-accumulation micro-step, so this is not optional.
  2 V6's 3x regression on swz32ep16 -- correct and catastrophic, cause unknown, TMA box width is
    the first suspect.
  3 MEMBAR.ALL.CTA 29 -> 1,743 in the stmatrix arm, 16.6% of the added work, unexplained.
  4 The 192x192 family (V3/V4/V5) still has NO swizzle route: their pins are unchunked, and the
    index needs C_BOX_N == EPI_SPAN*8 while unchunked 192x192 gives C_BOX_N=96 (SPAN would be 12;
    only 2/4/8 exist). This is the group still under 90%.
  5 Re-test every null result recorded BEFORE the §H27za4 barrier removal. The swizzle was measured
    worthless at 09:27Z and is worth +5.0 after 19:13Z. §H27z.94/.97/.98/.99 are all in that window.

### §H27zb3-plan THE ADOPTION PATH INTO PRODUCTION -- deliberately NOT done yet

Step-3 "pins" are a MEASUREMENT concept: which config we score against cuBLAS's counterpart. They
do not change what BluTrain runs. That comes from the dispatcher, and the two must not be conflated.

HOW A SHAPE ACTUALLY GETS A KERNEL (Bgemm_sm90_dispatcher.cu:164-169, §H27z.45):

    cfg = lookup(kTable_<lay>, M, N, K)      TIER 1  exact (M,N,K) table, 437 entries
    if (cfg == 0xFFFF) cfg = tree_<lay>(...) TIER 2  fitted decision tree, only on a table miss

For BluTrain's 15 shapes the split is **1 TIER-1 / 14 TIER-2** (§H27z.53): only 16384x512x2048 nn
hits the exact table; the other fourteen fall through to the fitted tree.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ADOPTION -- it is SMALL, and it is deliberately last. Adding exact tier-1 entries
for the 15 shapes captures all of BluTrain and bypasses the tree for them. That is the whole change.
It is left until the optimisation work is finished, because every pin we adopt now would have to be
re-entered later anyway, and a half-updated table is worse than a consistent stale one.

THE PART THAT IS NOT SMALL, recorded so it is not mistaken for "just add swz64":
Bgemm_sm90_dispatch_table.h is GENERATED ("do not hand-edit") from a 225-shape x ~254-config
campaign plus a 204-shape small-output campaign. It contains ZERO swz64 entries and 21 ep32s2 ones.
Both campaigns ran BEFORE the §H27za4 barrier removal, so their winners were selected under exactly
the masking that made the swizzle measure -0.2 pts at 09:27Z on 2026-08-13 and +4.8 pts after 19:13Z.
So it is not merely that swz64 is absent from the candidate set -- the SELECTIONS ALREADY IN THE
TABLE, all 437 of them, and the three fitted trees, were chosen against a kernel that no longer
exists. Adding 15 entries fixes BluTrain; the other 422 stay suspect until the campaign is re-run.

ORDER OF WORK, agreed:
  1 finish optimising against the step-3 pins (measurement only, no production impact)
  2 THEN add tier-1 entries for the 15 shapes -> BluTrain picks them up
  3 SEPARATELY, re-run the dispatcher campaign with the post-barrier kernel and the new configs in
    the candidate set -> fixes the other 422 entries and the trees
Nothing in steps 2-3 is started. This entry exists so that "the dispatcher was never updated" is a
recorded decision with a reason, not an oversight discovered later.

    128x256 + swz64   +4.80

Same C_BOX_N=32, same EPI_SPAN=4, identical swizzle arithmetic, bit-exact both ways, opposite sign.
The swizzle is not a property of the epilogue -- it is a property of the epilogue ON A GIVEN TILE.

### WHAT THIS EXPOSES ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN

Every deep diagnostic this week was V8: the PC sampling, the fixed/variable K-decomposition, the

never been profiled at all, and we have been trying levers on it that were derived from a different
