Note `clkMin` at 1200/1300/1400 equals `clkAvg` exactly -- the lock is real. Everywhere else it is
hundreds of MHz below, and the reason string says POWER_CAP.

#### PHASE 2 OBSERVATIONS — the decisive evidence. It is cuBLAS's clock that moves, not ours.

This is the phase that settles everything. Clocks are per-kernel, in MHz:

| pin | clock | arm | %cuB | ourClk | cubClk | cub−our |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | free | default | 96.0 | 1513.0 | 1667.6 | **+154.7** |
| V1 | free | preheat | 112.0 | 1511.9 | 1446.1 | −65.7 |
| V3 | free | default | 97.1 | 1386.1 | 1429.7 | +43.6 |
| V3 | free | preheat | 100.8 | 1400.1 | 1377.2 | −22.9 |
| V6 | free | default | 97.2 | 1413.9 | 1445.2 | +31.3 |
| V6 | free | preheat | 101.2 | 1418.3 | 1397.8 | −20.5 |
| V8 | free | default | 95.8 | 1565.7 | 1696.2 | **+130.5** |
| V8 | free | preheat | 108.9 | 1599.2 | 1521.0 | −78.2 |
| V1 | 1200 | default | 105.7 | 1189.2 | 1182.9 | −6.3 |
| V3 | 1200 | default | 100.1 | 1192.3 | 1192.1 | **−0.2** |
| V6 | 1200 | default | 99.5 | 1191.9 | 1191.2 | **−0.7** |
| V8 | 1200 | default | 101.7 | 1169.7 | 1158.0 | −11.8 |
| V6 | 1400 | default | 99.2 | 1394.9 | 1394.7 | **−0.2** |
| V1 | 1755 | default | 99.7 | 1532.6 | 1614.8 | +82.2 |
| V3 | 1755 | default | 94.5 | 1403.0 | 1484.8 | +81.8 |
| V6 | 1755 | default | 94.5 | 1432.7 | 1505.5 | +72.8 |
| V8 | 1755 | default | 98.3 | 1594.1 | 1663.7 | +69.6 |

**In the default arm at free, cuBLAS runs 31 to 155 MHz FASTER than our kernel does, on the same
card, in the same process, seconds apart.** That is the entire mechanism. It was measured first,
while the card was cold and idle, so it got the boost clock.

What preheating does to each side, stated as a delta:

| pin | clock | our clock change | cuBLAS clock change | score change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | free | −1.1 | **−221.5** | +16.0 |
| V3 | free | +13.9 | **−52.5** | +3.7 |
| V6 | free | +4.4 | **−47.4** | +4.0 |
| V8 | free | +33.5 | **−175.2** | +13.1 |
| V1 | 1200 | +2.4 | +0.4 | −0.3 |
| V3 | 1200 | −1.4 | −1.2 | −0.1 |
| V6 | 1200 | +1.2 | −0.7 | +0.1 |
| V8 | 1200 | −1.6 | −2.2 | +0.5 |
| V6 | 1400 | −0.3 | −0.9 | +0.0 |
| V1 | 1755 | −46.6 | **−172.1** | +10.5 |
| V3 | 1755 | +35.2 | **−78.6** | +7.1 |
| V6 | 1755 | +34.3 | **−79.9** | +7.3 |
| V8 | 1755 | −5.4 | **−145.9** | +11.2 |

**Preheating does not speed OUR kernel up. It slows CUBLAS down to the speed our kernel was
already running at.** Our clock moves by −47 to +35 MHz with no consistent sign; cuBLAS's clock
falls every single time, by 20 to 222 MHz. At a lock that holds, both numbers are within 2.5 MHz
and the score does not move.

**AND THE CLOCK RATIO QUANTITATIVELY PREDICTS THE SCORE.** If a score is really just "our clock
vs their clock", then

    predicted %cuB(preheat) = %cuB(default) x [ (ourClk/cubClk)_preheat / (ourClk/cubClk)_default ]

Tested on all 20 pin x clock cells: **correlation r = 0.9741, mean absolute error 0.69 points**,
against arm swings as large as 16.0 points. The clock ratio is not merely correlated with the
order effect -- it accounts for essentially all of it.

#### PHASE 3 OBSERVATIONS — cuBLAS runs the identical kernel at every clock

| pin | free | 1200 | 1755 |
|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | `nvjet_sm90_tst_128x128_64x6_1x2_h_bz_split` | same | same |
| V3 | `nvjet_sm90_tst_192x192_64x3_1x2_h_bz_coop` | same | same |
| V6 | `nvjet_sm90_tst_192x192_64x4_2x1_v_bz_coop` | same | same |
| V8 | `nvjet_sm90_tst_256x128_64x4_1x2_h_bz_coop` | same | same |

Twelve profiles, four distinct kernel names, zero switches.

#### VERDICT ON EACH SUSPICION

- **(A) ORDER — CONFIRMED, and it is the whole free-clock deficit.** +4.70 median at free,
  +7.10 at 1755, exactly 0.00 wherever the lock holds, positive on all 15 pins, and predicted to
  within 0.69 points by the clock ratio alone.
- **(B) POWER — REFUTED.** The prediction was that OUR heavier instruction stream would earn our
  kernel a lower clock. The opposite is observed: under preheat our clock is flat or slightly UP
  while cuBLAS's collapses. We do not lose clock for being instruction-heavy. §H27z's parked
  power/clock track can stay parked, and this is the measurement that justifies it.
- **(C) KERNEL SWITCHING — REFUTED.** Identical kernel names at free, 1200 and 1755.

#### WHAT THIS CHANGES

**The free-clock "96.3%" was a measurement fault and must not be quoted again.** Corrected free
standing is ~100.8%. The locked-clock standing was right all along.

Per-pin standing at each clock, default arm, median of repeats. The three middle columns are the
locks the card can actually hold:

V7*/V8* rows carry the layout caveat below.

**TWO INDEPENDENT CONSISTENCY CHECKS, BOTH PASS.**

1. **The lock value does not matter once the lock holds.** Mean over the 8 clean pins:
   1200 -> 100.49, 1300 -> 100.51, 1400 -> 100.33. A spread of 0.18 points across a 200 MHz range.
2. **Every clean pin reproduces its committed scoreboard number.** V1 104.80-105.05 vs 105.19,
   V2 100.30-100.70 vs 100.63, V2b 99.85 vs 99.86, V2c 99.00 vs 99.03, V3 99.85-99.95 vs 99.90,
   V4 100.40 vs 100.49, V5 100.55 vs 100.54, V6 99.15-99.20 vs 99.27. All within ~0.12. The
   scoreboard and this suite were produced by different scripts on different days and they agree.

**Mean of the 8 clean pins across the three holdable locks: 100.48% of cuBLAS.**

#### RULES THIS ADDS TO THE CAMPAIGN

1. **Lock the clock, and then CHECK the lock held** -- read `clkMin` and the throttle reason from
   during the run. On this H200 the sustainable ceiling is between 1400 and 1474 MHz; a 1755
   request behaves exactly like free.
2. **Never compare a cold measurement against a hot one.** Whoever is measured first on an idle
   card wins by up to 16 points for no reason connected to the kernel.
3. **A free-clock comparison needs `BLUBLAS_PREHEAT_MS` or `BLUBLAS_REF_AFTER`**, otherwise it is
   measuring the boost-clock schedule.
4. **Report which arm and which clock a number came from.** A bare "%cuB" is now ambiguous.

#### FOUR BUGS FOUND WHILE RUNNING IT — all four silently produced clean-looking wrong numbers

- **The env-assignment bug — killed every swap row.** `${RA:+BLUBLAS_REF_AFTER=$RA} ./binary` does
  not set a variable; the shell parses the expansion as the COMMAND NAME. Every swap row failed
  and 225 rows the previous day came back empty. Fixed with an explicit `env`. **The pre-flight
  did not catch it because the pre-flight used a literal assignment** -- so it exercised a
  different code path from the grid. A pre-flight must run the same construction the grid runs.
- **Layout mixing in the batched grid.** Phase 1 batched by configuration name to save build time,
  but V7* (nn) and V8* (nt) SHARE the configuration `128x256x64_2x1_h_ep64swz128_rot2_pdl`, so a
  batch ran seven pins under a single layout flag and half of them got the wrong one. Caught only
  because V7 and V8b -- different shapes -- reported byte-identical 685.35 TFLOPS. Fixed by
  grouping on (configuration, layout). **The 7 affected pins are flagged and were excluded from
  every conclusion; the conclusion is stronger without them.**
- **Leaked clock samplers.** `kill $SP` killed a subshell, not the `nvidia-smi -lms` child under
  it. Over 500 accumulated and turned 8-second rows into 46-second rows, which is what made the
  first estimate come out at 40 hours. Fixed with one sampler for the whole phase.
- **Clock reported in Hz, not MHz.** `h27zD_perkernel.py` emitted raw `1512954621.7`. Fixed with a
  scale-if-greater-than-1e6 guard.

#### LIMITS OF THIS FINDING — stated plainly

- **All of it comes from ONE physical card**, `dry-snow-crunches-fin-03-GPU-0de7cb9c-eaa`. The
  mechanism (boost clock on an idle card) is generic to how NVIDIA GPUs manage clocks and there is
  no reason to expect it to be unique to this one, but the specific numbers -- +4.70 at free, the
  1400-1474 MHz sustainable ceiling, the 20-222 MHz cuBLAS drop -- are measured on that card only
  and are NOT verified across cards or on B300. Do not quote them as H200-wide, and do not quote
  them as universal.
- Phases 2 and 3 ran pin-by-pin, not batched, so they never touched the layout bug.
- The 1500/1600/1700 MHz points listed in the first suite header were dropped when the grid was
  cut to fit the time budget. 1474 and 1755 already bracket the sustainable ceiling, so no
  hypothesis lost coverage.

Artifacts: `profiling_reports/h27zD/` -- `rows.tsv` (746 rows), `perkernel.tsv` (40 rows),
`SUMMARY.md`, and `nsys/` (per-kernel profiles and kernel-identity logs).
Tools: `tools/h27zD_clock_suite.sh`, `tools/h27zD_perkernel.py`, `tools/h27zD_analyze.py`,
`tools/h27zD_timeit.sh`.

### §H27zE — THE CROSS-COMPARISON CAMPAIGN. Identity 15/15. And a measurement bug that invented a "+10.28% better than the pin" twice in a row.

Two things had never been done: (1) nothing ever CHECKED that cuBLAS launches the kernel we assume
it launches, and (2) every variant had only ever been run on its OWN shape.

**IDENTITY GATE — 15/15 MATCH.** nsys on all 15 pins, cuBLAS kernel name captured and diffed
against §H27zzj-C:

| pin | cuBLAS actually launched |
|---|---|
| V1 | `nvjet_sm90_tst_128x128_64x6_1x2_h_bz_splitK_NTT` |
| V2/V2b/V2c | `nvjet_sm90_tst_128x256_64x4_2x1_v_bz_coopA_NTN` |
| V3 | `nvjet_sm90_tst_192x192_64x3_1x2_h_bz_coopB_NNN` |
| V4 | `nvjet_sm90_tst_192x192_64x3_2x1_v_bz_coopB_NNN` |
| V5 | `nvjet_sm90_tst_192x192_64x3_2x1_v_bz_coopB_NTN` |
| V6 | `nvjet_sm90_tst_192x192_64x4_2x1_v_bz_coopB_TNN` |
| V7/V7b/V7c | `nvjet_sm90_tst_256x128_64x4_1x2_h_bz_coopA_NNT` |
| V8/V8b/V8c/V8d | `nvjet_sm90_tst_256x128_64x4_1x2_h_bz_coopA_TNT` |

Tile, cluster and raster agree on every shape. **The apples-to-apples pairing is verified, not
assumed.** §H27zzj-B is confirmed independently: V6 is the one 192x192 running 64x4; the rest 64x3.
The names now also carry `coopA`/`coopB` and a layout suffix, which older captures did not show.

**FIRST-PASS SCOREBOARD, each pin measured ALONE (this context is validated in §H27zF):**
mean **100.78% of cuBLAS**, 12 of 15 at or above parity, below only V2c 99.4, V6 98.9, V8d 99.9.
Movers vs the previous record: V8 +3.09, V5 +1.86, V8b +0.86, V7 +0.80; V1 −0.49, V6 −0.37.

**THE BUG.** Phase 2 passed all 9 champion configs to ONE process per shape and reported that
`128x256..._rot2_pdl` beat V2's pin by **+10.28%**, `+9.82%` on V2c and `+6.49%` on V2b. It
reproduced to two decimal places across two independent runs. **It was still wrong** — see §H27zF.
Reproducibility is not correctness: repeating a biased design forever just yields a precise wrong
answer, and no number of nsys passes would have exposed it.

**SEVEN DEFECTS IN THE TOOLING, ALL MINE, EACH FOUND ONLY BY BEING LOOKED FOR:**

| defect | consequence |
|---|---|
| EXPECT strings omitted the depth token (`128x256_2x1_v` is not a substring of `128x256_64x4_2x1_v`) | 11 FALSE `DIFFER` verdicts on a gate that had actually passed |
| resume key was (box, shape, rep), no LAYOUT | V8b silently skipped -- V7 `nn` and V8b `nt` share shape `16384x2048x2048`. **Same class as the §H27zD layout-grouping bug, reintroduced.** |
| clock locked once, verified once, at idle | **11 of 14 runs executed at 1980 MHz under a "1400" lock** and nothing said so |
| dispatcher home-pin lookup picked an arbitrary variant | nonsense deltas up to `+250.93%` |
| three clock helpers written but never called | the "fix" changed nothing |
| `clk_summary` emitted `NO SAMPLES`, not a valid assignment | `eval` fails -> unset var -> **crash** on the next arithmetic under `set -u` |
| header grew 11->15 columns with old files present | appending wide rows under a narrow header shifts every field index |

Fixes: per-run re-lock plus a during-run sampler recorded on every row; layout in all five resume
keys; a header-version guard that rotates a stale file instead of appending into it; and every one
verified by EXECUTION (all four append widths run and counted: P1=11, P2=15, P3=13, P3P=10).

### §H27zF — WHY: 713.90 alone, 648.73 alongside eight others. Not nsys, not order, not thermals.

Same config, same shape, same box, minutes apart, clock flat at 1410 (`clkMin == clkMax`):

    phase 1, alone, under nsys    256x128x64_2x1_h_ep32s2_pdl   713.90 TFLOPS  100.8%
    phase 2, 3rd of 9, no nsys    256x128x64_2x1_h_ep32s2_pdl   648.73 TFLOPS   91.4%

Seven arms on one shape, three reps, each arm changing exactly one thing:

| arm | A = the pin | B = the "winner" |
|---|---|---|
| alone | **713.24** | 715.42 |
| alone + nsys | **713.27** | — |
| A then B | 713.86 | 715.39 |
| B then A | 713.38 | 715.26 |
| A, C, B | 713.92 | 715.30 |
| **the nine-config list** | **666.47** | **715.66** |

- **nsys is INNOCENT** — 713.27 vs 713.24. Phase 1's number was right.
- **ORDER is INNOCENT** — A first 713.86, A second 713.38.
- **"more than one config" is INNOCENT** — two and three configs are both fine.
- **B is untouched in every context**, including 9th of 9.

**THE +10.28% COLLAPSES TO +0.31%.** Measured cleanly, 713.24 vs 715.42 — a tie. The pin was
never 10% behind; it was being deflated while its challenger was not, so the bias could not
cancel out of a ranking.

**CONSEQUENCE: phase 3 as designed was invalid** — 442 configs in one invocation is the same
context, worse. It was cancelled before running.

### §H27zG — it takes TWO predecessors. No single config does it.

Same config measured 17 ways; only what ran BEFORE it changed.

    baseline   0 predecessors   713.45
    cum1       1 predecessor    714.52     <- still clean
    cum2       2 predecessors   656.42     <- -8.0%
    cum3..cum8 3..8             645.89 - 660.70
    pair0..pair7  each single predecessor alone   713.14 - 714.03   <- ALL clean

**INSTRUMENT VALIDATION, free:** `cum1` and `pair0` are the same arm measured twice — 714.52 vs
713.72, agreeing to **0.1%**. The drop is 60x that. It is not noise.

So: **1 predecessor is safe, 2 is not**, no individual config is responsible, and the effect
spares some configs entirely (B at position 9). Mechanism NOT identified — there is no
`cudaMalloc` anywhere in the SM90 sources, so the obvious "split-K workspace" theory is dead.
**Parked as unexplained.** The design does not need the mechanism: measuring one config per
process avoids it by construction.

### §H27zI — THE DEFINITIVE MATRIX. 17 configs x 15 shapes, ONE CONFIG PER PROCESS. One win, eight ties, six pins already best.

Design, with the reason for each choice:

- **one config per process** — the only context that reproduced (six arms within 0.1% in §H27zF)
- **a null control** — after each shape, the pin is re-measured in a fresh process. pin(main) vs
  pin(null) IS the run's noise floor, measured rather than assumed
- **the decision rule written before any data existed** — a candidate must beat the pin by more
  than 2x the 95th-percentile null, floored at 0.5%. Anything less prints as a TIE and the pin
  stands. This rule is what §H27zE lacked
- **rotated shape order per rep**, so drift shows up as spread instead of favouring one shape
- **clock re-locked per invocation, sampled during it, recorded per row**; out-of-band rows dropped

**RESULT (rep 1, 270 measurements). Floor: 15 null pairs, median 0.18%, 95th pct 0.30% ->
threshold 0.60%. Two rows dropped by the clock gate (1613, 1588 MHz).**

    1 genuine WIN, 8 ties, 6 shapes where the pin is already best.

**THE THREE PHANTOM GAINS, RE-MEASURED PROPERLY:**

| shape | §H27zE claimed | §H27zI measured |
|---|---|---|
| 2048x2048x16384 | +10.28% | **+0.13% — tie** |
| 5632x2048x16384 | +6.49% | **+0.13% — tie** |
| 2048x50304x16384 | +9.82% | **the pin is BEST** |

Cross-check: §H27zF measured that pin alone at 713.24 on GPU 3; §H27zI got 713.82 on GPU 1 —
**0.08% apart on a different card.**

**TWO SIDE FINDINGS.** (1) `128x256x64_2x1_h_ep64swz128_pdl` and `..._swz64_pdl` — the variants
WITHOUT `rot2` — sit at or near the top on most shapes and had never been pinned anywhere. All
ties except V6. (2) On `2048x512x16384` (N=512) the 128x256 configs collapse to **179 TFLOPS**
against 605 for 128x128 — a 256-wide tile on N=512 is mostly wasted. Correctly caught rather than
shipped.

### §H27zJ — V6 CONFIRMED and PIN_BEST introduced. V6 crosses cuBLAS: 98.8% -> 100.8%.

The one win from §H27zI, re-run on V6's shape alone: 4 configs x 6 rounds, INTERLEAVED (round 1
runs all four, then round 2, ...) so drift moves all four together instead of favouring the first.
The pin is measured 6 times exactly like the candidates, so its own spread is the floor.

| config | median | %cuB | spread | vs pin | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`128x256x64_2x1_h_ep64swz128_pdl`** | **664.33** | **100.8%** | 0.36% | **+1.97%** | **CONFIRMED WIN** |
| `128x256x64_2x1_h_ep64swz128_rot2_pdl` | 663.85 | 100.7% | 1.40% | +1.89% | WIN |
| `128x256x64_2x1_h_swz64_pdl` | 660.43 | 100.1% | 0.14% | +1.37% | WIN |
| `192x192x64_2x1_h_rs8_dh_ubd_dw_skew_lsw_pdl_wlsm` | 651.50 | 98.8% | 0.18% | — | current pin |

Floor 0.18%, threshold 0.50%, win **+1.97% = 4x the floor**. Reproduced across two independent
runs: §H27zI 664.00/650.60, §H27zJ 664.33/651.50 — **0.14% apart**.

**V6 WAS ONE OF ONLY THREE SHAPES BELOW PARITY. IT IS NOW ABOVE IT.**

**PIN_MATCH vs PIN_BEST — the two jobs one field was doing.** `PIN[]` is the apples-to-apples
pin: it structurally matches what cuBLAS launches, so a comparison measures OUR CODE and not a
difference of tile shape. It must never change because something benchmarks faster — a slower
structural match is a finding. `PIN_BEST[]` is what should SHIP; it is free to be a different
structure because the dispatcher only has to be fast and correct. For V6 they now differ: cuBLAS
runs 192x192 so the match stays 192x192, while the dispatcher gets the 128x256. Every other shape
has `PIN_BEST == PIN`. Added to `tools/pins.sh`; existing scripts read `PIN[]` and are unaffected.

**Measured on GPU 1 of fine-mind-thinks-fin-02, locked 1400, every row 1410. A card change voids
the absolute figures.**

### §H27zE-BUILD — the compiler has been telling us the wgmma pipeline is serialized, in every build log, and nobody read it.

`make` emits, on a full build:

| | count | |
|---|---|---|
| **C7517** | 351 | `wgmma.wait_group is injected by compiler to allow use of registers defined by GMMA` |
| **C7515** | 6 | **"Potential Performance Loss"** — non-wgmma instructions define accumulator registers between the start and end of a pipeline stage, **serializing wgmma** |
| **C7519** | 3 | **"Potential Performance Loss"** — divergent path creates a dependence on a compiler-inserted `WG.AR`, again serializing wgmma |

**C7517 BY TILE FAMILY — and the correlation is uncomfortable:**

| tile | injected waits | variants | best %cuB |
|---|---|---|---|
| 192x192 | **168** | V3 V4 V5 V6 | 99.27 – 100.54 |
| 256x128 | 9 | V2 | 100.63 |
| **128x128** | **0** | V1 | **105.19** |
| **128x256** | **0** | V7 V8 | 99.01 – 101.06 |

45 warned configs have `PDL=true`, and among them are the exact parameter sets of the **V3/V4, V5
and V6 pins**. This is live shipping code.

Why it matters is recorded in our own source, at template:4956 (§H27zt's bisection):

    WROT=0                     0 warnings   1 DEPBAR
    WROT=1/2, guard as it was  1 warning    3 DEPBAR    <- the documented kill
    WROT=1/2, guard removed    0 warnings   2 DEPBAR

**A C7517 warning means EXTRA DEPBARs.** §H27zA measured V6's one remaining lever as
"BAR.SYNC 4 vs 2, +4.54 barrier stall". These may be the same thing. `drain_prev`, `skew_body`
and the `WROT==0` branch were all checked and their waits are already unconditional, so §H27zt's
fix is applied there — the trigger is elsewhere and was NOT identified. **Open lead, not a
conclusion.** Note the correlation is not proof: 192x192 also has by far the most registered
variants.

The C7515/C7519 nine are all `192x192 cluster 1x2` and **none has `PDL=true`**, so no shipping pin
is affected. One carries `_KLOOP_UNROLL=true` — a candidate explanation for §H27zdy's
"SASS target met, wall clock null": a divergent path serializing wgmma would cancel the gain.

**TWO DEAD THINGS REMOVED.** `--full-verify` was parsed, stored and **never read** — the switch
did nothing (verification already covers every element on the GPU, so nothing was unchecked, but
the flag was a lie). Deleted. `prev_stage` warns as unused but **is live at template:4974 and
:5389 for `WROT != 0`**; it is now `[[maybe_unused]]`, matching `head_stage` on the next line —
deleting it would have broken the rotation path.

§H27zI ran n=1, so the four shapes where the PIN DID NOT COME FIRST were re-measured on the §H27zJ
instrument (one config per process, candidates interleaved with the pin round by round, the pin's
own spread across rounds used as the floor). Candidates taken from the §H27zI ranking, not hardcoded.

| shape | pin spread | threshold | best challenger | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 `2048x512x16384` | **0.50%** | 0.99% | depth 7, +0.12% | **tie** |
| V2b `5632x2048x16384` | 0.11% | 0.50% | `128x256..._ep64swz128_pdl`, +0.26% | **tie** |
| V3 `16384x11264x2048` | 0.10% | 0.50% | — **pin is best** | **pin stays** |
| V8d `16384x2048x50304` | 0.17% | 0.50% | +0.02% | **tie** |

**0 confirmed wins across the four.**

**V1 WAS THE STRONGEST SUSPICION AND IT WAS WRONG — because V1 IS A NOISY SHAPE.** Its pin spread
is **0.50%**, three to five times every other shape here (0.10-0.17%). That is what produced the
+0.56% near-miss in §H27zI: a single-shot fluctuation on the noisiest shape we have. Record this —
V1 needs more rounds than the others before any V1 claim is believable.

**DEPTH 6 vs DEPTH 7 IS NOW CONFIRMED A TIE THREE INDEPENDENT TIMES:** §H27zC +0.12 favouring 6,
§H27zI +0.56 favouring 7, §H27zK +0.12 favouring 7 — all inside their own floors. Depth 6 stays on
the apples-to-apples rule (cuBLAS runs `64x6`), not on speed.

**V3 WAS A V6 LOOKALIKE AND ISN'T ONE.** In §H27zI the 128x256 family took the top two slots above
a 192x192 pin -- exactly V6's signature, which turned out to be a real +1.97%. Re-measured, the
same family lands BEHIND the pin (-0.10%, -0.17%). The signature is not sufficient; only the
measurement decides.

**MARGINAL CASE ON RECORD, DELIBERATELY NOT ACTED ON.** On V2b all four challengers beat the pin
consistently by 0.16-0.26%, each with a spread of 0.02-0.07% against a pin spread of 0.11%. The
consistency suggests a real but tiny effect. It is below the 0.50% threshold that was fixed BEFORE
the data existed, so it is a tie and the pin stands. Lowering the bar after seeing the numbers is
the exact failure this campaign was built to prevent. Revisit with more rounds only if 0.26% ever
matters.

**Also captured:** on `2048x512x16384` (N=512) the 128x256 configs measure **179.72 TFLOPS,
31.2% of cuBLAS** -- a 256-wide tile on N=512 wastes most of the work. The sweep found it instead
of the dispatcher shipping it.

### §H27zE-to-K SUMMARY — what the whole cross-comparison campaign concluded.

**15 shapes x 17 registered `_pdl` variants, every measurement one-config-per-process.**

1. **cuBLAS launches the kernel we assumed on all 15 shapes (15/15).** The apples-to-apples
   pairing of §H27zzj-C is verified rather than assumed, and §H27zzj-B is independently confirmed.
2. **EXACTLY ONE PIN WAS WRONG.** V6 -> `128x256x64_2x1_h_ep64swz128_pdl`, +1.97%, crossing parity
   98.8% -> 100.8%. The other 14 are correct: 6 already best, 8 ties inside their measured floors.
3. **`PIN_MATCH` / `PIN_BEST` split added to `tools/pins.sh`.** `PIN[]` keeps the structural match
   to cuBLAS for diagnosis and must never move for speed; `PIN_BEST[]` is what ships. V6 is the
   only shape where they differ.
4. **A measurement bug was found, quantified and designed out.** Passing many configs to one
   process deflates SOME of them 6-8% while sparing others (>=2 predecessors triggers it; the
   mechanism is still unidentified and there is no `cudaMalloc` in the SM90 sources to blame). It
   invented "+10.28% better than the pin" and reproduced it exactly twice. One config per process
   avoids it by construction.
5. **Repeating a measurement does not make it correct.** The phantom gain was stable to two
   decimal places across independent runs. Only a controlled experiment that varied the CONTEXT
   exposed it. Reproducibility answers "is it noisy", never "is it biased".
6. **State the decision rule before the data exists.** Every number in §H27zI/J/K is judged
   against a floor the run measured on itself, with the bar fixed in advance. That rule is the
   only reason the V2b +0.26% is recorded as a tie instead of a fifth pin change.

### §H27zL — C7517 EXPLAINED AND CLOSED: WGMMA_SKEW is the sole trigger, and skew PAYS FOR ITSELF. Keep it. §H27zbC's "does not pay yet" is corrected.

**THE TRIGGER, PROVEN BY KNOB BISECT** (local nvcc 13.0, sm_90a, no GPU needed):

| arm | C7517 | C7515 | C7519 | DEPBAR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 192x192 pin as shipped | 2 | 0 | 4 | 7 |
| **same, SKEW off** | **0** | **0** | **0** | **3** |
| same, DESC_HOIST off | 2 | 0 | 4 | 7 |
| same, UNIFORM_B_DESC off | 2 | 0 | 2 | 7 |
| same, EPI_LATE_STORE_WAIT off | 2 | 0 | 4 | 7 |
| 128x256 pin | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| **128x256 + SKEW** | — | — | — | **WILL NOT COMPILE** |

`WGMMA_SKEW` is the **sole** trigger. Every other knob flipped off still warns; skew off is clean.
Reproduced on all three 192x192 pins: DEPBAR **7->3** (V3/V4) and **15->11** (V5, V6), C7517 2->0
and C7519 4->0 in every case.

**AND IT EXPLAINS THE TILE CORRELATION THAT LOOKED SO DAMNING.** 128x256 with skew fails a
static_assert: *"WGMMA_SKEW needs >= 2 m64 atoms per warpgroup: it carries atom 0 to the next pass
and issues the rest on acquire, so MAX_ATOMS==1 has nothing to split (192x192 has 3; a SPLIT_M
128x256 has 1)"*. **128x128 and 128x256 show zero warnings because they CANNOT use skew, not
because they are better.** §H27zE-BUILD's "192x192 has 168 warnings and is our weakest family"
correlation is fully explained and carries no further information.

**WHY IT HAPPENS.** Skew splits the wgmma issue across the loop back-edge -- atom 0 of a stage is
issued one pass LATER than atoms 1..N, deliberately, to copy cuBLAS. That produces a peel, a body
and a tail, so the accumulators are reached from several paths. Our waits are correct on each, but
ptxas cannot PROVE one dominates them all, so it inserts its own.

**PRECISION IS NOT AT RISK, AND THE INJECTED WAIT IS WHY.** Without it the accumulators would be
read before the wgmma retired. ptxas is protecting correctness, not damaging it. Every row across
§H27zE/I/J/K -- 135 + 270 + 102 measurements -- came back `maxRelErr 0.00000`. This was only ever a
performance question.

**THE A/B: SKEW WINS. REMOVING IT COSTS US.** Three skew-off twins added, each identical to its pin
in every template slot except `/*SKEW=*/`. Measured on the §H27zJ instrument (one config per
process, arms interleaved round by round, the pin's own spread as the floor), GPU 1, locked 1400:

| shape | skew | no-skew | delta of REMOVING skew | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V3 `16384x11264x2048` | 672.09 | 668.36 | **-0.55%** | SKEW WINS |
| V4 `16384x50304x2048` | 688.13 | 686.45 | -0.24% | tie |
| V5 `2048x11264x16384` | 708.66 | 707.55 | -0.16% | tie |
| V6 `16384x5632x2048` | 651.40 | 643.87 | **-1.16%** | SKEW WINS |

**Mean -0.53%.** Two shapes lose clearly, two are neutral, none gains. **The 4 extra DEPBARs and
the compiler-injected waits are a price skew is earning.** KEEP SKEW.

**§H27zbC-RESULT IS CORRECTED.** It was titled *"THE MECHANISM IS PROVEN, THE IMPLEMENTATION DOES
NOT PAY YET"* and measured V3 at **-0.78%, skew WORSE**. On a clean instrument V3 now shows skew
**+0.55% BETTER** -- the sign flipped. That measurement predates the 400 ms window (§H27zdt-b) and
one-config-per-process (§H27zF). Skew's value is established here for the first time.

**CAVEAT ON RECORD:** V6's no-skew arm spread **1.58%**, ten times its skew arm (0.15%). The
direction agrees with V3 but V6's magnitude is the least trustworthy number in that table.

**WHAT REMAINS, PARKED.** The warnings stay, and are now known to be the cost of a knob worth
keeping. The open opportunity is the §H27zt fix applied to skew: keep the mechanism but restructure
so ptxas can prove our wait dominates every path, removing the injected waits for free. `drain_prev`,
`skew_body` and the `WROT==0` branch were all checked and their waits are ALREADY unconditional, so
the un-provable path is elsewhere -- most likely the peel/tail structure, where the k-loop may not
execute at all. A real investigation, not a quick win.

**TOOLING NOTE.** `-DBLUBLAS_SM90_FAST_BUILD` builds this experiment in ~5 min instead of ~1 h: the
pins and twins live in the `_SPLITK` list, which FAST_BUILD does not gate, so nothing needs adding
to the FAST list -- and adding them there produces "function has already been defined" for every
one. Never sweep or ship with that binary.

**AND §H27zA-BUG BIT AGAIN, IN A SCRIPT WRITTEN THE SAME DAY IT WAS DOCUMENTED.**
`strings "$BIN" | grep -qF "$c"` under `set -o pipefail` **rejects the config BECAUSE it was
found**: grep -q exits on the first match, strings takes SIGPIPE, pipefail makes the pipeline
non-zero, the `||` fires. It is a RACE -- it did not reproduce locally on 20,000 lines, and it
failed reliably against a 1327-kernel binary where `strings` is slow. Snapshot once into a variable
and match with a herestring; never pipe into `grep -q` under pipefail.

### §H27zM-VALIDATED — the re-pinned dispatcher passes end to end through the real entry points. Median 100.0% of cuBLAS, 8 of 15 above parity, at a verified lock.

Run through `blublasBgemmSM90_dispatch_{nn,nt,tn}` -- the public API BluTrain uses -- not per-config
test symbols. `examples/test_bgemm_sm90_dispatch_validate.cu` checks two independent claims:
**correctness** against cuBLAS, and **selection** (does the throughput match the config the table
NAMES). A table can hold the perfect answer while the lookup is wrong -- an off-by-one in the
binary search, an enum drifted from the switch, a silent miss into the tree -- and a
correctness-only test cannot see any of it, because the fallback still computes the right answer.

**FIRST ATTEMPT WAS RUN AT FREE CLOCK AND PROVED NOTHING ABOUT SELECTION.** Every `gotTF` came back
far above its `expectTF` (V1 686.8 vs 602.9) purely from boost, and the run reported a flattering
105.0% median with 14 of 15 beating cuBLAS. Work it through: the old V1 config at free clock would
read 542.3 x 1.14 = 617.9, still ABOVE the 584.8 tolerance floor -- **a wrong pick would have
passed.** "0 SLOW" meant nothing; the clock had already cleared the bar. The correctness half was
unaffected.

**RE-RUN AT A VERIFIED 1410 MHz LOCK -- the expectations were measured under exactly that
condition, so `gotTF` must now equal `expectTF`:**

| V2 `2048x2048x16384` tn | 713.7 | 713.3 | −0.06% | 100.3 |
| V2b `5632x2048x16384` tn | 659.0 | 661.2 | +0.33% | 100.0 |
| V2c `2048x50304x16384` tn (incumbent kept) | 736.2 | 743.0 | +0.92% | 100.2 |
| V3 `16384x11264x2048` nn | 672.2 | 671.9 | −0.04% | 99.8 |
| V4 `16384x50304x2048` nn | 688.4 | 688.1 | −0.04% | 99.9 |

### §H27zO — BLUTRAIN PORT AND THE 1.7B MEASUREMENT. GEMM 80.8% -> 96.6%. Two causes found and fixed, one real gap left that is NOT explained by anything we have tested.

> **SUPERSEDED IN PART BY §H27zW — read that first.** The "one real gap left that is NOT
> explained" IS now explained, and one claim below is wrong:
>
> - The residual gap was the **per-kernel sum double-counting our own stream overlap**. Measured
>   by sum-vs-union: 521 ms of our GEMM time runs concurrently, cuBLAS hides exactly 0.0 ms. Over
>   the whole run at locked 1400 we are **99.8%** of cuBLAS, not 96.6%.
> - **CAUSE 2 below ("nn/nt are CLOCK-LIMITED") is REFUTED.** At free clocks cuBLAS averages
>   1948 MHz and we average 1942 MHz -- 6 MHz apart -- and we draw LESS power (647 W vs 673 W).
>   We are not clock-starved and not power-capped; we stall more. The free-clock loss is real
>   (-1.57% tok/s) but it is a stall problem, not a clock or power problem.
> - The two-stream finding below is CONFIRMED and strengthened: cuBLAS's 0.0 ms hidden time proves
>   single-stream directly rather than by grep.

#### The port

BluTrain builds a SECOND, vendored copy of our library at
`BluTrain/Tensor-Implementations/BluBridge-BLAS/` (`BLAS_DIR := BluBridge-BLAS` in the tensor
Makefile). **Our top-level `src/` is never compiled into the trainer.** The port was 5 files plus
one Makefile line; `include/` was already identical:

| file | diff lines |
|---|---|
| `Bgemm_sm90_warpspecialized_template.cuh` | 3662 |
| `Bgemm_sm90_bf16.cuh` | 310 |
| `Bgemm_sm90_dispatch_table.h` | 51 |
| `Splitk_reduce.cuh` | 44 |
| `Bgemm_sm90_dispatcher.cu` | 7 |

`tools/verify_blutrain_wiring.sh` passes 20/20 after fixing two of ITS OWN stale assertions: the
table-entry count (423 -> 437, already failing before the port) and an exact tracked-file count that
only ever grows (now a floor). Full BluTrain build: **10m02s** measured -- the "~1 hour" quoted
repeatedly earlier in the day was never measured and was wrong.

#### Identity: 21/21 call sites verified

Every call site issues the config we pinned, and cuBLAS issues the kernel our §H27zE identity gate
recorded standalone. **The apples-to-apples pairing holds in the real trainer, not just on the
bench.** Total GEMM launches 34,720 in both backends -- identical work.

**THE AUGUST HEADLINE DEFICIT IS GONE.** `gate_up-fwd` (16384x11264x2048) was **75.0%** of cuBLAS
and "alone 34% of the deficit" because `tree_nn` returned 128x128. It now gets the pinned 192x192
and reads **98.3-99.8%**.

#### CAUSE 1 -- the backward pass runs on TWO streams and the per-kernel comparison never accounted for it

nsys, grouped by stream:

    ours    stream 7: 26,040 launches 8,880.5 ms | stream 16: 8,680 launches 3,199.0 ms
    cuBLAS  stream 7: 34,720 launches 11,248.3 ms   (ONE stream)

**8,680 is exactly the wgrad call sites** (1440x6 + 40). `MatmulBackward.cu` puts grad_B on a
secondary stream under `WITH_MYBLAS` so it overlaps grad_A; the cuBLAS branch serialises. So OUR
kernels were timed while sharing SMs and cuBLAS's never were.

Added `BLUTRAIN_BWD_SINGLE_STREAM=1`, **default OFF** (production keeps the overlap -- it is a real
wall-clock win). Worth **180 ms** of the 831 ms gap: 12,079.5 -> 11,899.3 ms, 93.1% -> 94.5%.

**MY ATTRIBUTION WAS WRONG AND THE DATA CORRECTED IT.** I predicted the contention penalised the
wgrad kernels. It penalised the **dgrad** kernels -- they run on the PRIMARY stream and were having
SMs stolen by the secondary-stream wgrad: `wV-dgrad` 65.2 -> 89.5 (+24.3), `lm_head-wgrad`
82.7 -> 95.5, `wQ-dgrad` 92.7 -> 97.6. The wgrad sites barely moved.

**ALSO FOUND: `mpirun` forwards ONLY what `-x` names.** `BLUBLAS_SM90_TRACE` and
`BLUBLAS_SM90_DISABLE` -- both documented as working debug switches -- were never in that list, so
setting them did nothing and would have read as "the switch has no effect". Now forwarded via
`MPI_FORWARD_ENV`.

#### CAUSE 2 -- nn/nt are CLOCK-LIMITED, and the bench ran locked while training runs free

Comparing the same shape+config on the bench (locked 1410) against training (free clock), BOTH
libraries speed up, but not equally:

| layout | our gain | cuBLAS gain | points we lose |
|---|---|---|---|
| nn | +16.1% | +22.5% | −5.1 |
| nt | +15.8% | +21.6% | −4.6 |
| **tn** | **+3.4%** | **+21.1%** | **−14.7** |

Three tn sites go BACKWARDS with more clock: `wV-wgrad` −0.2%, `wK-wgrad` −0.4%,
`gate_up-wgrad` −0.6%, while cuBLAS gains +13 to +32% on the same shapes. V1 was our BEST shape at
105.1% on the bench and reads **79.3%** in training -- not because we slowed (602 vs 603.5 TFLOPS,
identical) but because **cuBLAS went 574 -> 759**.

**Locking the training clock to 1400 CONFIRMED this for nn/nt and REFUTED it for tn:**

| site | free | locked | standalone |
|---|---|---|---|
| lm_head-dgrad nt | 88.2 | **99.8** | 100.1 |
| down-fwd nn | 91.6 | **98.8** | 99.7 |
| wQ-fwd nn | 92.4 | **97.3** | 99.5 |
| gate_up-wgrad tn | 88.1 | **88.6** | 100.3 |
| wQ-wgrad tn | 85.7 | **87.1** | 100.3 |
| wV-wgrad tn | 79.2 | **83.2** | **105.1** |

**At a held 1400: ours 96.6% of cuBLAS, 474 ms lost. nn 98.2%, nt 97.1%, tn 89.2%.**
nn and nt now match their standalone numbers within ~2 points. **tn does not.**

#### THE OPEN PROBLEM -- tn is 6 to 21 points worse in training than on the bench, at the SAME clock

**78% of the remaining 474 ms is tn/wgrad** (368 ms); `gate_up-wgrad` alone is 41.8%.

RULED OUT, each by measurement, not argument:
- **clock** -- persists at a held 1400
- **beta** -- all 34,720 cuBLAS launches are the `_bz` beta-zero kernel, so beta==0 everywhere
- **stream concurrency** -- persists with a single stream
- **wrong kernel** -- 21/21 sites verified issuing the pinned config
- **the cluster/raster mismatch** -- our `1x2_v` vs cuBLAS's `2x1_v` on `gate_up-wgrad` is REAL and
  violates the §H27z.86 swap rule, but it is IDENTICAL in the standalone run that measured 100.3%.
  **A constant cannot explain a difference.** It may still be worth absolute points; it is not the
  explanation for this gap, and it must not be recorded as one.

STILL LIVE:
- **L2 residency.** Our harness runs ~2000 back-to-back iterations on the SAME buffers; training
  touches fresh activations every call. These are precisely the high-K, small-output shapes where
  reuse would matter most. **The one tn site that DOES match is `lm_head-wgrad` at 99.8%** -- by far
  the largest (N=50304, 4552 us), too big for L2 reuse to help either library. That exception fits
  the L2 story and fits nothing else we have.
- strides / alignment of the trainer's tensors versus our freshly-allocated benchmark buffers.

**CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CAMPAIGN, and it is uncomfortable: every locked-clock tn number we have
quoted is optimistic.** The whole step-3 campaign measured at 1200-1400 locked, which is correct
for isolating kernel work but hides a ceiling production actually hits. A tn "100% of cuBLAS" on
the bench is 83-94% in the trainer at the same clock.

**Measured on GPU 3 of fine-mind-thinks-fin-02. Free-clock and locked-1400 captures both retained:
`nsys_blublas_repin`, `nsys_blublas_1stream`, `nsys_blublas_1stream_lock`, `nsys_cublas_repin`,
`nsys_cublas_lock`. The August baseline in `nsys_train_blublas/` was deliberately NOT overwritten.**

### §H27zW-FUTURE — PDL ON THE REMAINING BluTrain KERNELS. Parked as a future task, with the numbers that justify revisiting it.

**THE TASK.** Add PDL (the launch attribute + `griddep_wait` consumer half, and the `PREEXIT`
producer hint) to BluTrain's own kernels — `convert_type_kernel`, `gqa_v62` /
`gqa_backward_v26_kv`, `rms_norm_*`, `swiglu_*`, `add_kernel` / `add_inplace_kernel`,
`generic_strided_copy_kernel` — and measure whether the launch chain reconnects.

**WHY IT IS PARKED AND NOT CLOSED.** PDL is a property of the PAIR of consecutive launches
(§H27zv-D). Today only our 15 pinned GEMM configs opt in. Our GEMM is 37.62% of trainer GPU
time; its neighbours are BluTrain's own kernels at 62.38% across 128,843 launches, and none of
them opt in. So nearly every boundary in the real training loop is broken and PDL collects
almost nothing:

    where                       PDL's real gain
    standalone bench            +0.93% mean over 15 pins (V1 +6.25 is the outlier)
    trainer, whole run          +20.6 ms of 36,355.7 ms busy  =  0.06%

    union-vs-sum, day2 captures
      PDL ON    sum 36,716.3 ms   union 36,335.1 ms   overlap 381.2 ms
      PDL OFF   sum 36,355.7 ms   union 36,355.7 ms   overlap   0.0 ms

The bench earns +0.93% because its loop runs the SAME kernel back to back, so every boundary is
ours→ours. The trainer earns 0.06% because almost every boundary is ours→theirs.

**THE 381 ms IS NOT A SAVING, IT IS SPAN INFLATION.** PDL-on blocks launch early and then block
on `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()`, so launch-to-completion grows while the work does not. It
inflates the per-kernel SUM by 381.2 ms while the real wall-clock saving is 20.6 ms. That
inflation lands on dgrad and is the whole reason the trainer read 96.5% instead of 99.0%.

**WHY THE 0.06% IS A LOWER BOUND, NOT A VERDICT.** It was measured under nsys, where the GPU is
heavily idled by profiling overhead and kernels are spread apart — precisely the gaps PDL would
otherwise fill. A profiled run therefore CANNOT show PDL's production ceiling. Do not conclude
from it that PDL-everywhere is worthless. The decisive experiment is unprofiled end-to-end
tok/s with PDL on vs off.

**IF IT IS ATTEMPTED, REMEMBER THE beta GATE.** `beta != 0.0f` is first in a short-circuiting
`&&` (template:5465), so at `beta == 0` the epilogue's `C_in` read — the second global read of
prior-grid-written data, and the one branch PDL can actually break — never executes. Any PDL
correctness gate must run at `beta != 0` (§H27zv-D).

### §H27zW — THE PAIRED TRAINER CAPTURE. Locked 1400 we are **99.8%** of cuBLAS over the whole run; free clocks we are **98.4%**. The per-kernel sum was charging us 521 ms of our own overlap, and TWO of my earlier conclusions were wrong.

> **TWO NUMBERS BELOW ARE WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED IN §H27zX. Do not quote either of them.**
>
> - **The dgrad/wgrad split is wrong.** `tools/h27zW_sites.py` paired the two captures by kernel
>   START TIME. Our arm interleaves two CUDA streams and cuBLAS uses one, so the backward region
>   misaligns and the dgrad and wgrad rows were effectively SWAPPED. Re-pairing on
>   `correlationId` (launch order) gives **100.0000%** layout agreement on all four captures.
>   With multistream ON the correct values are **dgrad 91.8% locked / 88.5% free** and
>   **wgrad 94.6% locked / 92.6% free** — not the 87.7 / 84.6 written below. Forward is
>   unaffected: it is single-stream and block-contiguous in both arms.
> - **The locked cuBLAS clock summary is contaminated.** The run log for that phase
>   (`profiling_reports/h27zW/locked_1400/output.md`) prints `min 0 / mean 1353 / max 1410 MHz
>   (25 samples, 595 W)` for the locked cuBLAS arm. **That never happened.** An orphaned clock
>   sampler from an earlier failed run kept appending to
>   `h27zW/locked_1400/clk_cublas.csv` (2826 lines, mixing 345 / 450 / 855 / 900 and
>   1875–1980 MHz rows plus a torn `14101410` row). Filtering to well-formed rows with
>   utilization > 50% and memory > 1000 MiB gives **1410 / 1410 / 1410 MHz, 449 W mean**.
>   **The lock DID hold.** The other seven CSVs of the two campaigns are clean (91–98 lines).
>
> The sum-vs-union finding, the tok/s tie at locked clocks, the free-clock loss and the
> single-stream-cuBLAS proof below are all unaffected and stand.

`weak-word-closes-fin-03`, GPU 3, all four GPUs idle, `bluscript_config_profile.yaml`
(36 layers, 10 steps, grad_accum 4 -> 40 fwd/bwd passes, 34,720 GEMM launches). PDL OFF in every
BluBLAS arm. Secondary backward stream ON (production default). Both arms of each phase captured
back to back by `tools/h27zW_pair_nopdl.sh`, cuBLAS first.

#### WHY A NEW CAPTURE WAS NEEDED — none of the three day2 arms was both clean AND comparable

    day2_blublas        PDL ON   -> spans inflated; the inflation lands on dgrad
    day2_blublas_nopdl  PDL OFF  -> but BLUBLAS_SM90_TRACE=1, i.e. 34,720 host printf lines
                                    interleaved with the launch stream
    day2_cublas         clean, but its only clean partner was the PDL-ON arm

day2 also ran while GPUs 0 and 1 were at 100% for someone else, so it is not comparable to
anything measured on an idle box (23,402 tok/s there vs 27,353 here at free clocks).

#### THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT — sum vs union

`sum` adds every kernel's start-to-end. `union` merges the intervals, so concurrent work is
counted once. The difference IS the overlap.

    locked 1400        GEMM sum    GEMM union    hidden
      ours              13919.8      13398.4     521.3 ms
      cuBLAS            13325.9      13325.9       0.0 ms   <- single stream, proven not assumed
      gap  sum           +593.9  ->  95.7%
      gap  union          +72.6  ->  99.5%
      gap  WHOLE RUN      +73.6  ->  99.8%

    free clocks
      ours              12094.7      11628.0     466.7 ms
      cuBLAS            11241.3      11241.3       0.0 ms
      gap  sum           +853.4  ->  92.9%
      gap  union         +386.7  ->  96.7%
      gap  WHOLE RUN     +510.6  ->  98.4%

**cuBLAS hides exactly 0.0 ms.** That is the proof that its 34,720 launches are on one stream and
ours are not -- not an inference from grep, a measurement. Of our 594 ms locked "deficit",
**521 ms is our own overlap being double-counted and 73 ms is real.**

Cross-check, free: union says we lose 1.65% of the run, tok/s says 1.57%. Two independent
measurements agreeing to within a tenth of a point.

#### TWO CORRECTIONS TO WHAT I SAID EARLIER

**1. "PDL off lifts dgrad to 98-100%" was WRONG.** That came from `day2_blublas_nopdl`, which had
tracing on. The trace printf serialises the host and spreads the launches apart, which suppressed
the very stream overlap that penalises dgrad -- so dgrad looked clean for the wrong reason. With
PDL genuinely off and no trace, dgrad is still down with the secondary stream ON.

**~~dgrad reads 87.7% locked / 84.6% free, and `wQ-dgrad` 75.1%.~~ RETRACTED — those came from
start-time pairing, which swaps dgrad and wgrad (§H27zX).** Re-paired on `correlationId`, the same
two captures read **dgrad 91.8% locked / 88.5% free**, **wgrad 94.6% locked / 92.6% free**, and
**`wQ-dgrad/wO-dgrad` 89.4% locked**. And with the secondary stream turned OFF entirely the whole
effect disappears: **dgrad 100.0%, wgrad 99.0% at locked 1400** (§H27zX). So the residual dgrad
deficit under PDL-off is not a PDL artefact and not a kernel deficiency — it is SM contention from
our own two-stream overlap, and the correction to make to point 1 above is that the trace printf
suppressed the overlap, which is exactly the mechanism, just measured on the wrong rows.

**2. "We are +0.22% faster at locked clocks" was an artefact of one bad cuBLAS step.**

    cuBLAS  23397 23407 23384 23340 23387 23380  23034  23364   <- one outlier
    ours    23389 23392 23397 23389 23388 23393  23388  23373

Drop the outlier and cuBLAS averages 23,380 against our 23,389. It is a **TIE**, which is what the
union also says (we are 0.2% behind). Not a win.

#### FORWARD IS CLEAN AND IS ALREADY ANSWERED

The secondary stream carries wgrad only, so the forward sites never share with it:

                     locked   free
    fwd overall       98.7%   95.8%
      gate_up-fwd      99.5    98.2
      down-fwd         98.5    92.7     <- real, and nothing to do with streams or PDL
      wQ-fwd/wO-fwd    96.7    92.5

#### FREE CLOCKS: NOT A CLOCK DEFICIT, AND NOT A POWER CAP

    clock while busy   cuBLAS 1948 MHz    ours 1942 MHz      6 MHz apart
    power              cuBLAS  673 W      ours  647 W        we draw LESS
    tok/s              cuBLAS 27,788      ours 27,353        -1.57%, ranges do not overlap

**AND THE LOCKED PHASE OF THIS SAME CAMPAIGN HELD ITS LOCK, contrary to what its own run log says.**
The locked cuBLAS clock CSV was contaminated by an orphaned sampler (see the banner at the top of
this section and §H27zX). Cleaned: **1410 / 1410 / 1410 MHz at 449 W mean** for cuBLAS and
**1410 / 1410 / 1410 MHz at 430 W mean** for us. There was no dip to 1353 MHz and no 595 W arm.

**CAREFUL -- THIS DOES NOT REFUTE THE PARKED POWER/CLOCK TRACK, AND I SHOULD NOT HAVE SAID IT DID.**
The numbers above are `nvidia-smi` **device-level** samples taken every 2 s across a 285 s run --
9 samples for cuBLAS and 12 for ours. That is far too coarse to resolve a 0.3% clock difference,
and it averages over the whole run, of which our GEMM is only 37.6%. The parked track's figure was
measured on a completely different instrument: **per-kernel** clock via
`nsys --gpu-metrics-devices` on V2, giving ours 1389 MHz vs cuBLAS 1457 MHz (-4.7%).

Both can be true at once -- the device average can match while the clock DURING our GEMM kernels
specifically is lower. A coarse device average cannot arbitrate a per-kernel claim, and treating it
as if it could is exactly the error [[feedback-isolated-measurements-mislead]] warns about.

What the power number DOES support, weakly: neither library is near the 700 W cap (647 W and
673 W), so a hard power ceiling is not obviously what is holding our clock down in THIS
configuration. Drawing less while going slower is consistent with more stalling -- idle units burn
fewer watts -- but at 9-12 samples this is a hint, not a finding.

**THE INSTRUMENT THAT SETTLES IT** is the per-kernel clock, not the device average:
`tools/h27zw_clock_matrix.sh` already captures per-kernel clock + tensor/issue/smact/dram. Run it
on the two worst free-clock sites before drawing any conclusion about clock or power.

What each library gained from the 1400 -> ~1945 MHz change (+39% clock):

    cuBLAS   13325.9 -> 11241.3   = 1.185x   (+18.5%)
    ours     13398.4 -> 11628.0   = 1.152x   (+15.2%)

**Neither approaches 1.39x**, so both are latency/bandwidth-bound -- HBM does not speed up when
the SM clock does. cuBLAS simply tolerates it better. The question for the next step is therefore
narrow: *at 1945 MHz, what are our warps stalled on that cuBLAS's are not?*

#### EVERYTHING ELSE IS IDENTICAL

Total non-GEMM kernel time differs between the two runs by **37.9 ms** out of ~23,000. The matmul
really is the only moving part.

#### SCRIPT TRAPS FOUND BUILDING THIS (all fixed in the tool)

- **`nvcc not found`.** `/root/.bashrc` puts CUDA on PATH but returns early for non-interactive
  shells, so a script launched over ssh/nohup has no toolchain. Same class:
- **`mpirun` refuses to run as root** unless `OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT{,_CONFIRM}` are set. Both
  worked when launched by hand from a shell that already exported them, and failed over ssh.
  **A script that depends on who started it is not a measurement tool.**
- **Placement.** `mpirun` exports only what `-x` names, and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is NOT in the
  Makefile default. Without it the rank silently lands on GPU 0. The tool now asserts peak memory
  on the named GPU and aborts otherwise.
- **Error ordering.** Checking placement before exit code reported "WRONG GPU" for what was really
  a crashed launch -- a failed run has zero memory as a CONSEQUENCE. Exit code is checked first.
- **sqlite detection by glob**, because some nsys builds write `%q{OMPI_COMM_WORLD_RANK}`
  literally and an exact-name check calls a good capture "missing".

### §H27zX — THE SINGLE-STREAM CONTROL. At locked 1400 we are at PARITY (GEMM **99.1%**, whole-run union **99.6%**, tok/s a TIE); at free clocks there is a real, twice-reproduced **1.5%** loss that lives ENTIRELY in the forward `nn` sites; and the dgrad/wgrad deficits were **100% stream contention** — single-stream they read **100.0%** and **99.0%**.

#### SETUP

`weak-word-closes-fin-03`, GPU 3, all four GPUs otherwise idle. `bluscript_config_profile.yaml`:
36 layers, d_model 2048, 16/4 GQA heads, head_dim 128, ffn_hidden 5632 SwiGLU, context 4096,
vocab 50304, B×T = 4×4096, global_batch 65536 with grad_accum 4, 10 steps → 40 fwd/bwd passes.
**34,720 GEMM launches and 173,563 total kernels in EVERY arm** — the workload is identical across
all four captures, only the library and the stream count change.

Two campaigns, both with PDL off (`blublas_NO_PDL=1`):

    h27zW   multistream ON    production default
    h27zX   multistream OFF   BLUTRAIN_BWD_SINGLE_STREAM=1

Each campaign ran two phases, locked 1400 MHz and free clocks. **The cuBLAS arm was measured first
in every case**, because it historically benefits from a cold card (§H27zD) — so any residual order
effect works AGAINST us and cannot manufacture a win for us. Tool: `tools/h27zW_pair_nopdl.sh`.

reported numbers, not separately re-derived — the point is only that **the two filters differ, so
percentages must be read as reported and never recomputed by mixing columns.**

      wQ-wgrad/wO-wgrad     81.5%    97.3%     -15.8 pt
      gate_up-dgrad         86.0%    98.8%     -12.8 pt

**A 15-point per-kernel "deficit" that is created by our own scheduling decision.** Every one of
these rows was previously read as a kernel problem. None of them is.

#### WHAT MULTISTREAM COSTS OUR OWN KERNELS

Our own kernel time, OFF → ON — no cuBLAS in this comparison at all:

    locked    fwd    6797.6 -> 6802.2    +4.6 ms   +0.07%   untouched (fwd is single-stream either way)
              dgrad  3294.2 -> 3590.2  +296.0 ms   +9.0%
              wgrad  3369.4 -> 3527.3  +157.9 ms   +4.7%
    free      fwd    5821.1 -> 5823.9    +2.8 ms   +0.05%
              dgrad  2893.4 -> 3209.9  +316.5 ms  +10.9%
              wgrad  2903.7 -> 3060.9  +157.2 ms   +5.4%

Concurrency makes each backward kernel **genuinely slower** — this is SM contention, not a
measurement artefact; two kernels sharing the SMs each take longer — while overlapping them in
wall clock. The forward rows are the null: +0.07% and +0.05% on the half of the work the change
cannot touch.

**AND THE TRADE DOES NOT PAY.** Net wall clock, our GEMM union: 13,461.2 (OFF) → 13,398.4 (ON) =
**62.8 ms saved** out of 13,461.2. End-to-end: **tok/s +0.42% locked, −0.01% free.** The overlap
earns nothing in production conditions (free clocks are production) while costing ~3.4 points of
apparent per-kernel performance and, until this section, costing us a completely false diagnosis.

    locked            GEMM sum    GEMM union   hidden
      ours (ON)        13919.8     13398.4     521.3 ms
      cuBLAS            13325.9     13325.9       0.0 ms
      ours (OFF)       13461.2     13461.2       0.0 ms
    free
      ours (ON)        12094.7     11628.0     466.7 ms

Stream topology, **measured from `streamId`, not inferred**:

    cuBLAS, all four captures     stream 7 only          34,720 launches
    ours, multistream ON          stream 7  26,040  +  stream 16  8,680
    ours, multistream OFF         stream 7 only          34,720 launches

The 8,680 launches on stream 16 are exactly the wgrad sites, **verified two independent ways**:

1. The `(Sm90Layout)N` template argument (`enum class Sm90Layout { NN, NT, TN }`, so 0 = NN = fwd,
   1 = NT = dgrad, 2 = TN = wgrad) gives **NN 17,360 / NT 8,680 / TN 8,680**, and TN appears on
   stream 16 exclusively — zero fwd and zero dgrad launches there.
2. It matches cuBLAS's NT-layout kernel family count exactly: **5,800 + 2,880 = 8,680**.

**IMPORTANT — cuBLAS's "0.0 ms hidden" is a property of the HARNESS, not of cuBLAS.** The secondary
stream is created only on the `WITH_MYBLAS` path, so the cuBLAS build never gets one. cuBLAS would
overlap too if the trainer handed it two streams. This is not a cuBLAS design choice we are
observing, and §H27zW's "single stream, proven not assumed" should be read as "single stream
*because our harness only ever gives it one*". Corroborated by the cuBLAS arm being essentially
identical across the two campaigns, which is what you expect if the campaign flag does nothing to
it: GEMM sum **13,342.6 vs 13,336.3 locked (0.05%)** and **11,254.1 vs 11,263.8 free (0.09%)**.

(max = default = 700, so nothing is de-rated).

    LOCKED  cuBLAS h27zW   1410   1410   1410      449    469
            ours   h27zW   1410   1410   1410      430    481

**The lock held flat at 1410 in all four locked arms** (min = mean = max), which is what kills the
"1353 MHz / 595 W" line in the h27zW locked run log — see the retraction at the top of §H27zW.

At free clocks cuBLAS runs **10–25 MHz higher (0.5–1.3%)** and draws **19–26 W MORE**. Neither
library is anywhere near the 700 W cap: peaks are 690–695 W but means are 638–674 W.

**We draw LESS power while going SLOWER at effectively the same clock.** That is the signature of
more stalling — idle units burn fewer watts — rather than of a power or governor limit.
**RECORD THIS AS A HYPOTHESIS WITH A MATCHING SIGNATURE, NOT AS PROVEN.** The clock samples are
only 9–12 per arm and are DEVICE-level averages over a run in which our GEMM is 37.6% of GPU time.
A device average cannot arbitrate a per-kernel claim in either direction — that is the same error
[[feedback-isolated-measurements-mislead]] warns about, and it applies to the stalling story just
as much as it applied to the clock story it replaces.

#### CLOCK SCALING PER SITE, OURS vs cuBLAS

Clock went 1410 → ~1950, a factor of **1.383×**. Achieved throughput ratio, free TF ÷ locked TF,
same site, same pin, both libraries:

    down-fwd           ours 1.160x    cuBLAS 1.232x
    wQ-fwd/wO-fwd      ours 1.195x    cuBLAS 1.249x
    gate_up-fwd        ours 1.158x    cuBLAS 1.172x

**Neither library comes close to 1.383×**, so both are bandwidth/latency-bound — HBM does not speed
up when the SM clock does, and 1.16–1.25× out of 1.383× is what that costs. But cuBLAS converts
extra MHz into throughput measurably better on the `nn` forward shapes (+0.072 and +0.054 on the
two worst rows, +0.014 on `gate_up-fwd`), and **that difference IS the free-clock gap** — the same
two sites, ranked the same way, as the per-site table above. The gap is not "we lose at high clock"
in general; it is "these two shapes scale worse than cuBLAS's do".

#### TRAP — THE ANALYSIS SCRIPT'S OWN BUG (this is what broke §H27zW)

`tools/h27zW_sites.py` originally zipped the two arms **by global kernel start time**. With our arm
on two streams and cuBLAS on one, the backward region misaligns:

    pairing by kernel start time     layout signatures agree on   92.70% of positions
    pairing by correlationId         layout signatures agree on  100.0000% of positions

Under the broken pairing the "dgrad" rows held **90.5% true-wgrad** kernels and the "wgrad" rows
held **94.4% true-dgrad** kernels — the two rows were effectively SWAPPED. Forward was unaffected
because it is single-stream and block-contiguous in both arms, which is exactly why the output
looked credible: the half of the table that could be checked against the bench was right.

**A PAIRING THAT PRODUCES PLAUSIBLE NUMBERS IS NOT A VALIDATED PAIRING.** 92.70% agreement is high
enough to look like rounding and low enough to invert a conclusion. The script now prints its own
layout-agreement percentage on every run and refuses to be trusted below 100%.

#### TRAP — ORPHANED CLOCK SAMPLERS

The tool's clock sampler runs as a background subshell. Its `EXIT` trap reset the **clock lock**
only, not the sampler, so an interrupted or failed run leaves the sampler alive and appending to
its CSV. `h27zW/locked_1400/clk_cublas.csv` grew to **2826 lines** mixing an idle section
(345 MHz), the locked section (1410) and a free section (1875–1980), plus a torn row
(`14101410`) from two writers hitting the same line. Reading that run's `output.md` at face value
says the locked cuBLAS arm dipped to a **1353 MHz mean at 595 W**. **It did not.** Filtered to
well-formed rows with utilization > 50% and memory > 1000 MiB it is 1410/1410/1410 at 449 W.

The retained local copy (`profiling_reports/h27zW/locked_1400/clk_cublas.csv`, a partial sync at
1309 lines) shows the same signature and can be re-checked: 900 rows at 345 MHz, 281 at 1410, 101
at 1980, 13 at 1965, 2 at 855, 1 at 450, and the single torn `14101410`. **The other seven CSVs of
the two campaigns are clean at 91–98 lines** — the length of the file is itself the detector, and
the tool should assert it.

#### ATTRIBUTION METHOD, AND ITS REAL VALIDITY CRITERION

Per-site attribution works by taking the paired launches inside each cuBLAS kernel-NAME group,
sorting them by duration, and cutting at known launch counts. For the 14,400-launch
`256x128_64x4_1x2_h_bz_coopA_NNT` group:

    cut boundary 1        gap   145,249 ns
    cut boundary 2        gap   309,889 ns
    3rd-largest gap anywhere    3,552 ns
    margin                      87x (boundary 2)   and   41x (boundary 1)

The two cuts are the #1 and #2 largest gaps in the sorted array by 87× and 41×. Clusters do not
overlap by a single nanosecond: **zero of 14,400 launches are ambiguous.**

**BUT THE STATED JUSTIFICATION WAS WRONG.** The claim "sites in a group differ in FLOPs by 4× or
more" is **FALSE** — `down` and `wQ` differ by only **2.75×** and one boundary is only **1.80×**.
What actually makes the method work is that **within-site duration spread is 3.8–8.7% of the
mean**, so any FLOPs step above roughly **1.3×** separates cleanly. The real criterion is the ratio
of the FLOPs step to the within-site spread, not the FLOPs step alone.

**AND NOTHING IN THE PROCEDURE DETECTS A BAD CUT.** Sorting and slicing at a count always yields an
answer, correct or not, so the gap margins must be re-verified per capture. **They shrink at free
clocks: boundary-1 gap/spread falls from 30.7× locked to 5.4× free.** Still safe, but 5.4× is a
margin that a wider spread or a closer pair of shapes would eat.

#### CLEARED vs STILL OPEN

**CLEARED:**

- **The dgrad/wgrad deficits were stream contention, full stop.** Single-stream locked: dgrad
  **100.0%**, wgrad **99.0%**. Nothing was wrong with those kernels.
- **We BEAT cuBLAS on `wK-dgrad/wV-dgrad`** — 109.3% locked, 105.3% free — because cuBLAS needs
  split-K plus a reduce on that shape and we do not.
- **Locked-clock parity**: 99.6% whole-run union, 99.1% GEMM sum, tok/s a tie.
- **PDL affects nsys spans, not throughput**: 0.06% (§H27zW-FUTURE).
- **cuBLAS never runs multistream** — but only because the harness never gives it a second stream.
- **Nobody is power-capped** (means 638–674 W against a 700 W limit, peaks 690–695 W).
- **The locked clock held** — 1410/1410/1410 in all four locked arms; the 1353 MHz reading was a
  contaminated CSV.
- **The pairing and attribution methods are now validated** — 100.0000% layout agreement, cuts at
  87×/41× the next-largest gap, zero ambiguous launches.
- **Everything except the matmul is identical to 7.2 ms.**

**STILL OPEN:**

- **The free-clock gap.** 97.0% GEMM, 98.5% whole-run union, −1.54% tok/s, **reproduced twice**,
  and concentrated in forward `nn`: `down-fwd` 92.7%, `wQ/wO-fwd` 92.6%, `gate_up-fwd` 98.3%, with
  forward carrying **236 of 354 ms**. This is the one live performance question.
- **Why we draw 20–25 W less at the same clock.** Signature says stalling; 9–12 device samples
  cannot prove it.
- **Whether the 10–25 MHz free-clock difference contributes at all.** Needs PER-KERNEL clock via
  `tools/h27zw_clock_matrix.sh`, not device sampling. Do not settle this with `nvidia-smi` again.
- **`wQ/wO-fwd` reads 99.5% on the bench but 96.8% in the trainer** at the same shape, same config,
  same clock. Leading candidate: the trainer runs addmm with **`beta != 0`** while the bench
  measured **`beta == 0`** — the short-circuited `C_in` epilogue read that §H27zv-D flagged as an
  unexercised branch. That is a one-experiment question and it should be the next one asked.
- **Our split-K reduce is 2.84× slower than cuBLAS's** (47.4 ms vs 16.7 ms on 2,880 launches). Only
  30.7 ms, but it is the single largest non-GEMM difference in the entire run and it is ours.

### §H27zY — SINGLE STREAM IS NOW THE DEFAULT. The backward secondary stream could never have paid: one GEMM CTA fills an entire SM, so concurrent-kernel overlap is CAPACITY-IMPOSSIBLE, not merely small.

`BLUTRAIN_BWD_SINGLE_STREAM` now defaults to **ON** (single stream). Only a literal `=0` restores
the two-stream path. Changed in `MatmulBackward.cu`; the old default was OFF.

#### THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT — occupancy, not timing

From `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL` in the §H27zX captures:

    dynamicSharedMemory   229,376 B   (sharedMemoryExecuted 233,472 = 228 KB) of 228 KB   = 100.0%
    registersPerThread    168, block 384  ->  64,512 of 65,536 registers                  =  98.4%
    grid                  132 CTAs on a 132-SM H200                                       =  1 CTA/SM
    registers left for ANY co-resident CTA                                                =  1,024

**A second concurrent kernel cannot be co-resident with ours at all** — not another GEMM, not a
`convert_type_kernel`, not anything. Its CTAs cannot begin until one of ours retires and releases
its 224 KB. Overlap is therefore limited to TAIL-FILLING as CTAs drain. cuBLAS makes the identical
choice (`grid(2,66,1)` = 132 CTAs, block 384), so it would hit the same wall if the trainer gave it
two streams.

**This kills a whole class of proposals, not just this one.** Any future "overlap the GEMM with X"
idea on SM90 is answered by the occupancy before it is built. The win has to come from ELIMINATING
work, not overlapping it.

#### WHAT THE FEATURE WAS WORTH, AND WHAT IT COST

    tok/s          locked 1400   two-stream 23,389  vs single 23,292   = +0.42%
                   FREE CLOCKS   two-stream 27,353  vs single 27,357   = -0.01%   <- production
    noise floor    ~0.3% (same cuBLAS arm re-run across campaigns: 23,337 vs 23,406)

    cost to our own kernels    dgrad +9.0% locked / +10.9% free      wgrad +4.7% / +5.4%
    cost to measurement        3.4 points of apparent GEMM performance, permanently

Production runs free clocks, where it earns nothing above the noise floor. Worst case from the flip
is giving up 0.42% at a clock setting nobody trains at.

#### THE SWITCH ANNOUNCES THE MODE IT LATCHED

`bwd_single_stream()` now prints `[blutrain] bwd stream mode = SINGLE|TWO` once on stderr. This is
not decoration. Without it a lost override is INVISIBLE, and there are two independent ways to lose
one: a value carrying a stray space or newline from an `--env-file` / k8s manifest / Slurm
`--export` resolves to the default silently, and `mpirun` forwards only what `-x` names (§H27zP).
Either way an A/B compares the default against itself and reports a clean ~0% delta that reads as
CONFIRMATION rather than as a broken instrument.

Two env conventions now coexist and both key on `"0"` meaning OPPOSITE things — `blublas_NO_PDL`
is presence-based so even `=0` disables PDL, while `BLUTRAIN_BWD_SINGLE_STREAM=0` *enables* two
streams. **Do not edit one by analogy with the other.**

#### TWO PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS FOUND WHILE REVIEWING THIS, NOT FIXED

1. **`MatmulBackward.cu:720` — the two-stream rejoin can be skipped.** A `throw` sits between the
   pre-handshake (552-555) and the rejoin (724-727) with no RAII guard, so an exception leaves the
   primary stream never waiting for a grad_B still in flight on `stream_b`. Safe today only by
   coincidence of which fallback kernels exist. Now that `=0` is the only way to reproduce older
   captures, this path needs the rejoin made unconditional on scope exit.
2. **`MatmulBackward.cu:637` — the fp16 grad_B branch hardcodes `beta=0.0f`** and discards the
   caller's `beta_b`, which is exactly the defect the comment above it claims was fixed. bf16 is
   correct; fp16 is not.

### §H27zZ — THE REAL PRIZE IS NOT THE GEMM. 23.60% of trainer GPU time is dtype conversion, and BOTH backends are asked for bf16 output by a single reusable variable.

    convert_type_kernel<bfloat16_t,float>   34,936 launches   4,728.0 ms   12.88%   GEMM OUTPUTS, up-cast
    convert_type_kernel<float,bfloat16_t>   26,120 launches   3,938.2 ms   10.73%   GEMM INPUTS, down-cast
                                                              --------
                                                              8,666.2 ms   23.60%

For scale: our GEMM is 37.62% of GPU time and the remaining gap to cuBLAS at locked clocks is
**141.6 ms**. The up-cast alone is **4,728 ms — 33x larger than the gap we have been chasing.**

#### THE ROUND TRIP IS REDUNDANT AND LOSSY

BluTrain holds everything in fp32 (`rms_norm_*_sm90<float>`, `swiglu_*_kernel_vec<float>`,
`add_kernel<float>`). Per matmul: fp32 -> bf16 -> GEMM -> **fp32 accumulator rounded to bf16** ->
bf16 stored -> bf16 read back -> widened to fp32. Steps 4-6 are a round trip on a value that was
ALREADY fp32 in a register and is wanted as fp32 by the next consumer.

The rounding is OURS and EXPLICIT — `__float22bfloat162_rn` / `__float2bfloat16` at template
lines 5757, 5786, 5907, 5998, 6006, 6024, 6073, against `float acc[MAX_ATOMS][WG_NCHUNKS][CREGS_CHUNK]`
at 4863. **The MMA does not do it for us**; wgmma leaves fp32 in registers and the epilogue chooses.
So it is entirely in our hands. 34,936 up-casts against 34,720 GEMM launches = one per output.

#### THE DECISIVE FINDING — cuBLAS IS ASKED FOR bf16 OUTPUT BY ONE REUSED VARIABLE

`MatmulBackward.cu:1256-1264`:

    cudaDataType_t cuda_type = ... ? CUDA_R_16F : CUDA_R_16BF;
    cublasGemmEx(handle, opB_bwd, CUBLAS_OP_N, K_a, M, N, &alpha_f,
        b_ptr,  cuda_type, ldb_bwd,              // A  bf16
        go_ptr, cuda_type, ldgo_bwd,             // B  bf16
        &beta_f, ga_ptr, cuda_type, ldga_bwd,    // C  bf16   <-- SAME VARIABLE
        CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP);

One variable in all three slots. `cublas_api.h:3368` confirms `Atype`/`Btype`/`Ctype` are
INDEPENDENT parameters, so bf16-in/fp32-out is expressible — **the bf16 output is BluTrain's
choice, not a cuBLAS limitation.** This explains the capture showing 34,936 up-casts in BOTH builds.

**Consequences.** (1) The fix is a ONE-TOKEN change, `ga_ptr, cuda_type` -> `ga_ptr, CUDA_R_32F`.
(2) It is symmetric, so an apples-to-apples comparison survives — the identical change is available
to both backends, which is what makes this a legitimate optimisation rather than a benchmark trick.
(3) **The whole hypothesis is testable on the cuBLAS path FIRST, with our kernel untouched.**

#### ORDERED PLAN, CHEAPEST AND MOST DECISIVE FIRST

    step 0  ~2 min   probe: does the H200 cuBLAS heuristic ACCEPT 16BF in / 32F out? Heuristics do
                     refuse combinations -- sm_86 cuBLASLt returned zero algos for bf16 bias output.
    step 1  ~30 min  map the 21 sites' consumers. THE NUMBER THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING AND IS NOT YET
                     KNOWN: outputs feeding another GEMM want bf16 again, so fp32 output MOVES their
                     convert rather than removing it. 4,728 ms is a CEILING, not an estimate.
    step 2  ~1 hr    one-token change on the cuBLAS path + drop the matching convert + measure tok/s.
                     Proves the win at zero risk to our kernel.
    step 3           only if 0-2 pay: build it into our kernel as a TEMPLATE KNOB, never a separate
                     kernel -- a separate kernel cannot compose with cluster/swizzle/raster/PDL/skew.

#### TWO EXPECTED BLOCKERS FOR STEP 3, BOTH UNVERIFIED

- **Shared memory.** Our CTA already uses 100% of the SM's 228 KB (§H27zY). An fp32 epilogue
  staging tile is 2x the bytes of a bf16 one. If the epilogue smem is additive rather than aliased
  onto mainloop TMA buffers, it may not fit at all.
- **`stmatrix` is 16-bit only.** If the epilogue stages through `stmatrix` (knob `EPI_USE_STSM`),
  an fp32 path cannot use it and needs a different store.

#### PRECISION, STATED FAIRLY

bf16 is 1-8-7 (8 significand bits); fp32 is 1-8-23 (24). The widening back to fp32 is EXACT since
bf16 is a strict prefix of fp32, so **all the loss happens in our epilogue rounding**. Removing it
strictly increases precision — there is no accuracy traded for speed here. Against that, fp32
output doubles the store bytes; the convert kernel currently reads 2N and writes 4N bytes, so
removing it saves ~4N of traffic net. Quantify per shape before claiming a number.

### §H27aa — THE CONVERSION KERNELS RUN AT 35% OF HBM PEAK ON H200, AND THE VECTORIZED REPLACEMENT ALREADY EXISTS IN THE TREE — it is gated to sm_103 only. Three independent wins found, cheapest first, no GPU needed to find any of them.

Offline source investigation while the box was unavailable. This is the step-1 site mapping owed
by §H27zZ, and it found something larger on the way.

#### 1. WHERE THE CASTS LIVE — the trainer script, explicitly, not the library

Every cast is written in `train/production/bluscript.cpp` as `autograd::to_dtype`. There is no
hidden conversion inside the matmul op; the library never casts. Forward map (SPLIT attention
path, which is what `bluscript_config_profile.yaml` selects — `use_fused_rms_rope`, NOT
`fully_fused_attn`):

    line  site        cast out        consumer                         verdict
    256   wQ-fwd      -> Float32      fused_rms_rope (fp32 kernel)     fp32 GENUINELY used
    257   wK-fwd      -> Float32      fused_rms_rope (fp32 kernel)     fp32 GENUINELY used
    258   wV-fwd      -> Float32      reshape/transpose, then 319      *** NO fp32 CONSUMER ***
    319                -> Bfloat16     scaled_dot_product_attention
    328   wO-fwd      -> Float32      add (fp32 residual)              fp32 GENUINELY used
    362   gate_up-fwd -> Float32      swiglu (fp32)                    fp32 GENUINELY used
    365   down-fwd    -> Float32      add (fp32 residual)              fp32 GENUINELY used
    467   lm_head     -> Float32      loss                             fp32 GENUINELY used

**SIX of the seven forward sites genuinely want fp32**, so an fp32-output epilogue would remove
their up-cast rather than merely move it. That was the open question from §H27zZ and it resolves
in favour of the idea.

Backward: `AutogradMeta.cpp:116,158,173` — for low-precision params the incoming gradient is
up-cast to fp32 (`lowp ? u.as_type(Dtype::Float32)`) so accumulation across the 4 grad_accum
micro-steps stays fp32. So the wgrad up-cast is removable the same way, and an fp32 output with
`beta=1` could accumulate STRAIGHT into the fp32 gradient buffer, removing a read-modify-write too.

#### 2. THE BIG ONE — the convert kernel is scalar on H200 while a vectorized one sits in the tree

`ConversionKernels.cu:157-198`. The launcher has a vectorized fast path... gated on
`is_sm103_device()`:

    if (is_sm103_device() && in%16==0 && out%16==0) { convert_cuda_bf16_to_fp32_sm103(...); return; }
    int threads = 256;
    int blocks  = std::max(((n + threads - 1) / threads), (long)112);
    convert_type_kernel<Src, Dst><<<blocks, threads, 0, stream>>>(input, output, n);

`is_sm103_device()` is B300. **On H200 it never fires**, so all 61,056 conversions run
`convert_type_kernel`, which is ONE ELEMENT PER THREAD with no vectorization —
`input[idx]` / `output[idx]`, scalar loads and stores.

**MEASURED ACHIEVED BANDWIDTH** (h27zX captures; `n` derived exactly from the launch config, since
`blocks = ceil(n/256)` with `threads=256` gives `n = gridX*256` — verified: gridX 131072*256 =
33,554,432 = 16384x2048, gridX 720896*256 = 184,549,376 = 16384x11264, both exact):

    phase     launches   time        elements    traffic      achieved     % of ~4800 GB/s peak
    locked      61,056   8,666.6 ms  2,392 G     14,354 GB    1,656 GB/s        35%
    free        61,056   7,422.3 ms  2,392 G     14,354 GB    1,934 GB/s        40%

    per-kernel, locked:  1,656 / 1,638 / 1,651 / 1,665 / 1,671 / 1,650 GB/s -- uniformly ~1,650

A pure memory-bound kernel should reach 80-90% of peak. **We are at 35%.**

**THE REPLACEMENT IS ALREADY WRITTEN.** `ConversionKernelsSM103.cu` header, verbatim:

    bf16 -> fp32 : vec8_convert_to_fp32, block 256, full grid (n/8 threads), one vector/thread
                   ~5380 GB/s vs PyTorch 2131 = 2.52x
    fp32 -> bf16 : n <  38.6M -> vec8_convert_to_bf16   6042 GB/s
                   n >= 38.6M -> gridstride_vec_convert_to_bf16, GS_UNROLL=2   6877 GB/s @ 134M

and, decisively, from the same header:

    "these kernels use only vectorized loads + bf16 intrinsics, no tcgen05 / TMA / inline PTX"

**Nothing in them requires Blackwell.** The gate is where they were TUNED, not what they REQUIRE.

#### 3. THREE INDEPENDENT WINS, CHEAPEST FIRST

**WIN A — enable the vec8 converters on H200.** No new kernel to write. Widen the device gate,
validate bit-exactness, re-tune the size threshold for H200 (the 38.6M crossover is a B300 number).
If H200 reaches the same fraction of ITS peak, ~3,500-3,800 GB/s against today's 1,656-1,934, i.e.
roughly **2x on 8,666 ms = ~4.3 s of a 36 s run, ~12% of total GPU time.** Zero precision change,
zero change to our GEMM. **For scale: our entire remaining GEMM gap to cuBLAS is 141.6 ms.**

**WIN B — delete the wV round trip.** Trainer one-liner. `wV`'s output is cast bf16 -> fp32
(line 258) and then straight back to bf16 (line 319) with NOTHING consuming it as fp32 in between
— only `reshape`/`transpose`, which are layout ops. Both casts are pure waste. Needs validation
that removing the autograd cast nodes is safe on the backward edge, but the forward logic is
unambiguous.

**WIN C — fp32 output epilogue in our GEMM (§H27zZ).** Removes the up-cast entirely rather than
speeding it up. Now better justified, since step 1 shows 6 of 7 sites genuinely want fp32. Still
the hardest: 100% of shared memory already used, and `stmatrix` is 16-bit only.

**A and C OVERLAP** — if C lands, the up-cast disappears and A only helps the remaining down-cast.
So do A first: it is cheap, immediate, needs no kernel redesign, and it de-risks C by telling us
how much of the 23.60% is bandwidth versus launch overhead.

#### WHAT IS STILL UNKNOWN

- Whether the vec8 kernels are bit-identical to the scalar ones on H200 inputs. Both use
  `__float2bfloat16` / `__bfloat162float`, so they should be, but it must be VALIDATED not assumed.
- Whether H200 tensors always satisfy the 16 B alignment the vec8 path requires. The launcher
  already falls back to scalar if not, so the risk is silent non-improvement, not incorrectness --
  which means any A/B must CONFIRM the fast path actually fired, not just measure.
- The right size threshold on H200; 38.6M is a B300 crossover and cannot be assumed to transfer.

### §H27ac — THE CLOCK QUESTION IS CLOSED. At equal clock we are **100.42%** of cuBLAS — we BEAT it. The entire free-clock gap is a **3.42% clock deficit**, and the cause is that we issue **1.57-2.27x** the instructions for identical tensor work.

#### THE CAUSE, MEASURED PER KERNEL IN THE SAME CAPTURE
