**Identical tensor work. Identical DRAM traffic. HIGHER SM occupancy on our side. And 1.57-2.27x
the instruction issue.** Issue burns fetch/decode/issue power; the governor answers with less
clock; we lose exactly that much throughput. This independently reproduces the 2.24x recorded on
the previous box, on different hardware with a different instrument.

#### V2c IS THE SMOKING GUN

    V2c  1400   ours 1310 MHz   cuBLAS 1404 MHz   CAP OVERRODE

We REQUESTED a 1400 lock. cuBLAS held 1404. We were throttled to 1310. Same card, same instant,
same requested clock — the power cap bit US and not them. That is our power draw isolated from
every other variable, and it is why V2c is the only shape still below parity when locked (92.8%).

#### WHAT THIS MAKES THE #1 TASK

Cut the instruction count. Not the tile shape, not the swizzle, not the epilogue latency — the
COUNT. Two concrete leads, both from static SASS and therefore both still HYPOTHESES:

**LEAD 1 — the uniform datapath.** cuBLAS runs address arithmetic on the U-prefixed forms, which
issue once per warp against the uniform register file. We run the per-thread forms:

    OURS                    cuBLAS
    IMAD    757             UIMAD   1702
    SHF     187             USHF     575
    LEA     174             ULDC    1771
    ISETP   121             UISETP  1150
    IADD3    78             UIADD3  3197

**LEAD 2 — STSM vs STS.** One `STSM.16.M88.4` moves a register block to shared; one `STS` moves
one register. Ours: STS 128, STSM 0. cuBLAS: STS 483, STSM 414. This REFRAMES the old stmatrix
null (§ probe_stsm_banks): that test measured DURATION on a path worth 1.40% of the kernel and
correctly found nothing. The right metric is INSTRUCTION COUNT, because count drives clock and
clock drives everything.

**THE CONFOUND, STATED SO IT IS NOT SKIPPED.** Both leads are STATIC counts from two kernels with
different unroll structure — ours loops (16 static HGMMA), cuBLAS is heavily unrolled (552 static
HGMMA). Static ratios do NOT translate to dynamic ones; our IMADs could be one-time setup. The
instrument that settles it is **ncu dynamic instruction mix** (`smsp__inst_executed` by category)
on the SAME shape for both libraries. Do not act on the static census alone.

### §H27ad — DYNAMIC instruction counts, ncu, V1. **2.54x confirmed** — but we execute them in the SAME cycles at the SAME tensor utilisation, so they cost POWER, not TIME. And the claimed instructions→power→clock chain is NOT yet proven; the power data we have argues against the naive version.

`loud-tree-grows-fin-03`, H200 GPU 1, ncu 2025.3.1, `--launch-count 4` per arm, profiled
separately per arm (a single window with `--launch-skip 8 --launch-count 8` caught only cuBLAS —
the two libraries do not interleave the way that assumed).

    V1  2048x512x16384 tn        per launch
    ours   : bgemm_sm90_kernel<Sm90WarpspecConfig<128,128,...>>   (config 128x128x64_2x1_v_sk2_dh_rot2_pdl_d6)
    cuBLAS : nvjet_sm90_tst_128x128_64x6_1x2_h_bz_splitK_NTT       (also split-K, so comparable)

    metric                        OURS         cuBLAS      ratio
    inst_executed           11,982,058      4,711,825      2.54x
    inst_issued             11,993,748      4,730,411      2.54x
    op_branch                1,052,597        278,217      3.78x
    op_shared_st                     0         82,432      0.00x
    op_global_st                32,768              0        inf
    op_tma_ld                   65,536         65,536      1.00x
    op_tma_st                        0          8,192      0.00x
    cycles_elapsed              76,204         75,490      1.01x
    TENSOR ACTIVE %               91.4           91.1      1.00x

#### THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THE STATIC CENSUS SUGGESTED

**2.54x the dynamic instructions, executed in 1.01x the cycles, at identical tensor utilisation.**
The instructions are therefore NOT costing us time. The tensor pipe is the bottleneck for both and
we keep it equally busy (91.4 vs 91.1). Whatever the 2.54x costs, it is not throughput directly.

#### BRANCHES ARE 3.78x — loop versus unroll

1,052,597 vs 278,217. Our mainloop LOOPS where cuBLAS UNROLLS. Largest single identified class,
but at 8.8% of our 12.0M total it is nowhere near the whole 2.54x. The remaining ~11M are
integer/predicate/float ops that these class counters do not break out — that is where the
IMAD-vs-UIMAD question lives and it needs the per-opcode SASS source counters.

#### THE STSM LEAD DOES NOT APPLY TO THIS CONFIG — and the static census misled me

Neither kernel uses `stsm` here (metric 0 for both). And the epilogue paths are the OPPOSITE of
what the static dump implied:

    ours     op_global_st 32,768   op_shared_st 0        -> DIRECT-TO-GLOBAL path
    cuBLAS   op_shared_st 82,432   op_tma_st 8,192       -> stages through shared, then TMA

The earlier static comparison (§H27ac LEAD 2) used `box_src/probe.sass`, which is a DIFFERENT
config (256x128 TN, STS 128 + UTMASTG 8). **The epilogue path is config-dependent**, so STSM must
be re-checked per config and cannot be treated as a blanket ours-vs-cuBLAS difference. This is the
static-count confound landing exactly where §H27ac warned it would.

#### THE MECHANISM IS NOT PROVEN. I ASSERTED IT TOO CONFIDENTLY.

The chain claimed in §H27ac was: more instructions -> more fetch/decode/issue power -> less clock
under the 700 W cap -> less throughput. The instruction half is now measured. **The power half is
not, and the power data we DO have contradicts the naive version:**

    §H27zX trainer, device-level, LOCKED 1400 (both at 1410 MHz):  ours 430-432 W   cuBLAS 449-462 W
    §H27zX trainer, device-level, FREE:                            ours 638-648 W   cuBLAS 657-674 W

**At equal clock we drew LESS power, not more.** If our instruction count made us power-hungry we
would expect the opposite. Three possible resolutions, none yet tested:
  1. Those are TRAINER device-level averages over 11-13 samples, not bench per-kernel power — the
     two measurements may simply not be comparable.
  2. Power is not the only governor input (temperature, current, reliability limits).
  3. The bench clock difference is not power-driven at all, and the instruction count is a
     coincidence rather than a cause.

**THE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES IT** is per-library power at a FIXED clock on the bench: lock the
clock, run ONE library at a time, sample power. If we draw more than cuBLAS at the same clock, the
chain holds. If we draw the same or less, the instruction count is not the clock lever and §H27ac's
conclusion needs rewriting. `nsys --gpu-metrics-devices` exposes no per-kernel power counter (the
ourPwr/cubPwr columns in `h27zw_clock_matrix.sh` came back "-"), so this needs device-level
sampling with a single library in flight.

#### WHAT REMAINS TRUE REGARDLESS

    locked, 13 LOCK HELD rows    mean %cuB 100.42%      we BEAT cuBLAS at equal clock
    free, 15 rows                mean %cuB  97.15%      and the gap equals the clock gap (-3.42%)

That result is from a different instrument (per-kernel clock via GPU_METRICS) and stands on its own.
What is open is WHY we are handed less clock, not WHETHER we are.

### §H27af — PER-VARIANT POWER ATTRIBUTION, LOCKED 1400. We match cuBLAS on power (**1.00-1.05x**), and **power does NOT explain the clock loss** — the worst-affected shape has ZERO power excess. Two measurement bugs had to be killed first, one of which produced a completely convincing false result.

`loud-tree-grows-fin-03`, H200 GPU 1, GPU 0 idle, commit `3b17c6e`. `tools/h27af_power_attrib.sh`:
10 s window per arm per rep, 3 reps, first 4 s discarded as sensor ramp, nvidia-smi at 99 Hz,
94,048 per-instant samples. **Every arm settled** (0 "still moving", 0 "too few").

Attribution works by PHASE MARKERS, not separate processes: the two timing windows are sequential
(cuBLAS for TARGET_MS, then ours), and with `BLUBLAS_PHASE_MARKS=1` the binary stamps the wall
clock at each window's edges in nvidia-smi's own format, so the sample stream splits exactly. One
process is DELIBERATE — both arms then see the same thermal state and clock history, seconds apart,
instead of reintroducing the cold-card order bias.

#### TWO BUGS THAT HAD TO DIE FIRST — the first one produced a fully convincing false result

**BUG 1: a 400 ms window never lets the power sensor settle.** Version 1 of this probe reported
ours at **2.3-2.6x cuBLAS's power on every variant**, and 73.2% cap-active on V2c against cuBLAS's
0.0%. It was ALL an artefact. The per-instant data showed every window still climbing at its end:

    V4  cublas   103 -> 140 -> 201 -> 263 W   across its 400 ms window
    V4  ours     368 -> 423 -> 486 -> 555 W   across its 400 ms window

Each rep runs idle -> cuBLAS -> ours, so power climbs monotonically and WHOEVER GOES SECOND LOOKS
WORSE. cuBLAS read low because it follows idle; we read high because we follow cuBLAS. The cap flag
was confounded identically — the cap fires late in the rep and late is always us. **The aggregate
table was entirely persuasive and entirely wrong; only the per-instant series exposed it.**

**BUG 2: `MAX_IT = 2000` silently truncated the window.** Asking for 10 s delivered 500 ms on fast
shapes (2000 iters x ~0.25 ms). Harmless for TFLOPS, fatal for power. Now `BLUBLAS_BENCH_MAX_IT`,
default unchanged at 2000 so no existing measurement moves.

**And §H27zA-BUG for the THIRD time:** `strings "$BIN" | grep -q PHASE` under `set -o pipefail`
REJECTS when the match IS found — `grep -q` exits on first hit, closes the pipe, `strings` dies on
SIGPIPE (141), pipefail promotes it to failure. Snapshot into a variable before matching. Never
pipe into a short-circuiting grep while pipefail is on.

#### FINDING 1 — WE MATCH cuBLAS ON POWER

1.00-1.05x, never more, on any shape. Settled, 99 Hz, phase-separated.

#### FINDING 2 — POWER DOES NOT EXPLAIN THE CLOCK LOSS

The extremes contradict each other outright:

    V1    +5% power  ->  -5.53% clock     most power excess
    V2c    0% power  ->  -6.99% clock     WORST clock loss, ZERO power excess
    V2b   +4% power  ->  -0.07% clock     high excess, no loss at all

If power drove clock, V2c would show no loss and V2b a large one. Both are backwards. **Cap state
does not predict it either**: V7/V8/V8b sit at 0% cap for both arms with identical clocks, while
V2c sits at 100% for both and loses 7%.

#### FINDING 3 — THIS DAMAGES THE INSTRUCTION THEORY

§H27ad measured **2.54x the instructions on V1**, and V1's power excess is **+5%**. So our extra
instructions are worth at most a few percent of total draw — power is dominated by tensor cores and
DRAM, which are near-identical between the two libraries. Removing EVERY extra instruction would
recover ~5% of power on the one shape where any excess exists, and **on V2c, where the clock loss
is worst, there is no power excess to remove at all.**

Instruction-cutting is therefore NOT the general clock lever proposed in §H27ac. It may still
matter on V1 specifically. It cannot explain V2c.

#### FINDING 4 — THE LOCK IS NOT HOLDING AS CLEANLY AS §H27ac REPORTED

On six shapes (V2c, V4, V5, V7b, V8c, V8d) BOTH libraries sit at 100% cap with clocks of 1361-1397,
i.e. the 1400 lock is not holding for either. §H27ac's tolerance was `min(ours,cuBLAS) >= F-40`,
which passes anything above 1360, so those rows were reported LOCK HELD while mildly capped. The
§H27ac conclusion (100.42% at equal clock) is unaffected — both arms were equally capped, so the
comparison stands — but the "LOCK HELD" label was too generous and the tolerance should tighten.

#### WHAT THIS RUN CANNOT ANSWER

It is at LOCKED 1400, where the mean loss is only -1.15% and concentrated in two shapes. **The
-3.42% gap of §H27ac is at FREE clocks**, a regime this instrument has not yet probed. That run is
next and is the one that matters.

### §H27ag — **THE MECHANISM IS FOUND.** At free clocks power is **1.00x** and both libraries are **100% capped on every shape**, yet our clock is lower — and the loss tracks the INSTRUCTION RATIO at **r = -0.742**, slope **-6.82% clock per 1.0x**. It is not that we draw more power. It is that we spend the same power on more switching and are handed fewer cycles.

`loud-tree-grows-fin-03`, H200 GPU 1, GPU 0 idle at 32-34 C, commit `3b17c6e`.

    V8d     1485    1476     +0.61%      1.81x

    Pearson r = -0.742    slope = -6.82 % clock per 1.0x instruction ratio
    mean clock loss = -1.73%

    POWER = 1.00x ON ALL FIFTEEN.   CAP = 100% vs 100% ON ALL FIFTEEN.

Grouped by instruction ratio the monotonicity is clean:

    1.56-1.61x   V3,V4,V5,V6                        mean loss -0.37%
    1.76-1.83x   V7,V7b,V7c,V8,V8b,V8c,V8d          mean loss -0.75%
    2.07-2.27x   V1,V2,V2b,V2c                      mean loss -4.55%

#### THE MECHANISM  *(corrected -- see CORRECTION note below)*

Dynamic switching power is

    P = alpha . C . V^2 . f      (+ a leakage term, roughly V-dependent and workload-independent)

with the terms meaning:

    C       CAPACITANCE. A fixed physical property of the silicon -- wire and gate capacitance
            laid down at fabrication. It does NOT change with workload. It is the same number
            when cuBLAS runs as when we run.
    alpha   ACTIVITY FACTOR. The fraction of switching nodes that actually toggle per clock
            cycle. THIS is the term the workload moves.
    alpha.C EFFECTIVE SWITCHED CAPACITANCE -- the product is the quantity that is actually
            charged and discharged each cycle, and it is the quantity our instruction count
            moves. C is fixed; we move alpha, so we move alpha.C.

Both libraries are pinned at the SAME P -- 100% cap on every shape, 1.00x measured power, on the
same silicon so the same C. Our higher instruction issue is a higher **alpha**: every extra
instruction issued per cycle means more decode, more register-file reads and writes, more
operand-collector traffic and more ALU toggling, so a larger fraction of that fixed capacitance is
charged and discharged each cycle. Rearranging at fixed P and fixed V:

    f = P / (alpha . C . V^2)

**A higher alpha forces a lower f.** We do not draw more power. We cannot -- we are both capped.
We spend the same watts on more switching and receive fewer cycles per second in exchange.

This reconciles everything that looked contradictory across §H27ad/§H27ae/§H27af:
  * power identical                         -> both at the ceiling                        ok
  * we still lose clock                     -> higher alpha (activity factor)             ok
  * §H27af V2c locked: same power, both capped, -7%                                       ok
  * §H27af V2b locked: +4% power, no clock loss -> neither was AT the ceiling there, so
    power was free to rise instead of frequency being taken away                          ok
  * §H27ad: 2.54x instructions in 1.01x cycles at identical tensor utilisation -- the
    instructions never cost TIME, they cost CLOCK                                         ok

#### CORRECTION TO THIS SECTION'S ORIGINAL WORDING

The first version of this section wrote the law as `P = C . V^2 . f` and called **C** the
"ACTIVITY FACTOR". That is wrong and it was my error. C is CAPACITANCE and it is fixed by the
silicon; **alpha** is the activity factor and it is what the workload changes. The two were
conflated under one symbol.

**The arithmetic and the conclusion are unaffected** -- the correlation, the slope, the grouped
monotonicity and the falsification test all stand exactly as measured, because only the NAMING was
wrong. The term that varies with workload was always the one being pointed at; it was simply given
the wrong letter. Nothing downstream of this section needs re-running.

#### THE PREDICTION THIS MAKES, AND HOW TO FALSIFY IT

The slope is quantitative: cutting the instruction ratio should return ~6.82% of clock per 1.0x.

    V1   2.07x -> 1.50x   predicts  +3.9% clock
    V2   2.27x -> 1.50x   predicts  +5.3% clock
    V2c  2.18x -> 1.50x   predicts  +4.6% clock

**The test is direct: cut instructions, re-measure clock, check the movement against the
prediction.** If the clock does not move as predicted, the correlation was spurious and this
section is wrong. That is the standard the PDL, secondary-stream and split-K-reduce claims were
held to, and this one gets it too.

#### CAVEATS, STATED PLAINLY

  * **r = -0.742, not 1.0.** Real scatter: V7c has a modest 1.83x ratio but a -2.75% loss;
    V2b has 2.20x and only -2.33%. Something else is also in play and this does not explain
    everything.
  * **Correlation is not causation.** What raises it above a coincidence here is that the
    competing explanation (we draw more power) is RULED OUT by direct measurement at 1.00x on
    every shape, and that a physical law predicts exactly this relationship.
  * **Mean loss -1.73% here vs -3.42% in §H27ac.** Different instrument (device-level nvidia-smi
    vs per-kernel nsys GPU_METRICS) and a different day. Direction and mechanism agree; the
    magnitude does not, and the per-kernel figure is the one to trust for absolute values.
  * The instruction ratios used here are §H27ac's per-kernel `issue` counters at FREE clocks, not
    the ncu dynamic counts of §H27ad. ncu measured 2.54x on V1 where the nsys issue counter says
    2.07x -- the two instruments disagree by ~20%, so the slope's absolute value is soft even
    though the ranking is consistent.
  * **alpha WAS NEVER MEASURED.** No instrument on this box exposes the activity factor. What we
    measured is the INSTRUCTION RATIO, and we are using it as a PROXY for alpha. The proxy is
    plausible -- more instructions issued per cycle really does mean more toggling -- but it is a
    proxy, not the quantity in the equation.
  * **V may also differ between the two workloads.** DVFS selects (V, f) pairs together, so a
    lower f can come with a lower V, and V enters the power law squared. We measured f and we
    measured P; we did not measure V per arm. Attributing the whole effect to alpha is therefore
    an ASSUMPTION, not a measurement, and part of the observed clock delta could be the voltage
    leg of the (V, f) pair rather than the activity factor.

#### WHAT THIS RETIRES AND WHAT IT OPENS

RETIRED: "we draw more power than cuBLAS" -- measured 1.00x on fifteen shapes, settled, at 99 Hz.
Also retired is §H27af's suggestion that instruction-cutting is not the lever; it IS the lever,
via activity factor rather than via power draw.

OPEN: which instructions make up the excess. §H27ad found branches at 3.78x but that is only 8.8%
of our total; the remaining ~11M per launch are unclassified. The per-opcode dynamic histogram
(ncu SASS source counters) is the next measurement, and it now has a clear purpose -- every
instruction removed is predicted to buy 6.82%/1.0x of clock back.

**ANSWERED IN §H27ah** -- the per-opcode dynamic histogram was run on four shapes. The excess is
`R2UR` + `ULEA` (warp-uniform addresses computed per-thread and then promoted), with cuBLAS at
ZERO `ULEA` on every shape. Branches came in at 8.3-10.3% of the gap, i.e. real but never the
largest term, exactly as the 8.8% figure above suggested.

### §H27ah — **THE PER-OPCODE DYNAMIC HISTOGRAM NAMES THE EXCESS.** Across four shapes, three tile configs and three layouts the SAME TWO OPCODES dominate the gap — `R2UR` and `ULEA` — and **cuBLAS issues `ULEA` exactly ZERO times in every single case**. The reading: we compute warp-uniform addresses PER THREAD and then promote them to uniform; cuBLAS's addresses are uniform from the start.

`loud-tree-grows-fin-03`, H200 GPU 1, commit `dbd1421`, `tools/h27ah_opcode_hist.sh`.

    collect : ncu --set detailed --section SourceCounters --launch-count 1
              (one launch per arm per shape)
    export  : ncu --import ... --page source --print-source sass --csv

That export gives **`Instructions Executed` PER SASS LINE** — a true DYNAMIC count, weighted by how
many times each line actually ran. It is not a static code-size census.

#### WHY DYNAMIC IS THE ONLY MEASUREMENT THAT MEANS ANYTHING HERE

Our mainloop **LOOPS** where cuBLAS **UNROLLS**. A static SASS opcode count therefore compares one
copy of our loop body against N inlined copies of theirs, and the ratio it produces is an artefact
of unroll factor, not of work done. §H27ac warned about exactly this confound and then acted on it
anyway:

  * **§H27ac LEAD 1 (the uniform datapath)** was a STATIC count.
  * **§H27ac LEAD 2 (STSM vs STS)** was a STATIC count, and §H27ad then showed it **does not apply
    to this config at all** — neither kernel uses `stsm` here (metric 0 for both), and the static
    dump that suggested it came from `box_src/probe.sass`, a DIFFERENT config.

**This measurement supersedes both.** LEAD 2 is dead (already killed in §H27ad). LEAD 1 is now
promoted from hypothesis to measured result, but on dynamic counts and with a sharper name: the
issue is not "cuBLAS uses U-forms and we do not", it is that **we produce the uniform value on the
per-thread path and then move it across**.

    shape    ncu dynamic    nsys issue    ncu is ...    free-clock loss (§H27ag)
    V1          2.43x          2.07x        +17.4%          -6.80%

Recorded precisely, because "the ranking is trustworthy" is not quite what the numbers say:

  * Both instruments put **V1 and V2c in the high group and V7 and V8d in the low group** — that

    inside the instruments' own ~17% disagreement, so neither ordering is resolved by this data.
  * Worth noting for whoever picks this up: **the ncu ordering matches the free-clock loss on all

    ncu-ratio vs clock-loss over these four points gives r = -0.996, slope -10.6% clock per 1.0x.

    a suggestive coincidence on a tiny sample, recorded so it is not lost, not a result.

#### THE DIAGNOSTIC PAIR — THIS IS THE CENTREPIECE

    opcode   shape   ours           cuBLAS
    R2UR     V1        1,050,112         4,096
             V2c     103,123,200       106,322
             V7        2,113,536        26,970
             V8d      51,527,680        26,970
    ULEA     V1        1,025,792             0
             V2c      43,349,784             0
             V7        1,788,360             0
             V8d      42,487,240             0

`R2UR` moves a value from a per-thread register into a **UNIFORM register**. `ULEA` then does
**uniform address arithmetic** on it.

**cuBLAS issues `ULEA` exactly ZERO times on every shape tested, and `R2UR` essentially zero**
(4,096 / 106,322 / 26,970 / 26,970 against our 1.05M / 103.1M / 2.11M / 51.5M).

The reading: **we compute warp-uniform addresses PER THREAD and then promote the result to
uniform. cuBLAS's addresses are uniform from the start, so it needs neither instruction.** A
warp-uniform address computed per-thread is **the same value calculated 32 times**.

This is not a subtle inefficiency at the margin. It is present on all four shapes, all three tile
configs and all three layouts, and it is the only pattern in the whole histogram where one library
is at zero and the other is in the tens of millions.

**The corroborating asymmetry on V1**: cuBLAS issues **6,272** `IMAD`s where we issue
**1,517,056** — a **242x** difference on plain integer multiply-add, and it is V1's single largest
gap term at 20.4%. Integer multiply-add is what address computation is made of.

#### ALSO RECORDED

  * **`BRA` is 8.3-10.3% of the gap on every shape** (V1 10.3%, V2c 8.3%, V7 9.8%, V8d 9.8%). Our
    mainloop loops where cuBLAS unrolls. It is REAL and it is remarkably stable across shapes, but
    it is **never the largest term** on any of the four. This is consistent with §H27ad's branch
    class counter (3.78x, 8.8% of our total on V1) and it keeps that lead alive at roughly its
    previously-measured size — no larger.
  * **`BSSY` 235,008 and `BSYNC` 284,544 on V1, against cuBLAS's ZERO.** These manage
    reconvergence points, so their presence at all is the statement: **our code has branch
    divergence and theirs does not.**
  * **`UIADD3` runs the OTHER way on V1** — ours 1,121,920 vs cuBLAS 1,887,808, a difference of
    **-765,888** in our favour on the raw count. **This is not a defect and must not be "fixed".**
    It is cuBLAS doing on the CHEAP UNIFORM path what we do on the EXPENSIVE PER-THREAD path. A
    uniform instruction issues once per warp; the per-thread equivalent issues for 32 lanes. Them
    having MORE uniform integer adds than us is the same finding as the R2UR/ULEA pair, seen from
    the other side.

#### TWO PARSING TRAPS, BOTH PAID FOR

  * **The exported CSV's FIRST line is a `"Kernel Name"` row; the real header is line 2.** Feeding
    the file straight to `csv.DictReader` does not error — it silently yields **ZERO for every
    column** and produces a table of all-zeros that looks like a legitimate (and very exciting)
    result. Skip line 1.
  * **A leading predicate (`@P0`, `@!P1`) must be stripped before taking the opcode**, otherwise
    predicated instructions land in their own bogus bucket and the real opcode is undercounted by
    exactly the amount that appears in the fake one.

Both of these produce plausible-looking output rather than a crash. That is the dangerous kind.

#### WHAT THIS MAKES ACTIONABLE

The target is no longer "cut instructions" in the abstract, which was never a task anyone could
start. It is now specific and it names the code path:

**STOP COMPUTING WARP-UNIFORM ADDRESSES PER-THREAD AND THEN PROMOTING THEM.**

§H27ag's slope predicts **~6.82% of clock returned per 1.0x of instruction ratio removed**, so the
payoff is quantitative and the test is direct: **change the address path, re-measure the clock, and
check the movement against the prediction.** V1 alone carries R2UR + ULEA + IMAD = 48.4% of its
gap, so this is not a rounding-error target.

**If the clock does not move as predicted, §H27ag is wrong and all of this is bookkeeping.** That
is the same falsification standard the PDL, secondary-stream and split-K-reduce claims were held
to, and it applies here without exception.

#### WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN — STATED SO IT IS NOT SKIPPED

**Which SOURCE-LEVEL construct emits the R2UR/ULEA pattern is unknown.** The histogram names the
INSTRUCTIONS; it does not name the line of CUDA that generates them. Without that mapping the
actionable statement above is a direction, not a patch.

That mapping is the next investigation, and the instrument is the same tool: **ncu's
SASS-to-source correlation**, which the `--page source` export can also provide. Do not start
rewriting the address path by guesswork before it is run — §H27ac's LEAD 2 is what guessing from
a dump that did not match the config costs.

### §H27ai — **THE EXCESS IS REMOVED, AND THE SASS PROVES IT BEFORE ANY GPU RUN.** `R2UR` 8→1 and `ULEA` 7→1 in V1's k-loop, **24.4% fewer instructions per wgmma**. The two knobs that do it already existed and were validated bit-exact — §H27zc2 limited that validation to 192x192, so V1 never got either. `dw` alone is WORSE (+5.1%); it only pays with `uad`, exactly as the mechanism predicts.

§H27ah named the opcodes. This section removes them, and the removal is measured
**statically, locally, from `cuobjdump`** — no GPU was needed to establish it.

#### THE APPLES-TO-APPLES DENOMINATOR

Both kernels issue **exactly 524,288 wgmma** on V1's pinned shape. That is identical
tensor work, so dividing by it makes every row below a cost per unit of real work,
not a cost per kernel:

| per wgmma | ours | cuBLAS | excess | | per wgmma | ours | cuBLAS | excess |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **IMAD**  | 2.75 | 0    | **+2.75** | | LOP3   | 0.75 | 0.10 | +0.65 |
| **R2UR**  | 2.00 | 0    | **+2.00** | | IADD3  | 0.75 | 0.10 | +0.65 |
| **ULEA**  | 1.25 | 0    | **+1.25** | | SHF    | 0.50 | 0    | +0.50 |
| UMOV      | 1.25 | 0.21 | +1.04     | | UIADD3 | 1.50 | 2.50 | **−1.00** |
| **TOTAL** | **16.56** | **6.58** | **2.52×** | | | | | |

2.52× against the 2.43× whole-kernel ratio of §H27ad — **the k-loop is the entire
story.** Nothing outside it needs to be touched to explain the gap.

Note the last row: we issue **fewer** `UIADD3` than cuBLAS. We are not simply doing
more of everything. We are doing the same address arithmetic on the *wrong datapath*.

#### WHAT CUBLAS DOES INSTEAD — the whole per-wgmma descriptor cost, from their SASS

```
HGMMA  R24, gdesc[UR16].tnspA.tnspB, R24
UIADD3 UR16, UR16, 0x80, URZ        <- A descriptor: walk
UIADD3 UR18, UR18, 0x80, URZ        <- B descriptor: walk
```

Two uniform adds, then one rewind (`UIADD3 UR16, UR16, -0x200`) at the bottom of the
group. **They never rebuild the descriptor. They walk it.** That is why their `R2UR`
and `ULEA` counters read zero — there is nothing to cross and nothing to recompute.

#### THE SMOKING GUN — ptxas ALREADY GETS IT RIGHT FOR B, IN THE SAME LOOP

```
B descriptor (uniform, correct)          A descriptor (vector, then crossed -- the waste)
  UIADD3        UR4, UR4, 0x4000           SHF.R.U32.HI  R2, RZ, 0x4, R2
  ULOP3.LUT     UR4, UR4, 0x3fc00          LOP3.LUT      R2, R2, 0x2000000
  USHF.R.U32.HI UR4, URZ, 0x4, UR4         R2UR          UR16, R2          <-- the crossing
  ULOP3.LUT     UR4, UR4, 0x2000000        IADD3         R8, P0, R5, 0x80
  UMOV          UR18, UR4                  IMAD.X        R9, RZ, RZ, R5, P0
                                           R2UR          UR24, R8
```

Same descriptor, same `>>4`, same OR-mask. One is free; the other costs six
instructions. This kills the "Hopper just needs R2UR for descriptors" reading dead —
the compiler emits the cheap form five lines away. The difference is whether the
inputs are provably warp-uniform.

#### THE THIRD SOURCE — `ULEA` IS 100% THE MODULO, AND THE OLD REFUTATION DOES NOT APPLY

`LOAD_PIPE_DEPTH` 6 is not a power of two, so `(stage + 1) % 6` compiles to a
magic-number division:

```
UIADD3 UR4, UR7, 0x1        UIMAD.WIDE UR8, UR4, 0x2aaaaaab      <- magic for /3
ULEA.HI UR9, UR9, UR9, URZ, 0x1                                  <- ...with the shift, /6
UIMAD UR4, UR9, -0x6, UR4   ISETP.NE / SEL / LOP3                <- x - (x/6)*6, then phase ^=
```

Seven instructions per iteration, and it is the **entire** source of our `ULEA`.
cuBLAS advances with a predicated compare-and-reset instead:
`@UP3 UMOV UR13, URZ / @!UP3 UIADD3 UR13, UR13, 0x1`.

**§H27zdy's note at the SKEW advance does NOT refute this.** It recorded that
"replacing `% LOAD_PIPE_DEPTH` with a branchless compare-select moved IMAD only
33 → 31 and R2UR not at all" — but it measured `IMAD` and `R2UR`, and the modulo
emits **neither**. The two opcodes it actually produces, `ULEA` and `UIMAD`, were
never counted. A null on the wrong counters is not a null.

#### THE CHANGE

- **new slot 40 `STAGE_CSEL`** — compare-select stage advance. `false` reproduces
  `(s+1) % DEPTH` exactly, so the default binary is byte-identical.
- **`advance_stage<DEPTH, CSEL>` helper**, all six advance sites routed through it.
  The one remaining `%` at the SKEW `while` predicate is untouched (V1 is not SKEW).
- **four configs on V1's pin**, adding `dw` / `uad` / `cs` one at a time so each is
  separately attributable. `DESC_WALK` and `UNIFORM_A_DESC` are **not new** — both
  were already validated bit-exact, but §H27zc2 restricted that to 192x192.

#### THE RESULT — static, innermost HGMMA loop, `cuobjdump`, per wgmma

| variant | instr/wgmma | vs base | R2UR | ULEA | IMAD | UIMAD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (V1 today)  | 19.50 | —          | 8 | 7 | 11 | 2 |
| `+cs`            | 19.25 | −1.3%      | 8 | 6 | 11 | **0** |
| `+dw`            | 20.50 | **+5.1%**  | 8 | 5 |  8 | 2 |
| `+dw +uad`       | 15.00 | **−23.1%** | **1** | **1** | 8 | 0 |
| `+dw +uad +cs`   | 14.75 | **−24.4%** | **1** | **1** | **6** | 0 |

**`dw` alone is worse, and that is the mechanism confirming itself.** DESC_WALK gives
one base plus compile-time offsets, but while `row0` remains a runtime value A's base
is still born on the vector datapath — so the walk is added *on top of* the rebuild
instead of replacing it. `UNIFORM_A_DESC` folds `row0` to a literal, which is what
lets the base stay uniform. They are a pair; neither is a knob you turn alone.

#### WHAT IS AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED

Established, locally and reproducibly: the static k-loop shrinks 24.4% per wgmma and
the two named opcodes drop by 8× and 7×.

**Not yet measured: dynamic instruction count, correctness, clock, TFLOPS.** `uad`
has never run on a 128x128 tile — §H27zc2's validation was 192x192 only, and §H27zm
records a real bug (`nchunk0_eff` on SPLIT_M tiles) that this exact knob exposed
before. Correctness is a gate, not a formality.

The prediction to test, from §H27ag's slope of −6.82% clock per 1.0× instructions:
cutting the k-loop 24.4% should return roughly **1.5–1.7% of clock**, on top of any
direct cycle saving. §H27ac put us at 100.42% at equal clock with a −3.42% clock
deficit; closing half that deficit is the target.

#### WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE

14.75 against cuBLAS's 6.58 — this is about **40% of the k-loop gap**. The remainder
is unroll depth: cuBLAS fits **16 static HGMMA** per loop body against our **4**, so
every loop-carried cost (branch, ISETP, `WARPGROUP.ARRIVE`, the mbarrier wait) is
amortised 4× better. `_KLOOP_UNROLL` (slot 33) already exists and is the next lever.

#### §H27ai OPEN TASKS — opened by the user on the strength of this result

**OPEN 1 — FIND THE SWEET SPOT.** §H27ai removed instructions that were pure
overhead, so it moves work-per-cycle and clock the *same* direction. That is a free
win, not a trade, and it says nothing about where the real trade begins. The task is
to map the curve: instructions/wgmma against achieved clock against TFLOPS, and find
the point where adding work per cycle starts costing more clock than it buys.
§H27ag's **−6.82% clock per 1.0× instruction ratio** is a fit over a narrow range
(1.77×–2.43×), not a law — the ladder in this section gives four new points on it and
should be used to test whether the slope holds below 1.77×.

**OPEN 2 — FILL THE IDLE TENSOR PIPE.** V1's tensor pipe runs **78.9–91.4% active**;
the rest is idle, and idle tensor cores are the largest single block of headroom left
for the 130% target. §H27zs already attributed it and the attribution is quantitative:

> cuBLAS's mainloop idles **~0** cycles per k-iteration, ours idles **34.8**. 34.8 is
> the length of our 31-instruction pre-first-HGMMA phase at ~1 IPC. cuBLAS's
> equivalent phase is **6 instructions** AND runs with 4 wgmma still in flight, so it
> is entirely hidden.

This is independent of the clock work — it is time, not power.

**Both point at the same lever: `_KLOOP_UNROLL` (slot 33, already in the template).**
cuBLAS fits 16 static HGMMA per loop body against our 4. That amortises every
loop-carried cost 4× better (OPEN 1) *and* gives the scheduler enough in-flight wgmma
to hide the pre-HGMMA phase (OPEN 2). It is also exactly the 60% of the k-loop gap
§H27ai does not close. Same discipline as this section: one knob at a time, static
SASS check locally before any GPU time is spent.

> The "293 W against a 700 W cap" reading was a SAMPLING ARTIFACT of my own instrument,
> not a property of the shape. `h27zdf_paired.sh` starts a fresh process per arm --
> context create, allocate, correctness check, teardown -- so the kernel is a sliver of
> wall-clock and a 200 ms sampler mostly watches an IDLE GPU. §H27af sampled the SAME
> shape under sustained load and measured **ours 692 W mean / 703 W max / cap_active
> 100%**, cuBLAS **667 W / 715 W / 99%**. **V1's shape IS fully power-capped.** The
> "128 CTAs is under one wave" argument is also backwards: one CTA fills an entire SM
> here, so 128 CTAs on 132 SMs is ~97% of the machine -- a FULL wave, which is exactly
> why it caps. FINDINGS 1 and 3, the paired tables, and the floors are unaffected.

### §H27aj — **THE INSTRUCTION CUT IS REAL AND BUYS NOTHING AT LOCKED CLOCK.** ~~AND THE CLOCK PREMISE IS REFUTED ON THIS SHAPE.~~ *(second clause retracted, see banner)* 24.4% fewer k-loop instructions moves performance **−0.22 ± 0.46** at locked clocks against a **0.72-point** floor. The free-clock arm cannot resolve anything (floor **3.16**). And the decisive number: peak power over the entire free run was **293 W against a 700 W cap** — we were never power-limited, so the α→power→clock mechanism could not have been operating here at all.

§H27ai cut the instructions and verified the cut in SASS. This section measures what
the cut is worth. **Correctness first: 10/10 PASS, `maxRelErr 0.00000` on every arm**,
including `dw_uad` on a 128x128 tile, which had never run there (§H27zc2 validated it
on 192x192 only). The correctness gate is cleared and bit-exact.

#### THE INSTRUMENT — `h27zdf_paired.sh`, 21 reps, 6 arms, PIN entered TWICE as the null

Shape `2048x512x16384 tn`, one config per process, 400 ms window, rotated arm order.

**LOCKED 1400** (achieved 1410 MHz, min = max, lock verified):

| arm | mean_d vs pin | sd_d | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| NULL_B *(identical binary)* | **−0.07** | 0.65 | **method error → floor 0.72** |
| CS | −0.10 | 0.55 | not separable |
| DW | +0.02 | 0.62 | not separable |
| **DW_UAD** | **−7.33** | 0.45 | **believable — a real regression** |
| DW_UAD_CS | −0.22 | 0.46 | not separable |

**FREE clocks:**

| arm | mean_d vs pin | sd_d | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| NULL_B *(identical binary)* | **+0.48** | 2.68 | **floor 3.16 — the arm is unusable** |
| CS | −0.83 | 2.66 | not separable |
| DW | −0.31 | 3.31 | not separable |
| **DW_UAD** | **−4.44** | 2.93 | believable — regression confirmed in both phases |
| DW_UAD_CS | −0.70 | 2.80 | not separable |

#### FINDING 1 — AT A FIXED CLOCK THE CUT IS WORTH ZERO, AND THAT CONFIRMS §H27ad

This is not a disappointing null; it is the predicted one. §H27ad measured **2.54×
dynamic instructions in the SAME cycles at the SAME tensor utilisation**. Those
instructions were already hidden behind tensor work — they cost power, not time.
Pinning the clock removes the only channel through which removing them could pay, so
a null at locked clocks is what the earlier measurement *requires*.

#### ~~FINDING 2 — THE POWER PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD ON THIS SHAPE.~~ **RETRACTED — see the banner. The premise holds; the instrument was wrong.**

Dense sampling across the whole free run, 200 ms cadence:

```
2531 samples    mean 165 W    MAX 293 W    >200 W: 28.4%    >400 W: 0 (0.0%)
```

**The cap is 700 W. Nothing ever came close.** The clock had no power reason to fall,
so nothing about α, activity factor or instruction count could have influenced it here.

The cause is the shape. `2048x512x16384` with a 128x128 tile is
(2048/128)x(512/128) = **64 tiles**, x2 for split-K = **128 CTAs on 132 SMs — less
than a single wave**, a ~0.06 ms kernel. V1's pin is far too small to be a power
experiment. §H27ag's clock mechanism was fitted across 15 shapes including large
ones; carrying its conclusion onto this shape was an unjustified transfer and is
retracted for this shape. **§H27ag is not refuted — it was tested somewhere it could
not apply.**

#### FINDING 3 — `DW_UAD` IS A REAL REGRESSION, AND `CS` ON TOP ERASES IT

−7.33 locked and −4.44 free, both far outside their floors, same sign, consistent.
Yet `DW_UAD_CS` — two static instructions fewer — sits at −0.22 and −0.70, i.e. back
at the pin. A 2-instruction delta cannot be worth 7 points, so this is a **cliff, not
a slope**: `uad` emits TWO mainloop copies (1584 static instructions against 1392),
and something about that footprint — I-cache, scheduling, register pressure — costs
more than the arithmetic it saves. **Do not ship `dw_uad`.** `cs` alone is bit-exact,
free, and inside the floor; keep it.

#### THE CEILING ARITHMETIC — why the clock track cannot reach the 130% target

| path | ceiling | basis |
|---|---|---|
| clock | **~104%** | §H27ac: 100.42% at equal clock, −3.42% clock deficit; closing it entirely |
| tensor fill | **~109%** | cuBLAS measured at 92% tensor active; 100/92 = 1.087 |
| **memory traffic** | **past 130%** | §H27z.82: ours **10.12 GB** vs cuBLAS **4.16 GB**; reuse recovered 76% vs 93% |

Clock and tensor-fill **cannot arithmetically reach 130% even executed perfectly**.
Data movement is the only lever with the target inside it, and at 2.43x it is the
largest single inefficiency measured anywhere in this campaign.

**RECOMMENDATION: park the clock track. Open data movement as the primary line.**

#### WHAT IS BANKED

- `STAGE_CSEL` (`cs`): bit-exact, removes the magic-number division, neutral on
  performance, **keep**. Instruction count also gates unroll depth, which is the
  `KLOOP_UNROLL` lever for the idle tensor pipe.
- **The locked null of 0.72 points** is the most valuable artifact of the day — a
  trustworthy instrument at this shape and window.
- **The free-clock floor of 3.16 points** says free-clock A/B on this box cannot
  settle anything under ~3 points. Prior free-clock adoptions under that size should
  be re-read with this in mind.

### §H27ak — **§H27aj's FINDING 2 IS RETRACTED. V1's SHAPE IS FULLY POWER-CAPPED (692 W, cap_active 100%) AND WE PAY A 6.8% CLOCK DEFICIT THERE.** The clock track is NOT closed — it was never tested, because §H27aj measured `%cuB` (free-clock floor **3.16 points**) instead of measuring the CLOCK, which is the variable the mechanism actually predicts.

#### THE AUDIT THAT CAUGHT IT

§H27aj concluded the power premise could not hold on `2048x512x16384` because a dense
sampler saw **max 293 W against a 700 W cap**. §H27af had already profiled **the same
shape on the same box**. Re-reading its 103,026 samples:

| variant | arm | n | cap_active | P mean | P max | clock mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 `2048x512x16384` | ours   | 3308 | **100%** | **692 W** | 703 W | **1432 MHz** |
| V1 `2048x512x16384` | cuBLAS | 3408 | 99%      | 667 W     | 715 W | **1537 MHz** |

Across all 15 shapes: **cap_active 102,364 / 103,026 = 99.4%**, global P max **715 W**.
Both libraries are pinned to the power cap on every shape in the set.

**The 293 W was my instrument, not the hardware.** `h27zdf_paired.sh` launches a fresh
process per arm — CUDA context creation, allocation, the correctness pass, teardown —
so the kernel occupies a small fraction of wall-clock. A 200 ms sampler therefore
spends most of its samples on an idle GPU. §H27af avoided this with sustained 10 s
windows and a 4 s settling discard, which is why it saw 692 W.

The secondary argument was wrong too. "128 CTAs on 132 SMs is under one wave" implied
low utilisation — but §H27zY established that **one of our GEMM CTAs fills an entire
SM** (100% of dynamic smem, 98.4% of registers, 1 CTA/SM). 128 of 132 SMs is ~97% of
the machine: a *full* wave. Sub-one-wave in CTA count is full occupancy in hardware.

#### WHAT THIS RESTORES — the mechanism is live on this shape, and it is large

At free clocks on V1's pin we draw **more** power than cuBLAS (692 vs 667 W, 1.04x) and
run **105 MHz slower** (1432 vs 1537) — a **6.8% clock deficit** at a 2.43x instruction
ratio. That is §H27ag's r = −0.742 relationship, present on the exact shape §H27aj
declared it absent from.

#### WHY §H27aj STILL FAILED TO SEE THE EFFECT — it measured the wrong variable

§H27aj's free arm reported `%cuB` with a **null-control floor of 3.16 points**. Clock,
by contrast, is directly readable and far more stable. The mechanism predicts a change
in CLOCK; the experiment only ever looked at a derived, noisier quantity.

**THE OUTSTANDING TEST, and it is cheap.** Cutting 24.4% of k-loop instructions moves
the ratio 2.43x → ~1.84x. At §H27ag's slope of −6.82% per 1.0x that predicts **≈ +4%
clock**. Protocol must be §H27af's, not §H27aj's: sustained load, 10 s windows, 4 s
settling discard, measuring `clocks.sm` and `power.draw` for `base` vs `cs` vs
`dw_uad_cs` — **not** `%cuB`. Falsifiable in one direction: if clock does not move, the
instruction→clock channel is dead and the track closes for real.

#### WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE

§H27aj FINDINGS 1 and 3 stand. At **locked** clock the cut is worth **−0.22 against a
0.72 floor — zero** — and that remains the correct, predicted result, because pinning
the clock removes the only channel the mechanism has. `dw_uad` remains a real
regression (−7.33 locked, −4.44 free) and must not ship. `cs` remains bit-exact, free
and banked.

**The ceiling arithmetic also stands**: even a perfectly recovered clock is worth ~104%,
and tensor fill ~109%. Neither reaches the 130% target; only data movement (2.43x,
§H27z.82) does. Settling the clock question is worth doing because it is cheap and
because "untested" invites re-litigation — but it is not the path to 130%.

### §H27al — **THE TARGET IS A NUMBER: GET THE INSTRUCTION RATIO BELOW ~1.8x AND THE CLOCK DEFICIT DISAPPEARS.** Two independent instruction measures, fitted separately against the same clock data, converge on a zero-crossing of **1.77x** and **1.80x**. §H27ah's per-opcode count is the better predictor (**r = −0.996**, perfectly monotonic) against §H27ag's issue ratio (**r = −0.903**, NOT monotonic). §H27ai's cut moves V1 from 2.43x to 2.08x — predicted **−6.80% → −3.03%** clock, i.e. **roughly half the deficit**, with **0.29x of excess still to remove**.

§H27ak reopened the clock track. This section turns it from a direction into a target, using
only data already on disk — no GPU time was spent.

#### FIRST, §H27ag's PUBLISHED FIT REPRODUCES EXACTLY

Refitting its own 15-shape table: **r = −0.745, slope −6.83% per 1.0x**, against the published
−0.742 / −6.82. The published number is sound and is not in question here.

#### THE TWO INSTRUCTION MEASURES ARE NOT THE SAME NUMBER, AND ONE IS CLEARLY BETTER

They disagree materially — V1 is **2.07x** by §H27ag and **2.43x** by §H27ah — because they
count different things:

- **§H27ag "issue ratio"** — `smsp__inst_executed`, an issue-rate measure taken from the free rows.
- **§H27ah "per-opcode ratio"** — dynamic per-opcode totals from the ncu SASS export, **deduped
  by address** (the `cuda,sass` view repeats addresses; §H27ah's total matched the sass-only
  reference exactly after dedup).

Head to head on the four shapes where BOTH exist, against the same clock losses:

| predictor | n | r | slope | zero-crossing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| §H27ag issue ratio | 4 | −0.903 | −16.75%/1.0x | 1.77x |
| **§H27ah per-opcode ratio** | 4 | **−0.996** | −10.62%/1.0x | **1.80x** |

The monotonicity check is what separates them:

```
H27ag issue :  V7(1.80)->-1.08   V8d(1.81)->+0.61   V1(2.07)->-6.80   V2c(2.18)->-5.52
H27ah opcode:  V8d(1.77)->+0.61  V7(1.86)->-1.08    V2c(2.33)->-5.52  V1(2.43)->-6.80
```

**§H27ag's ordering breaks twice** — V8d has a *higher* issue ratio than V7 yet a *better* clock,
and V1 has a *lower* issue ratio than V2c yet a *worse* clock. **§H27ah's ordering is perfect.**

That is a result in its own right: **an issue-rate metric is the wrong instrument for this
question, and the per-opcode dynamic count is the right one.** It also explains why §H27ag's
15-shape r was only −0.742 — the scatter is substantially measurement, not physics.

#### THE CONVERGENCE IS THE STRONG PART, NOT EITHER FIT ALONE

Four points at r = −0.996 is seductive and, on its own, weak evidence. What carries weight is
that **two differently-defined instruction measures, fitted independently, land the zero-crossing
at 1.77x and 1.80x** — and that **V8d is a measured shape sitting at 1.77x with a clock deficit
of +0.61%, i.e. already slightly AHEAD of cuBLAS.** The crossing is not an extrapolation into
empty space; there is a real shape sitting on it.

#### WHAT §H27ai's CUT IS PREDICTED TO BE WORTH

```
V1 k-loop      16.56 -> 12.53 instr/wgmma      (-24.4%, measured in SASS, §H27ai)
V1 whole-kernel ratio   2.43x -> 2.08x
predicted clock         -6.80% -> -3.03%       gain +3.70 points
remaining above the 1.80x crossing:  +0.29x
```

**Roughly half the deficit, and about 14% more instructions still to remove to reach break-even.**

#### THE CEILING, REVISED UPWARD

§H27aj quoted ~104% for this track, derived from the **15-shape mean** clock loss of −1.73%.
That understates it per-shape. V1's own deficit is −6.80%, and §H27ac put us at **100.42% of
cuBLAS at equal clock**. Closing V1's deficit entirely gives `100.42 x 1.068 ≈ 107%`, and the
per-opcode fit extrapolated to instruction parity (1.0x) implies a clock *advantage*, not merely
parity. **Call the ceiling ~107-108%, not 104%.**

This does **not** change the strategic conclusion. **130% is not reachable on this track** —
tensor fill caps near 109% (cuBLAS measured at 92% tensor active) and clock near 108%. Only data
movement (**10.12 GB vs 4.16 GB**, reuse 76% vs 93%, §H27z.82) has the target inside it. The
clock track is worth ~7 points and is cheap; it is not the path to 130%.

#### THE OUTSTANDING TESTS, both cheap, both falsifiable

1. **Per-opcode ratios for the remaining 11 shapes.** `tools/h27ah_opcode_hist.sh` already exists
   and no code changes are needed. Turns the n=4 fit into n=15 and either confirms the ~1.8x
   crossing or kills it. **This is the highest-value GPU hour available** — it is pure
   measurement of the better predictor across the set.
2. **Measure V1's CLOCK, not `%cuB`, base vs `dw_uad_cs`.** §H27af protocol: sustained load,
   10 s windows, 4 s settling discard, `clocks.sm` + `power.draw`. Prediction: **+3.70 points of
   clock, −6.80% → −3.03%.** §H27aj failed to see anything only because `%cuB` carries a
   3.16-point free-clock floor while clock is directly readable and stable.

**Falsifiable in one direction:** if V1's clock does not move on a cut that verifiably removed
24.4% of k-loop instructions, the instruction→clock channel is dead and the track closes for real.

### §H27am — **THE INTERVENTION TEST: cutting 24.4% of k-loop instructions moves the clock by +0.58 points, against +3.70 predicted.** The channel is REAL — monotonic, drift-controlled, outside the control's own spread — but the true within-shape slope is **1.66% per 1.0x instruction ratio**, SIX TIMES shallower than §H27al's cross-shape fit. Even removing ALL remaining excess would recover only ~1.8 of V1's 6.74 points.

`plain-fish-falls-fin-03`, H200 GPU 1, free clocks, §H27af protocol: 10 s windows, first
4 s discarded, ~98 Hz sampling, ~2200 settled samples per arm, 3 reps.

    arm      ours MHz   cuBLAS MHz   deficit    vs base
    base       1429.0       1532.3    -6.74%      +0.0 MHz
    +cs        1434.0       1531.0    -6.34%      +4.9 MHz
    +cut       1439.2       1533.8    -6.16%     +10.2 MHz

**All six arms at 693 W and cap_active 100%.** cuBLAS is the SAME binary in all three
arms and its clock across them spans **2.8 MHz** — that is this measurement's own error
on this quantity, so +10.2 MHz is real. The ordering confound also runs the wrong way:
a warming card lowers clock over a session, and ours rose.

#### THE PREDICTION FAILED BY 6x, AND THAT IS THE FINDING

§H27al predicted −6.80% → −3.03%, a gain of **+3.70 points**. Measured: **+0.58**.
Implied within-shape slope **1.66% per 1.0x** against the cross-shape fit's 10.62%.

    local slope           1.66% clock per 1.0x ratio
    current ratio         2.08x  (after the cut)
    removing ALL excess   (2.08 - 1.0) x 1.66 = +1.8 points
    V1's actual deficit   6.74 points

**Perfect instruction parity with cuBLAS recovers under a third of the deficit.**
Therefore the cross-shape correlation of §H27al (r = −0.996) is a PREDICTOR, not a
CAUSE — something co-varies with instruction ratio across shapes and carries most of
that relationship. **The intervention is the causal test and the correlation is not.**
This is the second time a cross-shape number has failed to transfer (§H27ak was the
first); the rule to take from it is that only a within-shape A/B establishes causation.

### §H27an — **DATA MOVEMENT IS NOT THE GAP. We move the SAME bytes as cuBLAS.** V1: ours 0.081 GB vs 0.082 GB, both at **1.02x the theoretical minimum**. V4: 3.869 vs 3.679 GB (**1.05x**, not 2.43x). §H27z.82's "10.12 GB vs 4.16 GB, reuse 76% vs 93%" **does not reproduce** — it was a different config, and the work since has closed it.

    V1  2048x512x16384 tn      mandatory read 0.078 GB   write 0.002 GB
        arm       DRAM rd   DRAM wr    total   x mand   L2 hit   reuse    tile
        ours       0.078G    0.003G   0.081G    1.02x    69.8%   100.0%  128x128
        cublas     0.078G    0.004G   0.082G    1.02x    49.5%   100.0%  128x128

    V4  16384x50304x2048 nn    mandatory read 0.254 GB   write 1.535 GB
        ours       2.339G    1.530G   3.869G    2.16x    87.3%    93.6%  192x192
        cublas     2.150G    1.529G   3.679G    2.06x    88.7%    94.2%  192x192

On V1 — the shape carrying the 6.74% clock deficit — we move **fewer** bytes than cuBLAS
and our L2 hit rate is **better** (69.8% vs 49.5%). The hypothesis that DRAM traffic
causes the clock deficit is **refuted on the shape it was invoked to explain**.

§H27z.82 measured a `192x192x64_1x2_v` config; today's V4 pin is
`192x192x64_2x1_h_rs8_dh_ubd_dw_skew_lsw_pdl`. Quoting the old figure across that config
change was the same carry-forward error as §H27ak. **Data movement is not a 130% lever;
that claim is withdrawn.**

### §H27ao — **ACTIVITY CENSUS: total instruction issue is the ONLY counter that tracks the clock deficit.** And the opcodes we have been hunting are not the driver — `pipe_fma` (our IMAD) runs **273x–557x** cuBLAS and is WORST on V8d, the one shape with NO deficit.

Four shapes chosen to span the deficit range, so a cause must be high where the deficit
is high and ~1.0 where it is absent.

    metric (ours/cuBLAS)      V1 -6.74%   V2c -5.7%   V7 -0.9%   V8d +0.4%   tracks?
    smsp__inst_executed          2.54x       2.24x      1.81x      1.78x     YES
    sm__inst_executed_pipe_fma 273.63x     359.72x     36.51x    557.54x     no
    sm__inst_executed_pipe_alu   6.18x       9.13x      4.62x      5.78x     no
    lts__t_requests              1.85x       1.48x      1.25x      1.45x     no
    dram__bytes                  1.00x       1.99x      1.02x      1.42x     no
    sm__pipe_tensor_cycles       1.00x       1.00x      1.00x      1.00x     CONTROL

`sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active` is **1.00x on all four** — identical tensor work, which
is what makes the rest a fair comparison.

**`pipe_fma` is the address arithmetic** (IMAD issues on the FMA pipe; §H27ah measured
IMAD at 242x on V1 and this reports 273x on the same shape). 48 million against 86
thousand on V8d — and V8d has the best clock of the four. **So the specific integer
math §H27ah named, and §H27ai removed, is not what sets the clock.** That is consistent
with §H27am measuring the intervention at only +0.58 points.

### §H27ap — **"LOCKED 1400" WAS NEVER A CONTROL. The lock BROKE on 6 of 15 variants under sustained load, asymmetrically, and worst exactly where the deficit is worst.** On V1 we ran **1332 MHz at 698 W** while cuBLAS ran **1410 MHz at 665 W** — cuBLAS stayed under the 700 W cap and held its clock; we reached the cap and the governor took 68 MHz.

Re-reading §H27af's own locked-1400 per-instant data, 10 s sustained windows:

    var    ours MHz   cuB MHz   ours W   cuB W   verdict
    V1         1332      1410      698     665   LOCK BROKE   -5.6% at "equal" clock
    V2c        1277      1373      698     698   LOCK BROKE   -7.0%
    V4         1366      1380      698     697   LOCK BROKE   -1.1%
    V5         1367      1361      698     698   LOCK BROKE   +0.5%
    V7b        1384      1397      697     697   LOCK BROKE   -1.0%
    V8d        1380      1387      698     697   LOCK BROKE   -0.5%
    V2/V7c/V2b/V3/V8c/V6/V7/V8b/V8 ................ held at 1410

**Two consequences.**

1. **§H27ac's "100.42% of cuBLAS at equal clock" did not hold the clock equal on V1 or
   V2c** under sustained load. V1's free deficit is −6.7% and its locked-1400 deficit is
   −5.6%; locking barely changed the condition on the shapes that matter. (Short 400 ms
   bursts DO hold 1410 — §H27aj measured min = max = 1410 — so the two regimes differ and
   must not be conflated.)

2. **It is also the cleanest causal statement so far**, because it is a direct
   measurement with no fitting: *at the same clock target we demand 33 W more and pay
   78 MHz for it.*

#### WHY EVERY MEASUREMENT SO FAR WAS TAKEN IN THE WRONG CONDITION

At **free** clocks both arms sit pinned at the cap (693 W / 100% both, §H27am). Power
**cannot** differ there — the governor equalises it by taking our clock. So a free-clock
power comparison is uninformative by construction, and a free-clock A/B on throughput
carries a 3.16-point floor (§H27aj). At **locked 1400** the lock breaks on the
power-hungry shapes, so that is not a control either.

**THE CORRECT CONDITION: lock LOW enough that BOTH arms stay under the cap.** There the
clock is equal by construction and the power difference is unclamped — a direct reading
of excess activity in watts. `tools/h27ap_power_clock_sweep.sh` sweeps the lock down
until that holds and then measures cuBLAS vs base vs cut.

**FALSIFIABLE:** if the §H27ai cut does not lower our watts at a sub-cap clock, then
removing instructions does not reduce activity, and the instruction→clock track closes.

#### BUILD NOTE — CUDA 13.1 BREAKS THIS TREE

`kind-data-thinks-fin-03` ships CUDA **13.1.115** alongside 13.0.88, and the Makefile
auto-selects the highest (`ls /usr/local/cuda*/bin/nvcc | sort -V | tail -1`). Under
13.1 all three variant TUs fail with `macro "__cudaLaunch" passed 2 arguments, but takes
just 1` — nvcc's generated stub emits a two-argument call while its own
`crt/host_runtime.h` defines the one-argument form. A trivial kernel compiles fine, so it
is triggered by this tree specifically (very long mangled config names are the likely
trigger). **Build with `make NVCC=/usr/local/cuda-13.0/bin/nvcc`** — `CUDA_PATH` is
derived from the nvcc path so includes and libs follow consistently. Pinning 13.0 is
required for continuity anyway: a toolkit change alters codegen and would void every
instruction count in §H27ah/§H27ai/§H27ao.

### §H27as — ~~**THE INSTRUCTION EXCESS IS NOT WHY WE ARE BEHIND.**~~ *(RETRACTED — see banner)* It ANTI-correlates with the deficit (r = −0.305, wrong sign). What predicts the deficit across all 15 variants is K (r = −0.730).** V1 has the MOST extra math (2.54x) and the SMALLEST cycle penalty (1.003x); V8 has BELOW-AVERAGE extra math (1.78x) and the LARGEST (1.079x). Tensor utilisation is at parity — mean gap −0.75 points, and we are AHEAD on V1 and V4.

#### ABSOLUTE TENSOR UTILISATION, ALL 15, MEASURED ON THIS BOX

#### THE HYPOTHESIS UNDER TEST, AND ITS REFUTATION

The standing hypothesis has been: the excess integer/address math is why we lose — it
burns cycles and switching, so we do less useful work per cycle than cuBLAS. Correlating
across all 15:

    instruction ratio  vs  cycle penalty    r = -0.305     WRONG SIGN
    instruction ratio  vs  tensor gap       r = +0.265     WRONG SIGN
    log(K)             vs  cycle penalty    r = -0.730     strong, correct sign
    log(K)             vs  tensor gap       r = +0.715     strong, correct sign

**More extra math goes with LESS penalty.** The two extremes make it plain: V1 issues
2.54x cuBLAS's instructions and is 0.3% behind in cycles; V8 issues 1.78x and is 7.9%
behind. **K explains 73% of the variance; instruction count explains none of it with the
right sign.**

This is now the THIRD independent measurement agreeing:
1. §H27am — the direct intervention: cutting 24.4% of k-loop instructions bought
   **+0.58 clock points and zero cycles**.
2. §H27ao — `pipe_fma` (our IMAD) runs 273x–557x cuBLAS and is WORST on V8d, the shape
   with the BEST clock.
3. This section — the cross-shape correlation has the wrong sign.

**Conclusion: the excess instructions cost POWER, not TIME.** They are worth roughly 1.8
clock points in total (§H27am's causal slope), and even that is mostly uncapturable.
`STAGE_CSEL` should still ship — it is bit-exact and removes genuinely dead work — but
**the instruction hunt is not the performance lever and should not be resourced as one.**

#### WHY TENSOR CORES CANNOT BE THE ANSWER EITHER

Mean tensor gap across the 15 is **−0.75 points**, and we are AHEAD on V1 (+0.89) and V4
(+0.20). Tensor cores execute only `wgmma`; the integer math runs on the FMA, ALU,
uniform and LSU pipes and never occupies a tensor core. It can only steal *issue slots*,
and `wgmma` is asynchronous — one issue keeps the tensor pipe busy ~16-32 cycles, which
is a large shadow. The measurements say that shadow is not being exhausted: our tensor
utilisation matches cuBLAS's.

The absolute headroom to 100% is real (V8 29.5 points, V7c 13.8) but **cuBLAS does not
capture it either** (V8: they are at 75.38%). It is prologue fill, drain and wave
quantisation, and it shrinks with K exactly as amortisation predicts:

    K = 50304 -> 99.58%      K = 16384 -> 97-98%      K = 2048 -> ~91%      K = 512 -> 70.55%

#### WHERE THE WORK ACTUALLY IS

Five of fifteen are 2.2-7.9% behind and every one of them is low-K: **V8 (512), V7c,
V8b, V6, V7 (all 2048)**. That is one mechanism, not five separate problems — fixing
amortisation moves five variants at once. The remaining ten are within 1.6% and six of
them are within 0.8%.

**V8 alone is a larger deficit than everything chased on V1 over two days**, and V1 is
our BEST shape at equal clock. The obvious first question on V8: with K=512 and BK=64
that is **8 mainloop iterations against a pipeline depth of 6** — the pipeline barely
fills before it drains.

#### §H27as OPEN TASK — `KLOOP_UNROLL`, kept as cleanup, NOT as a performance lever

cuBLAS fits **16 static HGMMA per loop body against our 4**, so every loop-carried cost
(branch, ISETP, `WARPGROUP.ARRIVE`, mbarrier wait, stage advance) is amortised 4x better
on their side. Slot 33 `_KLOOP_UNROLL` exists in the template and has never been enabled
on any shipping config.

**Do it, but for the right reason.** §H27as refuted the performance case: instruction
count anti-correlates with the deficit (r = −0.305) and the direct intervention bought
+0.58 clock points and zero cycles. So the expected gain is ~0, and it must be gated the
same way everything else is — a config ladder, one knob at a time, bit-exact validation,
and the paired null instrument.

The reasons it is still worth doing:
- it removes genuinely dead work at the source rather than by hand-patching sites, which
  is what §H27ai had to do;
- unrolling by `LOAD_PIPE_DEPTH` makes `stage` a COMPILE-TIME constant, which deletes the
  stage-advance arithmetic entirely rather than merely cheapening it (§H27ai's `cs`);
- it is the last remaining structural difference from cuBLAS in the mainloop, so leaving
  it untested keeps an open question that will otherwise be re-litigated.

**Explicitly NOT expected to help the low-K shapes.** Deeper unrolling of an 8-iteration
mainloop (V8) makes the fill/drain problem worse, not better. Those need the opposite
treatment.

### §H27at — **§H27as IS RETRACTED. Measured against REAL throughput, the instruction ratio is the best predictor we have (r = −0.511, correct sign) and the shapes doing the most excess math ARE the shapes furthest behind (93.72% vs 96.33%).** §H27as reached the opposite conclusion because it used `sm__cycles_elapsed` from ncu as the outcome — and that quantity is **uncorrelated with real throughput (r = +0.197)**.

#### THE GROUND TRUTH — real %cuB, all 15 pins, one config per process, TARGET_MS=400

`kind-data-thinks-fin-03`, CUDA 13.0, free clocks.

    var    shape                lay     ourTF    cuBLAS    %cuB       var    %cuB
    V7c    16384x512x2048       nn     652.37    656.24   99.4%       V4    96.8%
    V8b    16384x2048x2048      nt     668.40    682.56   97.9%       V7b   96.7%
    V3     16384x11264x2048     nn     643.23    660.60   97.4%       V8d   96.7%
    V8c    16384x2048x11264     nt     689.13    707.94   97.3%       V2    96.1%
    V7     16384x2048x2048      nn     664.47    684.90   97.0%       V6    95.7%
    V8     16384x2048x512       nt     551.83    576.49   95.7%       V5    95.4%
                                                                      V2b   95.2%
    mean 96.1%   sd 2.27   range 89.1 - 99.4                          V1    94.5%
                                                                      V2c   89.1%

#### THE PROXY WAS ALMOST EXACTLY INVERTED

    var    ncu cycle ratio   ncu rank      real %cuB   real rank
    V8           1.079x        1 (worst)      95.7%       6
    V1           1.003x       15 (best)       94.5%       2 (near worst)
    V2c          1.007x       12              89.1%       1 (worst)
    V7c          1.032x        2 (near worst) 99.4%      15 (best)

`sm__cycles_elapsed` is measured under profiling — serialised launches, kernel replay,
clocks pinned by ncu — and does not survive contact with a real timed run. **It must not
be used as a performance outcome again.** §H27as's "the work is on the low-K shapes, V8
is the biggest deficit, V1 is our best shape" is wrong in all three parts: V8 is
mid-pack, V1 is second-worst, and the worst shape is V2c which the proxy ranked 12th.

#### RE-TESTED AGAINST REAL THROUGHPUT

    instruction ratio  vs  real %cuB    r = -0.511     correct sign, strongest predictor
    log(K)             vs  real %cuB    r = -0.381     weak
    tensor gap         vs  real %cuB    r = -0.207     weak
    ncu cycle ratio    vs  real %cuB    r = +0.197     useless

    instr ratio >= 2.2   V1, V2, V2b, V2c    mean  93.72% of cuBLAS
    instr ratio <= 1.6   V3, V4, V5, V6      mean  96.33% of cuBLAS
                                             difference 2.6 points

Robust to the outlier: dropping V2c gives r = −0.448 on n=14.

**So the original hypothesis stands: the shapes doing the most excess integer math are
the shapes furthest behind.** The four worst-offending configs by instruction ratio are
also, on average, 2.6 points further from cuBLAS than the four cleanest.

#### RECONCILING WITH §H27am's INTERVENTION

§H27am cut V1's k-loop 24.4% and measured **+0.58 clock points**, which read as "tiny" at
the time. Against the cross-shape slope here — roughly **2.7 points of %cuB per 1.0x of
instruction ratio** (2.61 points across a 0.97 range) — a cut of 2.43x → 2.08x predicts
**+1.24 points**. Measured +0.58 on the clock channel alone, with the %cuB channel buried
under a 3.16-point free-clock noise floor. Those are consistent within a factor of two;
they are not in conflict. The intervention was real and simply smaller than the fit, not
absent.

**Full instruction parity (2.43x → 1.0x) projects to roughly +3.9 points on V1.** That is
worth having and it is the best-supported lever on the board — but it is single-digit,
and it does not reach the 130% target.

#### METHOD RULE, EARNED TWICE TODAY

§H27ak retracted a conclusion built on a power reading taken in the wrong condition;
§H27as is now retracted for a conclusion built on a cycle counter that does not track
throughput. **Correlate against measured %cuB or do not correlate at all.** Profiler
counters are for finding MECHANISM once an effect is established in real timing — never
for establishing that the effect exists.

#### ALSO SETTLED TODAY — TILE ORIENTATION IS NOT THE ANSWER

cuBLAS runs `nvjet_sm90_tst_256x128_64x4_1x2_h_bz_coopA_*` on V7c/V8/V8b/V8d — a
**256x128 tile with a 1x2 cluster**, the transpose of our 128x256 with 2x1, so their
cluster multicasts A (the large operand) where ours multicasts B. Matching them on V8:

    128x256x64_2x1_h_ep64swz128_rot2_pdl   98.2%   <- ours, best
    256x128x64_1x2_h_rs2_ep32s2            93.6%
    256x128x64_2x1_h_ep32s2_pdl            92.4%
    256x128x64_1x2_h_ep32s2                88.3%
    256x128x64_1x2_h                       83.3%
    256x128x64_1x2_h_ep64s2                83.1%

**Every 256x128 variant is worse, by 5 to 15 points.** The long-standing "tile-orientation
unknown" that §H27zdispatcher recorded as gating the cuBLAS-variant pin is answered: our
orientation is the better one here, and matching cuBLAS's would cost us.

### §H27au — **FIRST GATED WIN. Removing the dead address math on V2c's config is worth +1.95 points, paired and null-controlled, bit-exact.** 40.3% fewer k-loop instructions per wgmma (R2UR 16→1, IMAD 6→2). V2c was our worst shape at 89.1%; the full rung takes it to ~91.4%. `cs` alone buys NOTHING (−0.07) — the win is the descriptor work.

V2c (`2048x50304x16384 tn`, `256x128x64_2x1_h_ep32s2_pdl`) is the worst shape in the set
(§H27at) and carries one of the four highest instruction ratios (2.24x), which against
real %cuB is the strongest predictor available (r = −0.511). Its baseline is also worse
than V1's: **it does not set DESC_HOIST at all**, so it runs the full `make_gmma_desc_*`
rebuild on every wgmma rather than merely hoisting it.

#### STATIC — innermost HGMMA loop, cuobjdump, per wgmma

    variant                     instr/wgmma   vs base   R2UR  ULEA  IMAD
    base +dh +dw                    17.00      +9.7%      16     7     7   WORSE without uad
    base                            15.50       0.0%      16     7     6
    base +cs                        15.25      -1.6%      16     6     6
    base +dh                        13.00     -16.1%      16    7    13
    base +dh +dw +uad                9.50     -38.7%       1     5     2
    base +dh +dw +uad +ubd           9.50     -38.7%       1     5     2   ubd is a NO-OP
    base +dh +dw +uad +ubd +cs       9.25     -40.3%       1     4     2

`ubd` (UNIFORM_B_DESC) changes **nothing** on this config — 76 static instructions with
and without. `dw`+`uad` already puts B's descriptor on the uniform path here. And `dh+dw`
without `uad` is again WORSE than baseline, the same pairing as §H27ai: DESC_WALK stacks a
walk on top of a rebuild unless UNIFORM_A_DESC has folded `row0` to a literal first.

#### MEASURED — `h27zdf_paired.sh`, 15 reps, 5 arms, PIN entered twice as the null, locked 1410

    arm         mean_d    sd_d   min_d   max_d   verdict
    NULL_B       +0.37    1.00   -2.60   +1.50   <- METHOD ERROR, floor = 1.37 points
    CS           -0.07    0.89   -2.30   +0.90   nothing
    DHDWUAD      +1.45    0.82    0.00   +2.80   marginal, sits on the floor
    FULL         +1.95    1.30   -0.70   +4.50   BELIEVABLE

Net of the null's +0.37 bias, **~+1.6 points**. All seven rungs PASS with
**maxRelErr 0.00000**. Single-shot %cuB for reference: base 89.5% → full rung 91.2-91.8%
(cuBLAS's own column moved 717.59-726.49 across those runs, 1.2%, so the paired number is
the one to quote).

**`cs` alone is worth nothing.** Removing the magic-number division does not pay by
itself — consistent with §H27aj, where `cs` measured −0.10 on V1 against a 0.72 floor.
It stays because it is bit-exact and removes dead work, not because it is fast.

#### THIS ALSO APPLIES TO V2 AND V2b

Both pin the same `256x128x64_2x1_h_ep32s2_pdl` config (V2 96.1%, V2b 95.2%). The rung is
registered for the config, not the shape, so both should carry the same benefit. **Not yet
measured on them** — that is the next gate before any dispatcher change.

#### WHAT DEAD WORK REMAINS — read straight off the best rung's SASS

The winning rung still **rebuilds** the descriptor base every k-iteration instead of
carrying it. From the 74-instruction loop body:

```
S2UR   UR23, SR_CgaCtaId        <- cluster CTA id re-read EVERY iteration, loop-invariant
UIMAD  UR8, UR4, 0xc000         <- stage * 49152 as a MULTIPLY, every iteration
ULEA   UR9, UR23, UR8, 0x18     <- the remaining ULEA lives here
ULOP3 / USHF / ULOP3 / USHF / UIADD3.X ...   <- ~18 instructions rebuilding both bases
```

then the useful part — eight `UIADD3.64` walking the per-wgmma offsets, which is exactly
cuBLAS's shape. **We perform their walk, but rebuild the base first; cuBLAS carries the
base in a register and rewinds it at the bottom of the group.**

Remaining, in size order:

| # | dead work | cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | descriptor base REBUILT per iteration instead of accumulated (`+= copy_size>>4`, rewind on wrap) | ~18 instr |
| B | `stage * copy_size` via multiply + sign-extend chain | ~4 instr |
| C | `S2UR SR_CgaCtaId` re-read though loop-invariant | 1-2 instr |
| D | phase flip on the VECTOR path (`ISETP`/`SEL`/`LOP3` on R7/R12) | 3 instr |

A, B and C are one change: keep the descriptor base live across iterations. That is the
last structural difference from cuBLAS's mainloop and the natural next knob (`DESC_ACCUM`).

### §H27aw — **DEAD-WORK SWEEP COMPLETE ACROSS ALL 15 PINS. Every rung is bit-exact (maxRelErr 0.00000, 50+ runs). The answer is DIFFERENT for every tile — there is no universal setting.** 256x128 takes the full stack (+1.95 paired, believable); 128x256 takes `dh` ONLY (+0.37% mean, 7/7 shapes, sign-test p = 0.016) and REGRESSES on the deeper walk; 192x192 needs nothing (already `R2UR 0`); 128x128 already regressed on `dw_uad` (−7.33).

#### THE FOUR FAMILIES, AND WHY ONE ANSWER DOES NOT FIT THEM

| family | pins | had | verdict | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `256x128` | V2, V2b, V2c | nothing | **adopt `dh_dw_uad_ubd_cs`** | **+1.95 paired (believable)**, 3/3 single-shot |
| `128x256` | V7, V7b, V7c, V8, V8b, V8c, V8d | nothing | **adopt `dh` ONLY** | **+0.37% mean, 7/7, p = 0.016** |
| `192x192` | V3, V4, V5, V6 | dh dw ubd | **no change** | `uad` is a byte-identical no-op |
| `128x128` | V1 | dh | **no change** | `dw_uad` = −7.33 (§H27aj) |

#### 128x256 — SEVEN PINS, AND THE DEEPER WALK IS A REGRESSION

    shape        _dh      _dh_dw_uad   _dh_dw_uad_ubd   _dh_dw_uad_ubd_cs
    V7        +0.73%        -1.12%          -1.05%           -0.70%
    V7b       +0.56%        +0.96%          +0.86%           +1.56%
    V7c       +0.15%        -0.80%          -0.99%           -0.95%
    V8        +0.35%        -0.21%          -0.94%           -0.31%
    V8b       +0.19%        -1.51%          -1.43%           -1.18%
    V8c       +0.49%        +1.20%          +0.97%           +0.80%
    V8d       +0.14%        -0.75%          -0.50%           -0.31%
    mean      +0.37%        -0.32%          -0.44%           -0.16%
    wins         7/7           2/7             2/7              2/7

**`dh` alone is positive on every one of the seven shapes.** Each delta is far below the
1.37-point paired floor measured on V2c, so no single-shape paired test could resolve it —
but **7/7 in the same direction across INDEPENDENT shapes is a two-sided sign test at
p = 0.016.** That is the correct instrument for a sub-floor effect and it is why the
result is claimable at all.

The deeper rungs REMOVE MORE INSTRUCTIONS (−23.5% vs −17.3% static) and go BACKWARDS
(2/7). Instruction count is not monotone with performance on this tile.

#### 256x128 — THREE PINS, THE FULL STACK PAYS

    shape        base TF   _dh_dw_uad   _dh_dw_uad_ubd_cs
    V2            696.82      +0.94%           +0.48%
    V2b           641.09      +0.41%           +1.59%
    V2c           645.85      +2.45%           +0.96%
    mean                      +1.27% (3/3)     +1.01% (3/3)

Both rungs win on all three. The paired null-controlled run on V2c (§H27au) is the
tie-break and it favours the full stack: **FULL +1.95 (believable) vs DHDWUAD +1.45
(marginal, sitting on the 1.37 floor)**. Adopt `dh_dw_uad_ubd_cs`.

#### 192x192 — NOTHING TO DO, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED

A `_uad` twin of each of the three 192x192 configs compiled to a **byte-identical k-loop**:
102 static instructions, 12 wgmma, **8.50 per wgmma, R2UR 0 / ULEA 6 / IMAD 0** with and
without. `ubd` already puts both descriptors on the uniform datapath at this tile. The
three twins were deleted rather than shipped as dead configs.

At **8.50 instructions per wgmma this family has the cleanest mainloop in the set** — and
it also refutes the prediction that V3/V4/V5/V6 were sitting in the bad dw-without-uad
state seen on V1 and V2c. They were not.

#### THE GENERAL LESSON

The same five knobs produce four different verdicts on four tiles. `dw` requires `uad` on
128x128 and 256x128 but is a **regression even with it** on 128x256; `ubd` is essential on
192x192, a no-op on 256x128, and irrelevant on 128x256; `cs` is worth nothing anywhere
(−0.07 V2c, −0.10 V1) yet is kept because it is bit-exact dead-work removal. **Every tile
must be measured; nothing generalises.**

#### ADOPTION POLICY IN FORCE (user directive, 2026-08-27)

*"If you remove redundant instructions or dead work and it is correct with no precision
issues, keep it even if performance is not what we expected — you removed something
unwanted anyway."*

Applied as: **keep if bit-exact AND not a measured regression.** `cs` qualifies at zero
gain and stays. `dw_uad` on 128x128 (−7.33) and on 128x256 (2/7, mean −0.32%) does not,
and stays out.

#### EXPECTED EFFECT OF ADOPTION, all bit-exact

    V2    95.1% -> ~95.8%      V7  97.6% -> ~98.3%      V8b 97.8% -> ~98.0%
    V2b   94.1% -> ~96.2%      V7b 95.4% -> ~96.2%      V8c 96.4% -> ~96.9%
    V2c   89.1% -> ~91.4%      V7c 95.0% -> ~98.3%      V8d 97.3% -> ~97.4%
                               V8  95.3% -> ~94.6%
    V1, V3, V4, V5, V6 unchanged.   Set mean 96.1% -> roughly 96.7%.

Not yet applied to `Bgemm_sm90_dispatch_table.h` — the pin change is a separate, gated step.
