### §H27ax — **WE HAVE BEEN COUNTING THE WRONG THING ALL SESSION. Our UNIFORM instruction count is already at PARITY with cuBLAS (1.16-1.36x, r = +0.061 against real %cuB — no relationship). The entire excess is VECTOR: 2.35-3.67x, r = −0.642, the best predictor found.** A vector op drives 32 lanes where a uniform op drives one, so total-instruction counting weights them equally when they differ ~32x in switching cost.

This is not a new discovery — it is written in the template at slot 34 (§H27zm) and I did not
find it until now:

> *"Our UNIFORM instruction count already MATCHES cuBLAS (216.2M vs 215.6M, 1.0023); the
> entire excess is VECTOR, 578.5M vs 181.6M, and a vector op drives 32 lanes where a uniform
> op drives one — **which is why three instruction-count cuts moved the clock 0.0** while the
> vector share stayed put."*

Re-deriving it from today's §H27ao census against today's real %cuB (§H27at):

    var     total x   uniform x   VECTOR x   real %cuB
    V1        2.54x       1.36x      3.67x       94.5%
    V2c       2.24x       1.17x      3.30x       89.1%
    V7        1.81x       1.16x      2.35x       97.0%
    V8d       1.78x       1.19x      2.35x       96.7%

    total instructions   vs real %cuB   r = -0.545
    UNIFORM instructions vs real %cuB   r = +0.061      <- NO relationship
    VECTOR  instructions vs real %cuB   r = -0.642      <- the metric

**`smsp__inst_executed` must be decomposed before it is used.** Uniform ratio spans
1.16-1.36 across shapes — essentially parity — while VECTOR spans 2.35-3.67. Every
conclusion drawn from the total is diluted by a term that carries no signal.

**This retro-explains the session.** §H27am's cut bought +0.58 clock points; §H27au's V2c
stack bought +1.95. The difference is what each removed: V2c's took **R2UR 16 → 1**, and
R2UR *is* the vector→uniform crossing, so that cut removed VECTOR work. Cuts that shuffled
uniform arithmetic moved nothing.

#### CONSEQUENCE 1 — THE HUNT'S TARGET CHANGES

Stop optimising `smsp__inst_executed`. Target **vector-datapath instructions**: `IMAD`,
`IADD3`, `LOP3`, `SHF`, `ISETP`, `SEL`, `LEA` and every `R2UR` that marks a value born on
the wrong datapath. The census must report `total`, `uniform` and `total − uniform`
separately from now on.

#### CONSEQUENCE 2 — `KLOOP_UNROLL` IS THE DESIGNED FIX, AND §H27as's PARKING NOTE WAS WRONG

The remaining dead work identified in §H27au — the per-iteration descriptor rebuild
(`S2UR SR_CgaCtaId`, `UIMAD stage*copy_size`, ~18 instructions of mask/shift/OR/sign-extend)
— is *exactly* what slot 33 was written for:

> *"dw's expression `a_desc_tile + ((st*copy_size)>>4)` is already optimal WHEN st is
> constant — it folds to one UIADD3, **which is cuBLAS's whole descriptor cost**. The only
> defect is that st is runtime, which also forces the mod-3 magic divide and the stage*8
> barrier offset. STAGE_SPECIALISE had the right goal but resolved st with a RUNTIME
> if-chain, paying more than the literal saved: **+30.7% executed instructions**. Unrolling
> gives the same literals with no dispatch and no carried state."*

Three consequences:
- **A `DESC_ACCUM` carried-state knob should NOT be written.** It is the third form of an
  idea already measured to backfire (STAGE_SPECIALISE, +30.7%). Unrolling is the form that
  works because it needs neither dispatch nor carried state.
- **§H27as's note parking KLOOP_UNROLL as "cleanup only, expect ~0" is withdrawn.** That was
  written when the performance case rested on total instruction count. Making `stage` a
  compile-time literal removes the multiply, the modulo AND the barrier-offset multiply, and
  those are vector-datapath costs.
- It remains true that unrolling an 8-iteration mainloop (V8, K=512) will not help; the
  template already notes the loop must align to the ring first, at most D−1 runtime
  iterations, then run literal bodies, then a residue.

**NEXT: enable `_KLOOP_UNROLL` on the 256x128 and 128x256 families and measure it with the
vector/uniform split reported, not the total.**

### §H27ay — **`KLOOP_UNROLL` IS REFUTED, AND THE VECTOR MODEL PREDICTED IT.** Unrolling cuts TOTAL instructions 6.8% and raises VECTOR instructions **36%** — it moves work off the uniform datapath onto the vector one. Performance follows VECTOR: flat (654.21 vs 654.14), and unroll-without-`dw` is **−14%**. §H27ax's metric made an out-of-sample call it could have failed.

§H27ax argued the excess is VECTOR, not total, and §H27ax's consequence 2 named
`KLOOP_UNROLL` as the designed fix for the remaining descriptor rebuild. That second claim
is now tested and **wrong**, by the metric from the first claim.

`192x192x64_1x2_v_rs8`, shape `2048x11264x16384 tn`, one config per process:

    config                  ourTF    %cuB      total       uniform       VECTOR
    dh_ubd_dw_skew_lsw     654.14   95.0%   161,497,515   78,653,388   82,844,127
    dh_ubd_dwunr_skew_lsw  654.21   94.6%   150,481,284   37,690,092  112,791,192
    dh_ubd_unr_skew_lsw    562.85   81.6%   166,941,675   53,657,868  113,283,807

                            total      uniform      VECTOR     %cuB
    +unroll (on top of dw)  -6.8%       -52.1%      +36.1%     flat
    +unroll (without dw)    +3.4%       -31.8%      +36.7%     -13.4 points

**Unrolling halves the uniform count and inflates the vector count by a third.** Making
`stage` a compile-time literal does remove the multiply, the modulo and the barrier-offset
arithmetic — all of which were UNIFORM ops, the cheap kind — while the D literal bodies
apparently expand vector-datapath work. Net: the metric that carries no signal improves,
the metric that predicts performance gets worse, and performance is flat.

**THIS IS THE VALIDATION OF §H27ax.** Total instructions said the change was good (−6.8%);
vector said it was bad (+36%); the hardware agreed with vector. Had we still been judging by
`smsp__inst_executed.sum` — as the template comment beside these very configs instructs
("judge these by smsp__inst_executed.sum first (exact, noise-free), %cuB second") — we would
have adopted a change worth nothing and then extended it to ten more pins.

#### CONSEQUENCES

- **Do NOT extend `KLOOP_UNROLL` to the non-SKEW mainloop.** That work is cancelled; it
  would have been the largest implementation task on the board (256x128 and 128x256 = ten of
  fifteen pins) for a change that worsens the governing metric.
- **§H27ax's consequence 2 is withdrawn.** The parking note on §H27as was right for the
  wrong reason: KLOOP_UNROLL is indeed not a lever, though not because instruction count is
  irrelevant — because it raises VECTOR count.
- **`DESC_ACCUM` stays unwritten**, now for a second independent reason. Both remaining
  forms of "make the stage term cheap" — carried state (STAGE_SPECIALISE, +30.7%) and
  literal bodies (KLOOP_UNROLL, +36% vector) — have now been measured and both fail.
- **The per-iteration descriptor rebuild stays.** It is ~18 instructions, but they are
  UNIFORM ones (`UIMAD`/`ULOP3`/`USHF`/`UIADD3`), which the correlation says do not cost
  performance. §H27au's remaining-dead-work list was ranked by instruction count and is
  re-ranked by this: items A, B and C are all uniform-datapath and are NOT worth chasing.
  Item D — the phase flip on the VECTOR path (`ISETP`/`SEL`/`LOP3` on R7/R12) — is the only
  one that targets the right datapath, and it is 3 instructions.

#### WHERE THE VECTOR EXCESS ACTUALLY IS

With uniform at parity and vector at 2.35-3.67x, the hunt should now enumerate VECTOR ops in
the mainloop and ask of each: why is this per-thread? The known answer for the biggest one is
already recorded at slot 34 (§H27zm) — on SPLIT_M tiles `row0 = g * WG_MATOMS * 64` with `g`
runtime lands `LEA / LOP3 / SHF / VIADD` on the vector path and then `R2UR` back, and that is
what `UNIFORM_A_DESC` fixes. It affects **ten of fifteen pins** (256x128 x3, 128x256 x7),
which is consistent with §H27au measuring +1.95 on V2c where `uad` took R2UR 16 -> 1.

### §H27az — **THE VECTOR CENSUS. Every k-loop instruction classified by datapath, all rungs. `vec/wgmma` explains every result of the day.** 192x192 runs at **0.58**, 256x128+uad at **1.62**, and the 128x256 family — SEVEN pins — is stuck at **7.00**, a 12x gap. Two concrete mechanisms found: ptxas computes the descriptor chain on BOTH datapaths and feeds the tensor core from the VECTOR copy; and on 128x256 `uad` flips `S2UR` to `S2R`, moving the whole chain to the vector path.

Instructions are classified as UNIFORM (`U`-prefixed, one lane per warp), VECTOR (per-thread,
32 lanes), or crossings (`R2UR`/`S2UR`, charged to VECTOR since the value was born on the
wrong side). Static, innermost HGMMA loop, `cuobjdump`.

    config                              body  wgmma  VECTOR  uniform   vec/wgmma   measured
    192x192  dh dw ubd                   102     12       7       69      0.58      cleanest family
    256x128  +dh +dw +uad (+ubd)(+cs)     74      8      13       39      1.62      +1.95  WIN
    256x128  +dh                         104      8      54       29      6.75
    256x128  base                        124      8      62       41      7.75
    256x128  +dh +dw   (no uad)          136      8      63       52      7.88      worse
    128x256  +dh +dw +uad +ubd +cs        74      4      26       27      6.50      -0.16%
    128x256  +dh                          81      4      28       34      7.00      +0.37%  WIN
    128x256  base                         98      4      37       43      9.25
    128x256  +dh +dw +uad                 75      4      45       10     11.25      -0.32%  worse

**`vec/wgmma` predicts every measured outcome.** `uad` on 256x128 takes it 7.88 -> 1.62 and
won +1.95; the identical knob on 128x256 takes it 9.25 -> **11.25** and regressed. That is why
one knob behaved oppositely on two tiles, and total instruction count could never have
explained it (256x128 −38.7% and 128x256 −23.5%, both "improvements").

#### MECHANISM 1 — ptxas COMPUTES THE DESCRIPTOR TWICE AND USES THE VECTOR COPY

From `128x256 +dh`, the winning rung, these appear as adjacent pairs:

```
>> LOP3.LUT  R4,   R4,  0x3fc00, RZ,  0xc0      <- VECTOR
   ULOP3.LUT UR4,  UR4, 0x3fc00, URZ, 0xc0      <- UNIFORM, same operation
>> SHF.R.U32.HI  R4,  RZ,  0x4, R4              <- VECTOR
   USHF.R.U32.HI UR4, URZ, 0x4, UR4             <- UNIFORM, same
>> LOP3.LUT  R18,  R4,  0x10000, RZ,  0xfc      <- VECTOR
   ULOP3.LUT UR26, UR4, 0x10000, URZ, 0xfc      <- UNIFORM, same
>X R2UR UR24, R18                                <- HGMMA is fed from the VECTOR copy
```

repeated for all four k-step offsets (`0x10000/2/4/6`). **The uniform results (`UR26`) are
computed and never consumed.** Cost per body: ~8 vector ops + 8 `R2UR` crossings + 8 dead
uniform ops.

The trigger is visible two lines up:

```
>> IMAD.U32 R5, RZ, RZ, UR10    <- copies a UNIFORM register INTO a vector register
>> LEA      R4, R3, UR4, 0xd    <- R3 is per-thread and poisons the chain
```

`R3` is the warpgroup index `g` — exactly what slot 34 (§H27zm) recorded on the 256x128 tile
as `LEA R11, R3, UR16, 0xe` (shift differs because WG_MATOMS differs). `row0 = g*WG_MATOMS*64`
with runtime `g` is the single per-thread value that drags the whole descriptor chain onto the
vector datapath.

#### MECHANISM 2 — ON 128x256, `uad` FLIPS THE DATAPATH THE WRONG WAY

The first instruction of the loop, same tile, two rungs:

    +dh            S2UR UR24, SR_CgaCtaId      cluster id -> UNIFORM register
    +dh +dw +uad   S2R  R21,  SR_CgaCtaId      cluster id -> VECTOR register

With `uad` on, ptxas reads the cluster CTA id into a vector register and then runs **the
entire** address chain per-thread — every address computation, the mbarrier addressing, the
`PRMT`, the arrive addresses. The uniform count collapses 34 -> 10 while vector rises 28 -> 45.

`uad` folds `row0` to a literal and specialises the mainloop per warpgroup (two copies).
On 256x128 that lets the chain go uniform and R2UR drops 16 -> 1. On 128x256 the same change
makes ptxas abandon the uniform datapath entirely. **The knob's effect is a ptxas scheduling
decision, not a property of our source**, which is why it cannot be predicted from the source
and must be read out of SASS per tile.

#### WHAT THIS MAKES THE NEXT TARGET

The 128x256 family is **seven of fifteen pins at 7.00 vec/wgmma against 192x192's 0.58**. The
prize is real: if that family reached even 256x128's post-`uad` 1.62, it would be the largest
single improvement available. But the two obvious routes are both closed —
`uad` flips the datapath (mechanism 2) and `dw` needs `uad`.

The open question is therefore narrow and concrete: **how do we make `g` warp-uniform to ptxas
on this tile without triggering the S2R flip?** `g` is warp-uniform in VALUE (it is
`threadIdx.x / 128`) but ptxas cannot prove it, and `uad`'s way of telling it — folding to a
literal via per-warpgroup specialisation — costs more than it saves here.

Note also that `192x192` gets **12 wgmma per loop body against 128x256's 4**, so it amortises
whatever per-body cost remains 3x better. Part of the 12x gap is the numerator and part is the
denominator.

---

### §H27b0 — **`UNIFORM_A_SHFL`: one line, VECTOR ops cut 4x on the BM=128 tiles, +1.08% measured on 7 of 15 pins, bit-exact.** A warp broadcast tells ptxas `row0` is uniform without duplicating the mainloop — succeeding exactly where `UNIFORM_A_DESC` backfires.

#### THE GAP IT FILLS

§H27az established that on a SPLIT_M tile `row0 = g*WG_MATOMS*64` is the single per-thread
value that drags A's whole descriptor chain onto the vector datapath, and that
`UNIFORM_A_DESC` fixes it by folding `row0` to a literal — which requires instantiating the
mainloop once per warpgroup. That pays on 256x128 (BM=256, 8 wgmma/body): vec/wgmma
7.88 -> 1.62, **+1.95 paired**. On the BM=128 tiles it backfires: ptxas reads the cluster id
with `S2R` instead of `S2UR` and moves the entire chain per-thread, 7.00 -> **11.25**, −0.32%.

`row0` is warp-uniform in VALUE — it derives from `threadIdx.x/128` — but ptxas's divergence
analysis cannot prove it. A warp broadcast states the fact directly (the CUTLASS
`canonical_warp_group_idx` idiom), with no duplicated mainloop and no literal folding:

```c
row0_eff = __shfl_sync(0xffffffffu, row0, 0)
```

Guarded mutually exclusive with `UNIFORM_A_DESC` by static_assert — two ways to say the same
thing; enabling both is meaningless.

#### STATIC — the vector density collapses

    config                 body  wgmma  VECTOR  uniform   vec/wgmma
    128x256 +dh              78      4      28       31      7.00
    128x256 +dh +shfl        69      4       7       42      1.75    -75%
    128x128 +dh (V1)         78      4      33       28      8.25
    128x128 +dh +shfl        61      4       8       36      2.00    -76%

Eight of fifteen pins move from the worst vector density in the set into the same class as
256x128's tuned 1.62, against 192x192's 0.58 reference.

#### MEASURED — two independent passes, all bit-exact (maxRelErr 0.00000)

    shape     pass1    pass2     mean
    V7       +1.09%   +0.37%   +0.73%
    V7b      +0.71%   +0.95%   +0.83%
    V7c      -0.47%   +2.57%   +1.05%
    V8       +0.84%   -0.11%   +0.36%
    V8b      +0.21%   +1.51%   +0.86%
    V8c      +0.60%   +0.57%   +0.58%
    V8d      +1.17%   -0.02%   +0.57%
    mean     +0.59%   +0.83%   +0.71%

    per-shape means : 7/7 positive, sign-test p = 0.016
    all 14 observations : 11/14 positive, p = 0.057
    overall +0.71%, sd 0.76, sem 0.20

The +0.71% sits below the 1.37-point paired floor, so the sign test across independent
shapes is again the correct instrument; a single-shape paired run could not resolve it.
Note V7c swings −0.47% to +2.57% between passes — single-shot free-clock noise on one shape
is ~3 points, which is exactly why per-shape single observations are not claimable and the
averaged 7/7 is.

**On top of `dh` (+0.37%, §H27aw) the family gains +1.08% against its original pin.**

#### V1 IS NOT SETTLED

`128x128 +shfl` shows the same static collapse (8.25 -> 2.00) but measured **−0.93%** in one
pass. V1's single-shot spread today has been 94.5 / 97.0 / 98.5%, so that is inside noise and
one observation decides nothing. Needs a second pass before any conclusion.

#### THE STANDING PICTURE

    family    pins   vec/wgmma   state
    192x192      4       0.58    optimal, nothing to do
    256x128      3       1.62    done, +1.95 paired  (via uad)
    128x256      7       1.75    done, +1.08 total   (via dh + shfl)
    128x128      1       2.00    static win, perf unresolved

**All four families are now within 0.58-2.00 vec/wgmma**, from a starting spread of
0.58-9.25. The remaining question is whether anything below ~1.6 is reachable, and 192x192
suggests it is — but 192x192 also gets 12 wgmma per loop body against the others' 4-8, so
part of its advantage is the denominator, not the numerator.

#### HONEST ACCOUNTING OF TODAY'S GAIN

Raw before/after is **96.06% -> 97.02%, +0.96 points**. But the four 192x192 pins whose
config was **not touched** moved **+0.47** on their own, which is pure measurement drift.
Drift-corrected: **+0.48 points**. The directly-measured A/B gains weight to +0.89. The truth
is **+0.5 to +0.9 points**, and the A/B numbers are the trustworthy ones because they were
paired or repeated within a session.

**This does not reach the 105-109% target.** At free clocks we are at 97%; at equal clock 99%.
One shape (V1) exceeds 105% at equal clock; the mean does not.

#### WHAT THE HUNT ACTUALLY ACHIEVED

Vector density across the pinned set went from **0.58-9.25** to **0.58-2.00** vec/wgmma. Every
family is now within ~3.5x of the best. That is the instruction excess substantially removed,
and it bought +0.5 to +0.9 points. **The remaining gap is therefore NOT instructions**, which
is itself the useful conclusion: further instruction work has a small ceiling.

- **V2c at 91.6% LOCKED** is the only shape with a large non-clock deficit — 7.5 points below
  the set mean at equal clock. It is `2048x50304x16384`, the widest-N shape. Whatever is wrong
  there is not instruction count and not clock. This is the single best-defined open target.
- The **~2.1-point clock deficit** across the set (§H27ag mechanism, §H27am measured the
  instruction channel at only 1.66%/1.0x).
- `UNIFORM_A_SHFL` should be considered for the remaining unpinned configs in the tree; it was
  only applied to the four pinned families.

### §H27b2 — **TILE AND RASTER ARE COUPLED, AND V2c's 8-POINT DEFICIT IS A TILE-SHAPE PROBLEM, NOT AN INSTRUCTION ONE. `128x256/2x1/v + dh + shfl` takes V2c from 89.7% to 96.9% at locked clock — +7.2 points, bit-exact.** Neutral on V2 (−0.2) and slightly negative on V2b (−0.45), so it is a per-shape pin, not a config-wide change. **This also corrects §H27aw.**

§H27b1 left V2c as the one shape with a large deficit that was neither clock nor instructions:
91.6% at locked 1400 against a set mean of 99.1%. ncu on that shape:

    arm      kernel                                          DRAM      L2 hit   tensor
    ours     256x128 tile, 2x1 cluster, raster h            7.765 GB   63.49%   98.52%
    cuBLAS   nvjet_sm90_tst_128x256_64x4_2x1_v_bz_coopA_NTN  6.807 GB   60.76%   98.90%

**cuBLAS runs the TRANSPOSED tile with VERTICAL raster and moves 1.14x fewer bytes at equal
tensor utilisation.** On `2048x50304x16384` — tiny M, enormous N — the raster direction decides
which operand stays resident in L2.

#### THE COUPLING, measured at locked 1400 on V2c

    config                                     tile/raster     %cuB
    256x128x64_2x1_h_ep32s2_pdl_dh_dw_uad_ubd_cs   256x128/h    92.4%   <- the pin
    256x128x64_2x1_v_ep32s2                        256x128/v    93.0%   raster alone: +0.6
    128x256x64_2x1_h_ep64swz128_rot2_pdl_dh_shfl   128x256/h    82.9%   tile alone: -9.5 (!)
    128x256x64_2x1_v                               128x256/v    94.0%   together: +1.6
    128x256x64_2x1_v_ep32s2                        128x256/v    94.6%   + matching epilogue

**The transposed tile is catastrophic with `h` raster and our best result with `v`.** Neither
knob is meaningful alone; they must move together.

**§H27aw is corrected.** Its conclusion "tile orientation is not the answer — every 256x128
variant is 5-15 points worse" tested 256x128 arms against a 128x256 pin **without pairing the
raster**, so it compared mismatched (tile, raster) combinations and concluded the tile was at
fault. The real finding is that the PAIR matters.

With V2c moved, the locked-clock mean goes **99.12% -> ~99.4%**, and the worst shape in the

    var           our pin              cuBLAS chooses          mismatch        locked %
    V1     128x128 2x1 v        128x128 1x2 h bz splitK      cluster+raster    104.4  (we lead)
    V2     256x128 2x1 h        128x256 2x1 v coopA          tile+raster       100.1
    V2b    256x128 2x1 h        128x256 2x1 v coopA          tile+raster        99.8
    V2c    256x128 2x1 h        128x256 2x1 v coopA          tile+raster        91.6  -> 96.9 FIXED
    V3     192x192 2x1 h        192x192 1x2 h coopB          cluster            98.6
    V4     192x192 2x1 h        192x192 2x1 v coopB          raster only        98.0
    V5     192x192 1x2 v        192x192 2x1 v coopB          cluster           100.2
    V6     192x192 2x1 h        192x192 2x1 v coopB          raster only        98.5
    V7/b/c 128x256 2x1 h        256x128 1x2 h coopA          tile+cluster    97.6-100.6
    V8/b/c/d 128x256 2x1 h      256x128 1x2 h coopA          tile+cluster    97.6-100.1

**Only V2c was badly wrong.** Everything else is within ~2 points of parity at equal clock,
and two shapes (V1 at 104.4, V7c at 100.6) beat cuBLAS while running a DIFFERENT shape to it.

#### MATCHING cuBLAS IS NOT A RULE — three outcomes from the same experiment

Tested at locked 1400, two passes each:

    V2c   match cuBLAS's (128x256, v)              89.7% -> 96.9%    +7.2   MATCHING WINS
    V4    match cuBLAS's raster v                  98.4% -> 96.8%    -1.7   MATCHING LOSES
    V6    match cuBLAS's raster v                  98.6% -> 98.4%    -0.2   no effect
    V3    switch to v, which cuBLAS does NOT use   98.5% -> 99.2%    +0.9   NON-MATCHING WINS

*(the v-raster arm lacks `pdl`, and `wlsm` on V6, so V4/V6 are confounded against their pins;
V3's gain is despite that handicap, which makes it the more solid of the three.)*

The V7/V8 family was already tested against cuBLAS's (256x128, 1x2) on V8 in §H27aw:
`256x128x64_1x2_h_ep32s2` 88.3%, `256x128x64_1x2_h` 83.3%, against our 128x256 pin at 98.2%.
**Matching cuBLAS there costs 10-15 points.** Seven pins confirmed better off as they are.

#### THE STANDING CONCLUSION

Tile/cluster/raster selection is a real lever — it is worth **+7.2 points on V2c** — but it is
**per-shape and empirical**. cuBLAS's choice is a hypothesis worth testing, not an answer to
copy: it wins on one shape, loses on another, and is beaten by a third option on a third.
Any future sweep must measure each (shape, tile, cluster, raster) combination rather than
infer from cuBLAS's dispatch.

#### PINNING DECISIONS OUTSTANDING (none applied; dispatch table untouched)

    V2c   -> 128x256x64_2x1_v_ep32s2_dh_shfl              +7.2 points, bit-exact
    7 pins-> 128x256x64_2x1_h_ep64swz128_rot2_pdl_dh_shfl  +1.08%, 7/7, p=0.016
    V2,V2b-> 256x128x64_2x1_h_ep32s2_pdl_dh_dw_uad_ubd_cs  +1.95 paired
    V1    -> 128x128x64_2x1_v_sk2_dh_rot2_pdl_d6_shfl      ~0 perf, 76% vector-op cut
    V3    -> a v-raster + pdl config does not exist yet    ~+0.9 indicated

### §H27b4 — **THE CLOCK DEFICIT IS SOLVED, AND IT IS NOT INSTRUCTIONS. At equal clock BELOW the cap we draw 1.11-1.13x cuBLAS's power. Removing 76% of the k-loop vector ops recovers only 2.1% of it.** The chain is now measured end to end: **+12% power -> 100% cap saturation (vs cuBLAS's 47.7%) -> −108 MHz -> the free-clock deficit.** The leading remaining suspect is **L2 request volume at 1.85x** with DRAM bytes at parity.

Three prior attempts to measure power at equal clock failed on `plain-fish-falls-fin-03`
(§H27ap). Two sampling faults had to be fixed first: `power.draw` is a **2.4 s trailing
average** (`nvidia-smi -q -d POWER` reports "Power Samples: Duration 2.36 sec"), and 100 Hz
sampling of `power.draw.instant` **aliases**. The working protocol is **30 s windows** (so the
lagging sensor settles INSIDE each arm's window), **8 s discarded**, **2 Hz sampling**,
persistence mode forced, and a clock lock low enough that BOTH arms stay under the cap.

#### THE MEASUREMENT — V1, `kind-data-thinks-fin-03`, settled, unclamped

    lock   cuBLAS W   ours W   ratio    cap% (ours/cuB)   achieved clock
    1000       427      472    1.11x       0% /  0%       1005 / 1005
    1200       540      612    1.13x       0% /  0%       1200 / 1200
    1400       696      698    1.00x     100% / 47.7%     1301 / 1409

**At equal clock, below the cap, we draw 11-13% more power.** The 1400 row is the consequence
in one line: we saturate the 700 W cap on **100%** of samples where cuBLAS saturates on 47.7%,
so the governor takes **108 MHz (7.7%)** from us and none from them. The 1.00x power ratio at
1400 is the CLAMP, not parity — which is exactly why every free-clock power comparison this
week read 1.00x and taught us nothing (§H27ag, §H27am).

#### AND IT IS NOT THE INSTRUCTIONS — the decisive control

`_shfl` cuts V1's k-loop vector ops from **8.25 to 2.00 per wgmma** (§H27b0), a 76% removal.
Same protocol, lock 1200:

    arm                      cuBLAS W   ours W   ratio
    V1 (old config)              540      621    1.15x
    V1 + shfl (vec 8.25->2.00)   540      608    1.13x

cuBLAS reads 540 W in both — a clean control. **The 76% vector-op cut bought 13 W = 2.1% of
power, and 87% of the excess survives.** The k-loop address arithmetic is NOT what burns the
12%.

This closes the instruction track honestly and completely. §H27am measured its performance
channel at +0.58 clock points; this measures its POWER channel at 2.1%; §H27b1 measured its
total worth at +0.5-0.9 points. Three independent measurements, all small, all consistent.

#### WHERE THE POWER ACTUALLY GOES — the one counter still far from parity

From the §H27ao census on V1, with DRAM at parity:

    dram__bytes.sum        ours   88,456,448    cuBLAS   88,378,624    1.00x
    lts__t_requests.sum    ours    4,405,890    cuBLAS    2,384,607    1.85x
    lts__t_sectors.sum     ours   14,862,825    cuBLAS    8,345,518    1.78x
    l1tex shared wavefronts                                            0.98x
    tensor cycles                                                      1.00x

**We issue 1.85x the L2 requests while moving identical DRAM bytes.** Sectors-per-request are
comparable (3.37 vs 3.50), so it is not a granularity problem — we simply go to L2 nearly
twice as often for the same data, and our L2 hit rate is correspondingly higher (69.8% vs
49.5%). L2 traffic is energy-expensive and it is the only major counter left at ~2x.

**NEXT CAMPAIGN: why do we make 1.85x the L2 requests for the same bytes?** That is now the
best-defined open question in the project, and unlike the instruction hunt it has a measured
power excess of ~12% behind it, worth roughly 8 points of clock.

### §H27b5 — **THE L2 EXCESS IS ENTIRELY ON THE READ PATH, AND THE CLUSTER-AXIS HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED.** Writes match cuBLAS to the sector, DRAM reads match to 56 sectors out of 2.6M, and reads are **1.24-1.62x**. Switching to cuBLAS's cluster axis makes us WORSE. The signature points at **coopA/coopB — cooperative tile loading across the cluster — which we have never implemented.**

#### READ vs WRITE — the write path is exonerated completely

    shape   L2 writes (ours / cuBLAS)      L2 reads (ours / cuBLAS)        DRAM reads
    V1        393,289 /   393,291  =1.000    12,776,156 /  7,882,457 =1.62   2,622,272 / 2,622,216
    V7      3,146,082 / 3,146,017  =1.000    36,122,548 / 29,163,296 =1.24   2,663,800 / 2,526,024
    V8b     3,145,922 / 3,145,908  =1.000    36,299,954 / 29,219,361 =1.24   2,686,032 / 2,541,608

**Writes are identical to the sector** on all three — the epilogue, the C store path and
split-K's partial traffic are all exactly cuBLAS's. **DRAM reads are identical too** (V1
differs by 56 sectors in 2.6 million). The entire excess is L2 READS: we pull the same bytes
out of L2 far more often than cuBLAS does.

#### THE CLUSTER-AXIS HYPOTHESIS, TESTED AND REFUTED

The natural explanation was multicast operand choice. Our 2x1 cluster spans M, so the two CTAs
share N and B is multicast; cuBLAS's 1x2 spans N, so they share M and A is multicast. On V1
A is 67 MB and B is 17 MB, so cuBLAS would be multicasting the operand 4x larger. Tested on
V1's shape, same tile, only the cluster axis and raster varying:

    config              cluster   L2 read sectors   DRAM read   L2rd per DRAMrd
    128x128x64_2x1_v      2x1        10,676,964     2,622,360        4.07   <- our best
    128x128x64_1x2_h      1x2        12,929,942     2,622,400        4.93
    128x128x64_1x2_v      1x2        13,738,888     2,622,352        5.24
    128x128x64_2x1_h      2x1        15,240,327     2,622,344        5.81
    cuBLAS (128x128 1x2)  1x2         7,882,457     2,622,216        3.01

**Switching to cuBLAS's cluster axis makes us WORSE, not better** (4.07 -> 4.93/5.24). DRAM
reads are constant across every arm, confirming the metric isolates L2 reuse cleanly. Our best
arrangement still re-reads each fetched line **4.07 times against cuBLAS's 3.01, a 1.35x gap.**

#### WHAT THE EVIDENCE POINTS AT — `coopA` / `coopB`

Every cuBLAS kernel on our pinned shapes carries a `coopA` or `coopB` tag:

    nvjet_sm90_tst_128x128_64x6_1x2_h_bz_splitK_NTT     V1
    nvjet_sm90_tst_256x128_64x4_1x2_h_bz_coopA_NNT      V7 / V8 family
    nvjet_sm90_tst_128x256_64x4_2x1_v_bz_coopA_NTN      V2 family
    nvjet_sm90_tst_192x192_64x3_*_bz_coopB_*            V3 / V4 / V5 / V6

§H27-roadmap already records these as *"NOT multicast — tile-shape cooperative variants"* and
lists them as **undone structural work**. The mechanism fits the measured signature exactly:
if the CTAs of a cluster each fetch a FRACTION of the shared tile from L2 and exchange the
rest through distributed shared memory, then **L2 reads for the shared operand halve while
DRAM traffic and writes are untouched** — reads 1.24-1.62x, DRAM 1.00x, writes 1.000x.

**This is a hypothesis consistent with all the evidence, not yet a proven cause.** What would
confirm it: DSMEM traffic counters on cuBLAS's kernel (a coop implementation must show
cluster-local shared-memory traffic our kernel does not have), or implementing coopA on one
config and checking the L2 read ratio falls toward 3.

#### WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ANYTHING ELSE FOUND TODAY

§H27b4 measured the power excess at **1.11-1.13x at equal sub-cap clock**, and proved it is not
instructions (76% vector-op removal bought 2.1%). L2 traffic is the only major counter still
far from parity, and L2 access is energy-expensive. If the L2 read excess is the power excess,
then closing it addresses **~12% power -> cap saturation -> ~8 points of clock** — an order of
magnitude more than everything the instruction hunt yielded.

**NEXT CAMPAIGN: implement `coopA` on one config and measure the L2 read ratio.**

### §H27b6 — **OUR LOAD PATH HAS NO WASTE. Measured L2 reads are 1.015x what our tile geometry REQUIRES.** The excess is not inefficiency to remove — it is that our tile x cluster structure needs more L2 traffic than cuBLAS's. And the hard fact: **cuBLAS uses a size-2 cluster and achieves 241 MB where the best any size-2 geometry can do on this shape is 384 MB.**

#### THERE IS NOTHING REDUNDANT IN THE LOAD PATH

V1, `2048x512x16384 tn`, tile 128x128, cluster 2x1, split-K 2. A = 64 MB, B = 16 MB,
M-tiles 16, N-tiles 4. Each A row-panel is needed by every N-tile; each B col-panel by every
M-tile; our 2x1 cluster spans M so the two CTAs share N and **B** is multicast /2:

    required = A x 4  +  B x (16/2)  =  256 + 128 = 384 MB = 12,582,912 sectors
    MEASURED                                                 12,776,156 sectors
    ratio                                                         1.015

**Every L2 read we issue is required by the structure we chose.** §H27b5 framed this as an
excess to hunt; it is not. The load path is already minimal. DRAM reads match cuBLAS to 56
sectors in 2.6 M and L2 writes match to the sector (§H27b5), so loads, stores and DRAM are all
clean. The only variable left is the structure itself.

#### BIGGER CLUSTERS DO CUT L2 TRAFFIC, EXACTLY AS THE ARITHMETIC SAYS

Same shape, cluster shape varied, base configs (no sk2/dh/pdl/rot2 — the TFLOPS column is
therefore NOT comparable to the pin and is omitted):

    cluster   L2 read MB   geometric prediction
    1x2            421         384
    2x1 (pin)      333         384
    1x4            347         320
    4x1            333         320
    2x2            324         256
    4x2            278         192
    2x4            262         192
    cuBLAS (1x2)   241          --

Direction confirmed: widening the cluster shares each fetched line across more CTAs and the L2
read volume falls. 2x4 reaches 262 MB, within 9% of cuBLAS.

#### BUT THE OCCUPANCY WALL IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED

§H27-persistent-grid records that on H200 a **size-4 cluster strands 12 CTAs** and costs
**-36 points of %cuB** unless the grid is sized via `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters`. Size-8
(2x4, 4x2) is worse. So the L2 saving from wide clusters is paid for in occupancy, and that
trade has already been measured as a loss.

#### THE FACT THAT REMAINS, AND IT IS ARITHMETIC NOT SPECULATION

    cuBLAS cluster on V1                     1x2  (size 2)
    cuBLAS measured L2 reads                 241 MB
    BEST any size-2 geometry achieves here   384 MB   (2x1 or 1x2, either operand multicast /2)

**cuBLAS obtains L2 reuse that a size-2 multicast cannot produce, without paying the size-4
occupancy penalty.** Their loading scheme shares each fetched line more widely than two CTAs.
That is a measured contradiction with the simple geometric model, and it is the whole gap.

**WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED:** the mechanism. §H27b5 proposed `coopA`/`coopB` from the kernel
name alone — that is inference from a string, not evidence, and it is withdrawn as a claim.
Naming the mechanism requires reading their load instructions out of SASS: how many TMA/LDG
issues, of what transfer size, with what multicast mask. Until that is done the honest
statement is the arithmetic one above.

**NEXT: disassemble cuBLAS's V1 kernel and count its load instructions and their multicast
masks against ours.** That is the only way to name what produces 241 MB from a size-2 cluster.

---

### §H27b7 — **SASS: WE ISSUE EXACTLY THE SAME TMA LOADS AS cuBLAS — same count, same multicast split — YET PULL 1.62x THE L2 SECTORS.** The gap is not how many loads, nor whether we multicast. It is **sectors touched per TMA transaction**, which is tensor-map geometry.

Disassembled both V1 kernels (`ncu --page source --print-source sass`, deduped by address,
dynamic execution counts), shape `2048x512x16384 tn`, our pin
`128x128x64_2x1_v_sk2_dh_rot2_pdl_d6_shfl`:

    ours                                    cuBLAS
      32,768  UTMALDG.3D                      32,768  UTMALDG.3D
      32,768  UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST            32,768  UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST
         640  UTMACCTL.PF                      8,192  UTMASTG.4D
                                               8,192  UTMACMDFLUSH
                                               1,024  LDS
                                                 512  LDG.E

**The load side is identical: 65,536 TMA loads each, split 50/50 between multicast and
non-multicast.** Against L2 read sectors of 12,776,156 (ours) and 7,882,457 (cuBLAS), that is
**1.62x the sectors from the same number of transactions.**

#### WHAT THIS ELIMINATES

- **"We issue more loads."** No — identical counts.
- **"We do not multicast."** No — we issue exactly as many `.MULTICAST` loads as they do.
- **"Wrong cluster axis / wrong operand multicast."** Already refuted by measurement in §H27b6
  (their axis makes us worse: 4.07 -> 4.93 L2 reads per DRAM read), and now also by the SASS:
  both clusters are size 2 and both issue 32,768 multicast loads.
- **`coopA`/`coopB` as "cooperative loading splits the fetch across CTAs."** If that were the
  mechanism their load COUNT would differ from ours. It does not. §H27b5's naming was
  inference from a kernel-name string and is withdrawn; this is the SASS evidence that settles
  it.

#### WHAT IT LEAVES

Same instruction, same count, same multicast — **different bytes moved per instruction.** A
`UTMALDG.3D` transfers whatever its tensor map describes, so the remaining variables are the
**box dimensions and the swizzle mode** on the TMA descriptor, and how many 32 B L2 sectors a
single box touches.

**THE NEXT AND ONLY REMAINING QUESTION: what box geometry does cuBLAS's tensor map use versus
ours?** Ours is built in `make_tensor_map_*`; theirs is set up host-side before launch. Our
descriptor uses a 5D box (atom 64x8) for MN-major per §H27-native-MN-major. Comparing box
dims and swizzle between the two is a bounded, concrete task and it is the last unexplained
step in the chain:

    box geometry (unknown)  ->  1.62x L2 sectors per TMA  ->  +12% power at equal clock
                            ->  100% cap saturation vs 47.7%  ->  -108 MHz  ->  free-clock deficit

---

### §H27b9/ba — **OUR TMA MULTICAST IS NEARLY INEFFECTIVE: disabling it costs only 2.5% of L2 reads.** We issue exactly as many `.MULTICAST` loads as cuBLAS (32,768) and get almost no sharing from them. Flipping the cluster axis with everything else held constant makes it WORSE, so it is not the operand choice.

#### THE MULTICAST-OFF CONTROL

Same config, `MULTICAST_A`/`MULTICAST_B` the only change, V1 shape:

    arm                       L2 read sectors   MULTICAST loads   ourTF    %cuB
    pin (multicast on)             12,781,162            32,768   613.64   100.0%
    pin + _nomc (off)              13,104,924                 0   616.14    99.8%
                                   ----------
    saving attributable to multicast:  323,762 sectors = **2.5%**

If 32,768 multicast loads each served two CTAs, disabling them would force ~32,768 extra
independent fetches and add on the order of **6.4 M sectors**. It adds **0.32 M**. Our
multicast is delivering roughly **5% of what the instruction is for**, and performance is
unchanged either way (613.64 vs 616.14 TF) — we pay for the instruction and get nothing.

#### THE CLUSTER AXIS, ISOLATED PROPERLY THIS TIME — AND STILL REFUTED

§H27b6 compared cluster axes using STRIPPED base configs (no sk2/dh/rot2/pdl), which was not a
valid isolation. Rebuilt as a true twin of the pin with only `2x1 -> 1x2` changed:

    config                                      cluster   L2 read MB   ourTF    %cuB
    128x128x64_2x1_v_sk2_dh_rot2_pdl_d6_shfl      2x1         391      625.01   97.9%
    128x128x64_1x2_v_sk2_dh_rot2_pdl_d6_shfl      1x2         412      561.29   89.6%
    cuBLAS (1x2)                                  1x2         241        --       --

**1x2 gives us MORE L2 traffic and 8 points less performance.** The hypothesis that we
multicast the small operand (B, 20% of bytes) where cuBLAS multicasts the big one (A, 80%) is
arithmetically appealing and **empirically wrong** — switching axes does not transfer the
saving to A. Do not revisit the axis.

#### WHERE THIS LEAVES THE CHAIN

Everything is now measured except one link:

    ???  ->  1.62x L2 sectors per TMA  ->  +12% power at equal clock
         ->  cap saturation 100% vs 47.7%  ->  -108 MHz  ->  free-clock deficit

Eliminated by direct measurement, all of them:
- more load instructions (identical counts, §H27b7)
- missing multicast instructions (identical counts, §H27b7)
- cooperative loading / coopA (would change the count; it does not)
- wrong cluster axis (worse when isolated properly, above)
- wider clusters (works, but size-4 strands 12 CTAs on H200, -36 pts)
- load-path waste (we are at 1.015x the geometric minimum, §H27b6)

What remains is that **the same instruction, issued the same number of times, with the same
multicast annotation, moves 1.62x the L2 sectors** — and separately that **our multicast
annotation buys only 2.5% where it should buy ~50% of its half**. Those two facts are probably
the same fact. The variable neither of them can be explained without is the **TMA descriptor
itself**: box dimensions, swizzle mode, and the multicast CTA mask actually programmed.

**NEXT: dump our `CUtensorMap` fields (box dims, element strides, swizzle, interleave) and the
multicast mask we pass, and compare against what the transfer size implies cuBLAS uses.** That
is the last unexamined object in the path.

#### AND THE STANDING THAT MATTERS

At equal clock on V1 the pin now measures **97.9-104.4%** across runs. The deficit is a
free-clock phenomenon caused by the power draw, and the power draw is caused by the L2
traffic. Nothing in the compute path is behind cuBLAS.

### §H27bb — **THE COOPERATIVE SLICING IS IMPLEMENTED AND CORRECTLY PARAMETERISED, YET DELIVERS A TENTH OF WHAT IT SHOULD.** Design predicts disabling multicast costs ~25% of L2 reads; measurement says **2.5%**. That factor of ten is the located, unresolved contradiction and it is where the ~12% power / ~8 clock points live.

#### THE CODE DOES THE RIGHT THING

`issue_operand_3d_mn` implements the CUTLASS pattern — **every** cluster peer issues the
multicast (not one elected leader), each for **its own K-slice**, each with a ctaMask covering
all peers, and the TMA engine replicates the write and the barrier arrival into every peer's
smem at the same relative offset:

```c
const int slice_bytes = AW * slice_k * 2;
tma_3d_gmem2smem_multicast(dst + i*ATOM_BYTES + slice_idx*slice_bytes,
                           tmap, mn0 + AW*i, k0 + slice_idx*slice_k, batch, mbar, ctaMask);
```

and the slice widths are derived correctly:

```c
constexpr int A_MN_SLICE_K = BK / CLUSTER_N;   // A shares over N
constexpr int B_MN_SLICE_K = BK / CLUSTER_M;   // B shares over M
static constexpr bool NEEDS_A_MULTICAST = MULTICAST_A && (CLUSTER_N > 1);
static constexpr bool NEEDS_B_MULTICAST = MULTICAST_B && (CLUSTER_M > 1);
```

For V1's `2x1` pin: `NEEDS_A_MULTICAST=false` (A is not shared — the two CTAs hold different M
rows, correct), `NEEDS_B_MULTICAST=true`, `B_MN_SLICE_K = 64/2 = 32` — **each peer fetches half
of B and broadcasts it.** This is cooperative loading, already present, correctly configured.

#### BUT THE HARDWARE DOES NOT DELIVER IT

A and B tiles are the same size here (`BM x BK` = `BN x BK` = 128x64), so B is half the load
volume. With multicast off, each CTA fetches the FULL B tile, so B's L2 traffic doubles —
predicting **+25% total L2 reads**. Measured (§H27b9):

    multicast ON    12,781,162 sectors
    multicast OFF   13,104,924 sectors
    delta                2.5%      <- predicted ~25%

**A factor of ten between design intent and measured effect.** Performance is likewise
unchanged (613.64 vs 616.14 TF), which is consistent: if the slicing were working, disabling it
would cost real bandwidth and show up.

#### WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT PLACE TO STOP AND HAND OVER

Everything else in the chain is now measured and closed:

    load instruction counts        identical to cuBLAS (32,768 + 32,768)
    multicast instruction counts   identical to cuBLAS
    DRAM reads                     identical (56 sectors in 2.6 M)
    L2 writes                      identical to the sector
    load-path geometry             1.015x its own theoretical minimum
    tensor utilisation             91-99%, above cuBLAS on two shapes
    compute throughput             83.48% vs 83.46%
    duration at equal clock        59.14 us vs 59.39 us  (we are FASTER)
    cluster axis                   refuted twice, properly isolated the second time
    coopA/coopB                    refuted -- it would change the load count; it does not

The single remaining discrepancy is that **our multicast issues the right instruction, the
right number of times, with the right slice width, and returns a tenth of the expected
saving.** Candidates, none yet tested: the ctaMask value actually programmed at runtime; the
cluster peers not being co-resident so the replication has no peer to serve; the mbarrier
transaction-byte accounting forcing a full-tile fetch regardless of slice; or the descriptor's
box geometry making a half-K slice touch the same number of L2 sectors as the full tile.

**The first check is the cheapest: print the runtime `ctaMask` and confirm it names two CTAs,
and confirm `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters` reports the cluster is actually co-resident.**

---

### §H27bc — **CAVEAT ON THE L2 FINDING, AND THE HONEST LIMIT OF THIS INVESTIGATION.** The multicast implementation is verified correct in code, end to end. But `lts__t_sectors_op_read` may count sectors DELIVERED rather than FETCHED, in which case multicast can never reduce it and the 1.62x is partly an artifact. **I cannot currently distinguish "our multicast is broken" from "the counter cannot see it working."** What survives regardless is the **+12% power at equal clock**, measured directly.

#### THE MULTICAST CODE IS CORRECT — verified line by line

    launch          cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension, clusterDim.x = CLUSTER_SIZE = 2   OK
    rank decode     cluster_local_m = rank % CLUSTER_M ; cluster_local_n = rank / CLUSTER_M  OK
    V1 (2x1)        local_m in {0,1}, local_n = 0  -> the two CTAs share N, differ in M     OK
    who multicasts  NEEDS_B_MULTICAST = MULTICAST_B && (CLUSTER_M > 1) = true               OK
                    NEEDS_A_MULTICAST = MULTICAST_A && (CLUSTER_N > 1) = false  (A not shared) OK
    mask            b_mask = ((1<<CLUSTER_M)-1) << (local_n*CLUSTER_M) = 0b11 -> BOTH CTAs  OK
    slice width     B_MN_SLICE_K = BK / CLUSTER_M = 32  (half of K per peer)                OK
    slice index     b_slice = cluster_local_m -> 0 and 1, different halves                  OK
    pattern         every peer issues its own slice with a full mask (the CUTLASS pattern)  OK

Nothing in the implementation is wrong. One stale comment was found — line ~6835 says
`// 1D: CLUSTER_M==1 always (static_assert)` and **no such static_assert exists**; V1 runs
CLUSTER_M=2. The comment is wrong, the code is not.

#### THE CAVEAT I SHOULD HAVE RAISED BEFORE CHASING THIS

`lts__t_sectors_op_read` may count sectors **delivered to requestors**, not sectors **fetched
from the L2 array**. A multicast performs one fetch and replicates to N CTAs; if the counter
charges all N deliveries, **multicast cannot reduce this metric by construction**, and the
measured 2.5% is what a correctly-working multicast would look like.

Supporting arithmetic: **B is 16 MB and the H200 L2 is 60 MB, so B is L2-resident.** Its 8-16
re-reads are L2 HITS whether or not multicast dedupes them. Multicast would save request
bandwidth, not fetches — and hits are counted.

**Both readings fit every number collected.** Distinguishing them requires a counter that
measures L2 array activity rather than delivered sectors (`lts__t_sector_op_read_hit/miss`
breakdowns, or an L2-fabric-side metric), which was not captured.

#### WHAT SURVIVES THE CAVEAT, AND IT IS THE IMPORTANT PART

The power measurement is direct and physical, not a counter inference:

    lock 1000   cuBLAS 427 W   ours 472 W   1.11x   both under cap
    lock 1200   cuBLAS 540 W   ours 612 W   1.13x   both under cap
    lock 1400   cuBLAS 696 W   ours 698 W   1.00x   ours 100% capped / theirs 47.7%
                                                    clock 1301 vs 1409  (-108 MHz)

**We burn 11-13% more power than cuBLAS at the same clock, below the cap.** That is real,
settled, reproducible, and it is the whole free-clock deficit. Removing 76% of the k-loop
vector ops recovered 2.1% of it (§H27b4), so the instruction path is not it. **What consumes
the other ~10% is still unidentified**, and the L2 read counter was the lead that may or may
not be pointing at it.

#### THE STATE TO HAND OVER

Measured and closed: load counts, multicast counts, DRAM traffic, L2 writes, load-path
geometry (1.015x minimum), tensor utilisation, compute throughput, duration at equal clock
(we are FASTER: 59.14 vs 59.39 us), cluster axis (refuted twice), coopA/coopB (refuted),
multicast implementation (verified correct).

Open: **what burns the 11-13% power at equal clock.** The next instrument is not another
hypothesis — it is a counter that separates L2 array reads from delivered sectors, so the L2
lead can be confirmed or dropped cleanly.

### §H27bd — **CAVEAT RESOLVED: IT IS NOT A COUNTER ARTIFACT. We issue 1.64x the L2 read REQUESTS and perform 2.35x the L2 HITS for identical DRAM traffic.** Requests are transactions, not deliveries, so multicast accounting cannot produce this. The extra traffic is entirely L2 hits — invisible in bandwidth, expensive in power — and it is the +12%.

§H27bc flagged that `lts__t_sectors_op_read` might count delivered rather than fetched
sectors, which would make multicast unable to reduce it. The request and lookup counters
settle it:

    metric                    ours          cuBLAS        ratio
    lts__t_requests_op_read     3,228,232     1,968,138    1.64x   <- TRANSACTIONS
    lts__t_sectors_lookup_hit   9,684,275     4,124,923    2.35x   <- L2 ARRAY accesses
    lts__t_sectors_lookup_miss  4,851,385     4,195,929    1.16x
    lts__t_sectors_op_read     12,760,819     7,988,075    1.60x
    dram__sectors_read          2,622,424     2,622,160    1.00x

**A request is a transaction issued to L2, not a sector delivered from it.** Multicast
delivery accounting cannot inflate a request count. **We genuinely issue 1.64x the read
transactions and perform 2.35x the hitting tag lookups.** The §H27bc caveat is withdrawn.

The internal consistency is exact: **misses 1.16x, DRAM 1.00x, hits 2.35x.** Our excess
traffic never reaches DRAM — it is all served out of the L2 array. That is precisely why it
was invisible to every bandwidth-oriented measurement this week (DRAM bytes at parity,
§H27an) while costing real energy: **an L2 hit is a tag lookup plus an array read, and we do
2.35x as many of them.**

#### THIS IS THE +12% POWER

    2.35x L2 array accesses (all hits, none reaching DRAM)
      -> +11-13% power at equal clock, measured below the cap (§H27b4)
      -> 100% cap saturation vs cuBLAS's 47.7%
      -> -108 MHz
      -> the entire free-clock deficit

Every link is now measured. The chain is closed from cause to effect for the first time.

#### AND IT EXPLAINS THE WHOLE WEEK OF NULL RESULTS

- Instruction cuts moved nothing (§H27am +0.58 pts, §H27b4 2.1% of power) because the power
  was never in the instruction path.
- Every power comparison at free clocks read 1.00x (§H27ag, §H27am) because both libraries
  are clamped at the cap there.
- Every memory-traffic comparison read parity (§H27an, 1.00x DRAM) because the excess never
  reaches DRAM.
- Tensor utilisation, compute throughput and duration at equal clock all matched or favoured
  us, because the compute path was never the problem.

**The one thing nobody measured until now was L2 hit volume**, and that is where the entire
deficit lives.

#### THE QUESTION THAT REMAINS

Why do we issue 1.64x the L2 read transactions for the same data? Not multicast (verified
correct, §H27bc), not load count (identical, §H27b7), not tile geometry waste (1.015x
minimum, §H27b6), not cluster shape (refuted twice). The remaining candidates are how long a
fetched line stays useful before being re-requested — smem residency, pipeline depth, and the
order tiles are scheduled in — i.e. **reuse depth, not reuse ratio**.

---

### §H27be — **THE CULPRIT IS NAMED: 67% of our L2 read requests are A, the operand a 1-D cluster cannot multicast — and EVERY clustering route is now closed by measurement.** 2x2 cuts requests 14.6% and costs **36.8 points** to occupancy, reproducing the recorded "-36 pts" to within a point. cuBLAS's 1.97 M is **below what any size-2 clustering can reach**, so their reuse is not from multicast at all.

#### OUR REQUEST COUNT IS EXACTLY OUR STRUCTURE

Both libraries issue the same 128 B L2 requests (ours 3.95 sectors/request, cuBLAS 4.06) — the
granularity is identical, only the COUNT differs. Ours decomposes exactly:

    A row-fetches = M x (K/BK) = 2048 x 256 = 524,288, once per N-tile (4)        2,097,152
    B row-fetches = N x (K/BK) =  512 x 256 = 131,072, once per M-tile (16) / 2   1,048,576
                                                              predicted total  =  3,145,728
                                                              MEASURED         =  3,228,232  (+2.6%)

**A is 67% of the requests, and A is precisely the operand our 2x1 cluster does NOT multicast**
(2x1 spans M, so the peers share N and only B is shared).

#### EVERY CLUSTERING ROUTE, CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT

    cluster   A reads   B reads   predicted requests   measured requests   %cuB
    2x1 (pin)    4x        8x         3,145,728            3,225,657       97.5%
    1x2          2x       16x         3,145,728                 --         89.6%   (§H27ba)
    2x2          2x        8x         2,097,152            2,755,877       60.7%

- **1x2 merely trades one multicast for the other** — identical predicted total, and measured
  worse. That is why §H27ba's axis flip failed, and the arithmetic explains it exactly.
- **2x2 multicasts both and does cut requests (−14.6%)** — but performance collapses
  97.5% -> 60.7%, i.e. **-36.8 points**, against the previously recorded H200 figure of
  "size-4 strands 12 CTAs = -36 pts". Reproduced to within a point. The grid is 128 CTAs in
  both cases, so at size 4 that is 32 clusters and the strand cost is real.

**The fix works on the metric and is unusable on this hardware.**

#### AND THE ARITHMETIC RULES OUT CLUSTERING AS cuBLAS'S MECHANISM

    best achievable by ANY size-2 clustering on this shape   3,145,728 requests
    cuBLAS measured                                          1,968,138 requests

cuBLAS is **37% below what size-2 clustering can reach**, and they use a size-2 cluster. So
their reuse does not come from multicast. Combined with §H27b7 (identical load instruction
counts) and §H27bc (our multicast verified correct line by line), the entire multicast /
cluster family is exhausted.

#### WHAT IS LEFT — OPERAND RETENTION ACROSS TILES

The only remaining source of reuse is **not re-fetching between tiles**. If a persistent CTA
processes several M-tiles at the same N consecutively, it can hold the B tile in shared memory
across them and fetch it once instead of once per tile. **We reload both operands every tile.**

Fitting cuBLAS's number: A x2 + B x7 = 1,966,080 against their measured 1,968,138 — i.e. B
fetched ~7 times where the tile count says 16. That is consistent with B being retained across
roughly half the M-tiles a CTA visits.

This is a **scheduling and smem-residency property, not a cluster property**, which is exactly
why no cluster shape could reach it and why every cluster experiment this session failed. It
is the "reuse DEPTH not reuse RATIO" distinction §H27bd pointed at, now with an arithmetic fit.

**NEXT: does our persistent tile loop re-issue the B TMA for consecutive tiles that share N?
If yes, that is the 1.64x, and retaining it is the fix.**

---

> **RETRACTED IN FULL BY §H27bg, before any code was written.** The fix is physically
> impossible: B's K-extent on V1 is **4.00 MB** against **228 KB** of shared memory that is
> already 100% used. The pipeline holds 6 of 256 k-iterations, capping cross-tile B retention
> at **2.3%**, not the 1.64x claimed. And the `A x2 + B x7 = 1,966,080` that matched cuBLAS so
> neatly was a CURVE-FIT — the B multiplier was solved for to reproduce their measurement, then
> presented as a mechanism. The same error as the coopA naming in §H27b5. The MEASUREMENTS in
> this section stand; the explanation does not.

### §H27bf — ~~**THE CULPRIT, FOUND.**~~ *(RETRACTED — see banner)* Our rasterisation deliberately puts consecutive tiles on the same N so B is reusable — and the load path re-issues the B TMA every tile anyway.** The re-fetches are all L2 hits, which is why they were invisible to every DRAM and bandwidth measurement while costing 2.35x the L2 array accesses and +12% power.

#### THE RASTER ALREADY CREATES THE REUSE

From the template's own cluster/raster pairing rule:

```
// 1xN (A-multicast across N) -> h (RASTER=1, N-fastest, reuses A's M-tile);
// Mx1 / MxN (B-multicast across M) -> v (RASTER=0, M-fastest, reuses B's N-tile).
```

V1 pins `2x1` + raster `v`, which is the correct pairing: **M-fastest, so consecutive tiles
visited by a CTA share the same N and therefore the same B tile.**

#### AND THE LOAD PATH IGNORES IT

There is no retention anywhere — `same_n`, `same_m`, `prev_tile`, `last_n`, `skip_load` return
nothing in the whole template. The persistent loop

    for (int task_id = cluster_id; task_id < total_tiles; task_id += num_clusters)

re-enters the mainloop per tile and re-issues **both** operands' TMA loads from scratch. **The
schedule sets up B-reuse and the loader throws it away.**

#### IT FITS EVERY NUMBER COLLECTED THIS SESSION

    B re-requested once per M-tile (16x, halved to 8x by multicast) where consecutive
    tiles could share it
      -> L2 read requests 1.64x, and A x4 + B x8 = 3,145,728 vs measured 3,228,232 (+2.6%)
      -> the re-requests are all HITS: lookup_hit 2.35x, lookup_miss 1.16x
      -> nothing extra reaches DRAM: dram__sectors_read 1.00x
      -> invisible to every bandwidth measurement all week (§H27an read parity)
      -> 2.35x L2 array accesses -> +11-13% power at equal clock (§H27b4)
      -> 100% cap saturation vs 47.7% -> -108 MHz -> the free-clock deficit

And it fits cuBLAS: **A x2 + B x7 = 1,966,080 against their measured 1,968,138.** B fetched ~7
times where the tile count says 16 — consistent with retaining B across roughly half the tiles
a CTA visits. Note this ALSO explains why their 1.97 M is **below what any size-2 clustering
can reach** (3.15 M): they are not getting it from multicast, they are getting it from not
re-fetching.

#### WHY EVERY OTHER EXPLANATION FAILED, IN ONE LINE EACH

    load instruction count      identical (§H27b7) -- it is not how many TMAs we issue
    multicast implementation    verified correct line by line (§H27bc)
    cluster axis 1x2            trades A's multicast for B's, same 3.15 M (§H27ba, §H27be)
    cluster 2x2                 cuts requests 14.6% but -36.8 pts to occupancy (§H27be)
    coopA / coopB               would change the load count; it does not (§H27b7)
    tile geometry               we are at 1.015x our own minimum (§H27b6)
    instruction / vector path   +0.58 pts, 2.1% of power (§H27am, §H27b4)

Every one of these is a property of a SINGLE tile. The waste is **between** tiles, which is
why nothing that looked inside one tile could see it.

#### THE FIX

Retain the B tile in shared memory across consecutive tiles that share N, and skip its TMA
issue. Requires the producer to compare the incoming tile's N against the previous tile's and
suppress the B load plus its share of the barrier transaction bytes. Real work — the pipeline
is currently per-tile with no cross-tile state — but well defined, and it is the last
unexplained term in the chain.

**Predicted effect:** B x8 -> B x~2-4 on V1 gives roughly 2.3-2.6 M requests against cuBLAS's
1.97 M, closing most of the 1.64x and therefore most of the 12% power and the 108 MHz.

### §H27bg — **§H27bf RETRACTED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION. Cross-tile B retention is physically impossible (4.00 MB of B against 228 KB of smem, already fully used), and my model of cuBLAS's kernel over-predicts their request count by 1.6x — so it does not describe their kernel and must not be built on.**

#### THE ARITHMETIC THAT KILLED THE FIX

    B across ALL K   BN x K x 2 = 128 x 16384 x 2 =   4.00 MB   <- what retention needs
    one pipeline stage BN x BK x 2               =  16.0 KB
    whole B pipeline (depth 6)                   =  96.0 KB
    H200 smem per CTA                            = 228.0 KB     (already 100% used, §H27zY)

    the pipeline can hold 6 of 256 k-iterations  = 2.3%
    -> ceiling on cross-tile B retention: **2.3%**, against the 1.64x it was proposed to fix

**B cannot be retained across tiles.** Its K-extent exceeds shared memory by 18x. §H27bf's
"the schedule creates the reuse and the loader throws it away" is wrong: the loader cannot
keep it. The rasterisation comment it quoted (`Mx1 -> v, reuses B's N-tile`) refers to **L2**
reuse across tiles, which is exactly what we already get — those re-fetches ARE the hits.

#### AND THE cuBLAS MODEL DOES NOT FIT

    model of their 128x128 / 1x2 / splitK kernel:
        A multicast over 2 N-peers   524,288 x 4 / 2 = 1,048,576
        B not multicast              131,072 x 16    = 2,097,152
        total                                          3,145,728
    cuBLAS MEASURED                                    1,968,138   -> model over-predicts 1.6x

The `A x2 + B x7 = 1,966,080` quoted in §H27bf as "fitting cuBLAS exactly" was obtained by
**solving for the B multiplier that reproduces their number**, then presented as a discovered
mechanism. It is a curve-fit with one free parameter through one data point. Same failure mode
as naming `coopA` off a kernel-name string (§H27b5).

#### WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS NOT NOTHING

Directly measured, no model in between:

    +11-13% power at equal clock BELOW the cap        (§H27b4, three lock points)
    100% cap saturation vs cuBLAS's 47.7%, -108 MHz   (§H27b4)
    L2 read REQUESTS 1.64x, lookup HITS 2.35x         (§H27bd)
    L2 misses 1.16x, DRAM reads 1.00x                 (§H27bd) -- the excess never reaches DRAM
    our request count matches OUR structure           3,145,728 predicted vs 3,228,232 measured
    everything else at parity; at equal clock we are FASTER (59.14 vs 59.39 us)

#### THE OPEN QUESTION, STATED CORRECTLY

**Why does cuBLAS need 1.6x fewer L2 read requests than any model of a 128x128 / BK=64 /
depth-6 / 1x2-cluster / split-K GEMM predicts?** Our own structure is fully explained by such
a model to 2.6%. Theirs is not explained by it at all. Something about their kernel's data
movement is outside this model, and until it is identified from measurement — not from kernel
names, not from curve-fits — no fix should be attempted.

**METHOD NOTE, third instance today.** §H27ak retracted a conclusion from a power reading taken
in the wrong condition; §H27as retracted one built on a counter that does not track throughput;
this retracts one built on a curve-fit. All three were caught before shipping, and this one
before a line of code. The recurring failure is **explaining a measurement with a mechanism
that was not independently observed.** The measurement is not the explanation.

### §H27bh — **SASS FLOW COMPARISON: the load paths are structurally EQUIVALENT, which rules out the load path as the source of the 1.6x L2 requests.** Same instruction mix, same descriptor usage, same multicast pattern per stage. What differs is packaging — we carry **12 TMA instructions that never execute** and peel the producer **7-way against their 2-way**.

Full instruction-order comparison of both V1 kernels, `ncu --page source --print-source sass`,
deduped by address, dynamic counts attached.

#### PER-STAGE LOAD PATTERN — IDENTICAL

    cuBLAS                                        OURS
      UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST [UR8],[UR34],UR33        UTMALDG.3D           [UR8],[UR16]
      UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST [UR8],[UR34],UR33        UTMALDG.3D           [UR8],[UR16]
      UTMALDG.3D           [UR16],[UR34]            UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST [UR8],[UR16],UR19
      UTMALDG.3D           [UR16],[UR34]            UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST [UR8],[UR16],UR19

Two multicast plus two plain per stage, one shared descriptor register, same 3-D form, same
65,536 dynamic total. **There is no difference in how a tile is fetched.**

#### WHAT DOES DIFFER — PACKAGING, NOT MECHANISM

    metric                    cuBLAS                          ours
    static UTMALDG                 8                            28
    execution profile      4 x 13,696 + 4 x 2,688      4 x 4,096 x 4 copies + 12 NEVER EXECUTED
    producer peel               2-way                        7-way
    TMA address span           2.3 KB                        7.0 KB
    leader election    uniform predicate (@UP3)      ELECT before every TMA (28 static)
    total static instr           1,200                        1,384

**Twelve of our TMA instructions have dynamic count ZERO on this shape** — pipeline peel copies
that never run. Together with the 7-way peel and the per-TMA `ELECT` (cuBLAS uses uniform
predication and never elects), that is genuine dead code and code-size waste worth removing on
its own merits. It is I-cache pressure, not L2 traffic.

#### THE NEGATIVE RESULT, WHICH IS THE POINT

**The 1.6x L2 read requests do NOT come from the load path.** Same instructions, same counts,
same descriptors, same multicast annotation, same per-stage order. Everything about how we
fetch a tile matches cuBLAS. Combined with the earlier eliminations this leaves very little:

    load instruction count / mix / order     identical            (this section, §H27b7)
    multicast implementation                 verified correct     (§H27bc)
    cluster shape                            all refuted          (§H27ba, §H27be)
    tile geometry                            1.015x minimum       (§H27b6)
    cross-tile retention                     physically impossible (§H27bg)
    writes / DRAM                            identical            (§H27b5)
    instruction & vector path                worth 2.1% of power  (§H27b4)

Unexamined sources that could still reach L2: **L1/TEX misses** — we issue 32,768 L1/TEX
requests at 74.72% hit rate where cuBLAS issues **ZERO** — and **instruction fetch**, given our
code is larger (1,384 vs 1,200) and far more scattered (7 KB vs 2.3 KB of TMA span).

Neither is obviously large enough to account for ~1.26 M extra requests, and **neither will be
claimed as the cause without measuring it.** Three explanations have already been retracted
today for exactly that error (§H27ak, §H27as, §H27bg).

### §H27bi — **LOCALISED, AND MEASURED THIS TIME: each of our TMA transactions decomposes into 41.3 L2 requests where cuBLAS's decomposes into 24.1.** Same instruction, same count (65,536 each), same 128 B request size — **1.71x the bytes moved per transaction.** This is tensor-map box geometry, and it is now a measurement rather than an inference.

L2 read requests attributed by source unit, V1, both kernels:

    metric                              ours          cuBLAS       ratio
    lts__t_requests_op_read          3,234,371       1,976,473     1.64x
    lts__t_requests_srcunit_tex_op_read 2,708,097 (83.7%)  1,581,383 (80.0%)   **1.71x**
    not from TEX                       526,274         395,090     1.33x
    l1tex__t_requests                   32,768               0        --
    UTMALDG dynamic                     65,536          65,536     **1.00x**

**83.7% of our L2 read requests arrive from the TEX unit — the TMA path — and so do 80% of
cuBLAS's.** The bulk of the traffic on both sides is the tile fetch, and we issue 1.71x as
many requests for it from an identical number of instructions:

    requests per TMA   ours 2,708,097 / 65,536 = 41.3
                     cuBLAS 1,581,383 / 65,536 = 24.1        ratio 1.71x

Request size is the same on both sides (3.95 vs 4.06 sectors, i.e. 128 B), so this is bytes:

    bytes moved per TMA   ours   41.3 x 128 = 5,286 B
                        cuBLAS   24.1 x 128 = 3,085 B

**Our TMA transactions move 1.71x more bytes than cuBLAS's.** Both kernels compute the same
GEMM and move identical DRAM traffic (1.00x, §H27b5), so the surplus is redundant — either
each box covers more than it needs, or consecutive boxes overlap.

#### WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM THE THREE RETRACTED CLAIMS

This is not inferred from a kernel name (§H27b5), not fitted to reproduce a number (§H27bg),
and not read off a counter that fails to track the outcome (§H27as). **Requests-per-instruction
is a direct ratio of two measured counters over an identical instruction count.** The
descriptor is the only object that can set it: given a fixed instruction and a fixed request
size, the number of requests one TMA decomposes into is a function of the box dimensions, the
element strides and the swizzle — nothing else.

#### THE MEASUREMENT THAT COMES NEXT

Dump our actual `CUtensorMap` fields for A and B — `boxDim[]`, `globalDim[]`, `globalStrides[]`,
`elementStrides[]`, `swizzle`, `interleave` — from `make_tensor_map_*`, and compute the bytes
one box covers. Compare against the 3,085 B/TMA that cuBLAS's measurement implies. If our box
covers ~5,286 B where the tile needs ~3,085 B, the surplus is visible directly in the
descriptor and the fix is a descriptor change, not a restructuring.

This is bounded: the fields are in our own code and the target number is already measured.

Clock, power and temperature all match to within 2 MHz / 0 W / 1 C. **The GEMM-level deficit does not survive to the application.**

`kind-data-thinks-fin-03`, GPU 0, CUDA 13.0, 1.7B production config (36 layers, 16 heads,
GQA-4, ffn 5632, context 4096, vocab 50304), production `global_batch` 2,097,152 (grad_accum
128), 15 steps per run, steady-state = mean of the last 12. Real `flux_*` shards.

    run                  tok/s     %cuB     clock      power (mean/peak)   temp
    BluBLAS  free       27,995   100.01%   1812 MHz    665 W / 818 W       64 C
    cuBLAS   free       27,992      --     1810 MHz    665 W / 820 W       65 C
    BluBLAS  locked     24,775    99.94%   1410 MHz    511 W / 628 W       59 C
    cuBLAS   locked     24,790      --     1410 MHz    511 W / 624 W       59 C

**+3 tok/s free, -15 tok/s locked. Both inside 0.06%.** Per-step spread within a run was
~0.16%, so these are separated by less than the noise.

#### THE GEMM DEFICIT DOES NOT REACH THE APPLICATION

The isolated GEMM measures, on V1's shape at equal sub-cap clock, **+11-13% power** (§H27b4)
driving **100% cap saturation vs cuBLAS's 47.7%** and a **-108 MHz** clock loss. At trainer
level none of it is visible:

    clock   1812 vs 1810 MHz    2 MHz apart
    power    665 vs  665 W      identical
    temp      64 vs   65 C      1 C apart

This is the dilution the arithmetic predicted and it is now measured, not argued: **our GEMM is
~38% of the trainer run** (§H27zW), so a 12% excess on that slice is ~4.5% of the whole, and the
remaining 62% is byte-identical work on both arms. Neither arm ends up cap-limited the way a
back-to-back GEMM loop does — at free clocks both sit at 665 W against a 700 W cap, i.e. **under
it**, which is exactly the condition where the GEMM's cap saturation cannot occur.

#### WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SAY

**Does:** on the workload that matters, with the current dispatch, BluBLAS and cuBLAS are
indistinguishable. The free-clock GEMM gap that consumed this session is an artifact of
measuring a GEMM in isolation at 100% duty cycle, a condition the trainer never creates.

**Does not:** this is the BASELINE BLAS. The dispatch table routes every shape to
pre-optimization configs; today's `_shfl` and `_dh_dw_uad_ubd_cs` rungs are compiled in but
**nothing selects them** (0 dispatch entries reference them). Today's +1.08% on seven pins and
the V2c work are absent from these numbers.

**Historical trainer figures (93.8% -> 96.4% -> 98.4%) are NOT comparable** — the trainer script
itself changed since they were taken (the wV round-trip removal and the SwiGLU work), so only
this same-day, same-script, same-box pair is a valid comparison.

#### ALSO FOUND — `pins.sh` DISAGREES WITH THE DISPATCH TABLE ON 2 OF 15 SHAPES

    var   pins.sh (what was benchmarked all day)        dispatch table (what production runs)
    V2c   256x128x64_2x1_h_ep32s2_pdl                   256x128x64_1x2_v_ep32s2      <-- DIFFERS
    V6    192x192x64_2x1_h_rs8_dh_ubd_dw_skew_lsw_pdl_wlsm  128x256x64_2x1_h_ep64swz128_pdl  <-- DIFFERS

The other 13 agree. **This puts today's headline V2c result in question**: its baseline was
measured at 89.1-92.4% using the `pins.sh` config, but production dispatches
`256x128x64_1x2_v_ep32s2`, whose dispatch-table annotation reads **812.9 TF** against the
~654-687 TF measured for the `pins.sh` baseline. If that holds, the "+7.2 points on V2c" improved
a config production does not use. Verification is queued (§H27bl); the claim should not be
repeated until it lands.

---

### §H27bl — **THE V2c CLAIM IS CORRECTED DOWNWARD: +1.4 / +2.2 points, not +7.2.** `pins.sh` and the dispatch table name different configs for this shape, and everything measured today used the `pins.sh` one — which production does not run and which is **4 points worse** than what it does run.

`2048x50304x16384 tn`, four configs, both clock policies, all PASS `maxRelErr 0.00000`:

    config                                          free %cuB   locked %cuB
    256x128x64_1x2_v_ep32s2        <- DISPATCHED       94.6%       94.1%
    256x128x64_2x1_h_ep32s2_pdl    <- pins.sh          90.5%       88.8%
    256x128x64_2x1_h_..._dh_dw_uad_ubd_cs               90.2%       89.6%
    128x256x64_2x1_v_ep32s2_dh_shfl <- our best         96.0%       96.3%

#### WHAT WAS WRONG

§H27b2 reported V2c going **89.7% -> 96.9%, +7.2 points**. That baseline was
`256x128x64_2x1_h_ep32s2_pdl`, taken from `pins.sh`. **Production dispatches
`256x128x64_1x2_v_ep32s2` instead**, and it is 4 points better than the pins.sh config
(94.6 vs 90.5 free). Against the config that actually runs, our best arm gains
**+1.4 points free and +2.2 locked** — real, and a third of what was claimed.

#### AND THE 256x128 LADDER IS THE WRONG TILE FOR THIS SHAPE ENTIRELY

`_dh_dw_uad_ubd_cs`, the rung that measured **+1.95 paired and null-controlled** in §H27au,
sits at **90.2% / 89.6%** — below the dispatched `1x2_v` at 94.6% / 94.1%. The +1.95 was a
real improvement to `256x128_2x1_h`, and `256x128_2x1_h` is simply not the right tile here.
**A gated, null-controlled, believable improvement to the wrong configuration is still worth
nothing**, which is the lesson.

The dispatch-table annotation on that row reads **812.9 TF**; measured today the same config
gives 678 TF free / 702 TF locked. That comment is stale and should not be trusted as a
baseline.

#### THE RULE THIS ESTABLISHES

**`pins.sh` is not the dispatch table.** They agree on 13 of 15 shapes and disagree on V2c and
V6. Any standalone result intended to justify a production change must be measured against
`Bgemm_sm90_dispatch_table.h`, not against `pins.sh`. Today's other results are unaffected —
the 128x256 family (7 pins) and V1 were verified to agree between the two — but V6's numbers
carry the same defect as V2c's and have not been re-measured.

#### WHAT IS STILL WORTH DOING ON V2c

`128x256x64_2x1_v_ep32s2_dh_shfl` beats the dispatched config by 1.4-2.2 points and is
bit-exact. Retargeting that one row is justified. It was deliberately left out of §H27bm's
retarget pending exactly this verification.
